questions.q: Let the three sides of a triangle are on the lines \(4x-7y+10=0\), \(x+y=5\) and \(7x+4y=15\). Then the distance of its orthocentre from the orthocentre of the triangle formed by the lines \(x=0\), \(y=0\) and \(x+y=1\) is
questions.sol: \(4x-7y+10=0\) and \(7x+4y=15\) are perpendicular, so the orthocentre is their intersection \((1,2)\). The second triangle is right-angled at \((0,0)\). Distance \(\sqrt{1+4}\).

questions.q: Let the area of a \(\Delta PQR\) with vertices \(P(5,4)\), \(Q(-2,4)\) and \(R(a,b)\) be \(35\) square units. If its orthocenter and centroid are \(O\left(2,\dfrac{14}5\right)\) and \(C(c,d)\) respectively, then \(c+2d\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(PQ\) is horizontal, so the altitude from \(R\) is \(x=a=2\). Area: \(\tfrac12\cdot7|b-4|=35\). The altitude from \(P\) (\(\perp QR\)) through \(O\) gives \(-12-\tfrac65(b-4)=0\), so \(b=-6\). Centroid \(\left(\tfrac53,\tfrac23\right)\).

questions.q: Let the points \(\left(\dfrac{11}2,\alpha\right)\) lie on or inside the triangle with sides \(x+y=11\), \(x+2y=16\) and \(2x+3y=29\). Then the product of the smallest and the largest values of \(\alpha\) is equal to :

Let \({}^nC_{r-1}=28\), \({}^nC_r=56\) and \({}^nC_{r+1}=70\). Let \(A(4\cos t,4\sin t)\), \(B(2\sin t,-2\cos t)\) and \(C(3r-n,r^2-n-1)\) be the vertices of a triangle \(ABC\), where \(t\) is a parameter. If \((3x-1)^2+(3y)^2=\alpha\), is the locus of the centroid of triangle \(ABC\), then \(\alpha\) equals
questions.sol: The ratios give \(n=8\), \(r=3\), so \(C=(1,0)\). Then \(3x-1=4\cos t+2\sin t\) and \(3y=4\sin t-2\cos t\); squaring and adding gives \(16+4\).

questions.q: Let a variable line of slope \(m>0\) passing through the point \((4,-9)\) intersect the coordinate axes at the points \(A\) and \(B\). The minimum value of the sum of the distances of \(A\) and \(B\) from the origin is
questions.sol: The intercepts are \(4+\tfrac9m\) and \(-(9+4m)\); the sum of distances is \(13+\tfrac9m+4m\ge13+12\).

questions.q: If the locus of the point, whose distances from the point \((2,1)\) and \((1,3)\) are in the ratio \(5:4\), is \(ax^2+by^2+cxy+dx+ey+170=0\), then the value of \(a^2+2b+3c+4d+e\) is equal to :
If the line segment joining the points \((5,2)\) and \((2,a)\) subtends an angle \(\dfrac\pi4\) at the origin, then the absolute value of the product of all possible values of \(a\) is :
questions.sol: \(\tan\dfrac\pi4=\dfrac{|5a-4|}{10+2a}\), giving \(a=\tfrac{14}3\) or \(a=-\tfrac67\).

questions.q: A ray of light coming from the point \(P(1,2)\) gets reflected from the point \(Q\) on the \(x\)-axis and then passes through the point \(R(4,3)\). If the point \(S(h,k)\) is such that \(PQRS\) is a parallelogram, then \(hk^2\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(Q\) lies on the line joining \(P\) to \(R'(4,-3)\): \(Q=\left(\tfrac{11}5,0\right)\). \(S=P+R-Q=\left(\tfrac{14}5,5\right)\).

questions.q: Two vertices of a triangle \(ABC\) are \(A(3,-1)\) and \(B(-2,3)\), and its orthocentre is \(P(1,1)\). If the coordinates of the point \(C\) are \((\alpha,\beta)\) and the centre of the circle circumscribing the triangle \(PAB\) is \((h,k)\), then the value of \((\alpha+\beta)+2(h+k)\) equals
questions.sol: \(AP\perp BC\): \(\beta-\alpha=5\); \(BP\perp AC\): \(3\alpha-2\beta=11\). So \(C=(21,26)\). The circumcentre of \(PAB\) (from the perpendicular bisectors \(x-y=2\) and \(-3x+2y=\tfrac{11}2\)) is \(\left(-\tfrac{19}2,-\tfrac{23}2\right)\). Value \(47-42\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in Z\) and let \(A(\alpha,\beta)\), \(B(1,0)\), \(C(\gamma,\delta)\) and \(D(1,2)\) be the vertices of a parallelogram \(ABCD\). If \(AB=\sqrt{10}\) and the points \(A\) and \(C\) lie on the line \(3y=2x+1\), then \(2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)\) is equal to
questions.sol: The centre is \((1,1)\), so \(\alpha+\gamma=2\), \(\beta+\delta=2\). (Checking: \(A=(-2,-1)\) satisfies \(AB=\sqrt{10}\) and lies on the line.)

questions.q: Let \(G(\alpha,\beta)\) be the circumcentre of the triangle formed by the lines : \(4x+3y=69\), \(4y-3x=17\) and \(x+7y=61\). Then \((\alpha-\beta)^2+\alpha+\beta\) is equal to
questions.sol: The first two lines are perpendicular, so \(G\) is the midpoint of the other two vertices \((12,7)\) and \((5,8)\): \(G=\left(\tfrac{17}2,\tfrac{15}2\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(R\) be the rectangle given by the lines \(x=0\), \(x=2\), \(y=0\) and \(y=5\). Let \(A(\alpha,0)\) and \(B(0,\beta)\), \(\alpha\in[0,2]\) and \(\beta\in[0,5]\), be such that the line segment \(AB\) divides the area of the rectangle \(R\) in the ratio \(4:1\). Then, the mid-point of \(AB\) lies on a
questions.sol: The triangle cut off has area \(\tfrac{\alpha\beta}2=2\), so the midpoint \((x,y)\) satisfies \(xy=1\).

questions.q: If the point \(\left(\alpha,\dfrac{7\sqrt3}3\right)\) lies on the curve traced by the mid-points of the line segments of the lines \(x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta=7\), \(\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) between the coordinates axes, then \(\alpha\) is equal to
questions.sol: The midpoint is \(\left(\tfrac7{2\cos\theta},\tfrac7{2\sin\theta}\right)\), so the locus is \(\tfrac{49}{4x^2}+\tfrac{49}{4y^2}=1\) with \(x,y>0\). With \(y=\tfrac{7\sqrt3}3\) the second term is \(\tfrac34\), so \(x=7\).

questions.q: Let the area of the triangle with vertices \(A(1,\alpha)\), \(B(\alpha,0)\) and \(C(0,\alpha)\) be \(4\) sq. units. If the points \((\alpha,-\alpha)\), \((-\alpha,\alpha)\) and \((\alpha^2,\beta)\) are collinear, then \(\beta\) is equal to
questions.sol: The area is \(\tfrac{|\alpha|}2=4\). The first two points lie on \(y=-x\), so \(\beta=-\alpha^2=-64\).

questions.q: Let two points be \(A(1,-1)\) and \(B(0,2)\). If a point \(P(x',y')\) be such that the area of \(\Delta PAB=5\) sq. units and it lies on the line, \(3x+y-4\lambda=0\), then a value of \(\lambda\) is
Let \(O(0,0)\) and \(A(0,1)\) be two fixed points. Then the locus of a point \(P\) such that the perimeter of \(\Delta AOP\) is \(4\), is
questions.sol: \(OP+AP=3\): an ellipse with foci \(O,A\), centre \(\left(0,\tfrac12\right)\), \(a=\tfrac32\) (vertical), \(b^2=2\), i.e. \(9x^2+8y^2-8y=16\). (The book key prints (d).)

questions.q: The region represented by \(|x-y|\le2\) and \(|x+y|\le2\) is bounded by a
questions.sol: The vertices are \((\pm2,0)\) and \((0,\pm2)\): a square of side \(2\sqrt2\).

questions.q: A triangle has a vertex at \((1,2)\) and the mid points of the two sides through it are \((-1,1)\) and \((2,3)\). Then the centroid of this triangle is
questions.sol: The other vertices are \((-3,0)\) and \((3,4)\).

questions.q: A point \(P\) moves on the line \(2x-3y+4=0\). If \(Q(1,4)\) and \(R(3,-2)\) are fixed points, then the locus of the centroid of \(\Delta PQR\) is a line
If \(5\), \(5r\), \(5r^2\) are the lengths of the sides of a triangle, then \(r\) cannot be equal to
questions.sol: Triangle inequalities give \(\tfrac{\sqrt5-1}2<r<\tfrac{\sqrt5+1}2\approx1.618\).

questions.q: Two sides of a parallelogram are along the lines, \(x+y=3\) and \(x-y+3=0\). If its diagonals intersect at \((2,4)\), then one of its vertex is
questions.sol: The given sides meet at \((0,3)\); the opposite vertex is \((4,5)\), and the other sides are \(x+y=9\) and \(x-y+1=0\). The vertices are \((0,3),(1,2),(4,5),(3,6)\).

questions.q: In a triangle \(ABC\), coordinates of \(A\) are \((1,2)\) and the equations of the medians through \(B\) and \(C\) are respectively, \(x+y=5\) and \(x=4\). Then area of \(\Delta ABC\) (in sq. units) is

A square, of each side \(2\), lies above the \(x\)-axis and has one vertex at the origin. If one of the sides passing through the origin makes an angle \(30^\circ\) with the positive direction of the \(x\)-axis, then the sum of the \(x\)-coordinates of the vertices of the square is
The \(x\)-coordinate of the incentre of the triangle that has the coordinates of mid points of its sides as \((0,1)\), \((1,1)\) and \((1,0)\) is
questions.sol: The vertices are \((0,0),(2,0),(0,2)\), a right triangle with \(r=\tfrac{2+2-2\sqrt2}2\); the incentre is \((r,r)\).

questions.q: If the line \(2x+y=k\) passes through the point which divides the line segment joining the points \((1,1)\) and \((2,4)\) in the ratio \(3:2\), then \(k\) equals
questions.sol: The point is \(\left(\tfrac85,\tfrac{14}5\right)\).

questions.q: Three distinct points \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are given in the \(2\)-dimensional coordinate plane such that the ratio of the distance of any one of them from the point \((1,0)\) to the distance from the point \((-1,0)\) is equal to \(1/3\). Then the circumcentre of the triangle \(ABC\) is at the point
questions.sol: All three lie on \(9[(x-1)^2+y^2]=(x+1)^2+y^2\), i.e. \(x^2+y^2-\tfrac52x+1=0\), whose centre is the circumcentre.

questions.q: Let \(A(h,k)\), \(B(1,1)\) and \(C(2,1)\) be the vertices of a right angled triangle with \(AC\) as its hypotenuse. If the area of the triangle is \(1\) square unit, then the set of values which '\(k\)' can take is given by
questions.sol: The right angle is at \(B\) and \(BC\) is horizontal, so \(h=1\); area \(\tfrac12|k-1|\cdot1=1\).

questions.q: If a vertex of a triangle is \((1,1)\) and the mid points of two sides through this vertex are \((-1,2)\) and \((3,2)\), then the centroid of the triangle is
questions.sol: The other vertices are \((-3,3)\) and \((5,3)\).

questions.q: Let \(A(2,-3)\) and \(B(-2,1)\) be vertices of a triangle \(ABC\). If the centroid of this triangle moves on the line \(2x+3y=1\), then the locus of the vertex \(C\) is the line
questions.sol: For \(C(h,k)\) the centroid is \(\left(\tfrac h3,\tfrac{k-2}3\right)\), so \(\tfrac{2h}3+(k-2)=1\).

questions.q: If the equation of the locus of point equidistant from the points \((a_1,b_1)\) and \((a_2,b_2)\) is \((a_1-a_2)x+(b_1-b_2)y+c=0\), then \(c=\)
questions.sol: Expanding \((x-a_1)^2+(y-b_1)^2=(x-a_2)^2+(y-b_2)^2\) and dividing by \(-2\).

questions.q: Locus of centroid of the triangle whose vertices are \((a\cos t,a\sin t)\), \((b\sin t,-b\cos t)\) and \((1,0)\), where \(t\) is a parameter, is
questions.sol: \(3x-1=a\cos t+b\sin t\) and \(3y=a\sin t-b\cos t\); square and add.

questions.q: Let \(A(4,-2)\), \(B(1,1)\) and \(C(9,-3)\) be the vertices of a triangle \(ABC\). Then the maximum area of the parallelogram \(AFDE\), formed with vertices \(D\), \(E\) and \(F\) on the sides \(BC\), \(CA\) and \(AB\) of the triangle \(ABC\) respectively, is ______.
questions.sol: The area of \(ABC\) is \(6\). With \(AF=t\cdot AB\), the parallelogram has area \(2t(1-t)\cdot6\), at most \(\tfrac12\cdot6\).

questions.q: Let \(A(6,8)\), \(B(10\cos\alpha,-10\sin\alpha)\) and \(C(-10\sin\alpha,10\cos\alpha)\), be the vertices of a triangle. If \(L(a,9)\) and \(G(h,k)\) be its orthocenter and centroid respectively, then \((5a-3h+6k+100\sin2\alpha)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: All vertices are at distance \(10\) from \(O\), so \(O\) is the circumcentre and \(L=A+B+C\). Then \(8+10(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha)=9\) gives \(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha=\tfrac1{10}\), so \(a=7\) and \(\sin2\alpha=\tfrac{99}{100}\). \(G=\left(\tfrac73,3\right)\). Value \(35-7+18+99\).

questions.q: Let \(A(-2,-1)\), \(B(1,0)\), \(C(\alpha,\beta)\) and \(D(\gamma,\delta)\) be the vertices of a parallelogram \(ABCD\). If the point \(C\) lies on \(2x-y=5\) and the point \(D\) lies on \(3x-2y=6\), then the value of \(|\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta|\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(A+C=B+D\) gives \(\gamma=\alpha-3\), \(\delta=\beta-1\). With \(\beta=2\alpha-5\) and \(3\gamma-2\delta=6\): \(\alpha=-3\), \(\beta=-11\), \(\gamma=-6\), \(\delta=-12\).

questions.q: Let \(A(1,0)\), \(B(6,2)\) and \(C\left(\dfrac32,6\right)\) be the vertices of a triangle \(ABC\). If \(P\) is a point inside the triangle \(ABC\) such that the triangles \(APC\), \(APB\) and \(BPC\) have equal areas, then the length of the line segment \(PQ\), where \(Q\) is the point \(\left(-\dfrac76,-\dfrac13\right)\), is ______.
questions.sol: \(P\) is the centroid \(\left(\tfrac{17}6,\tfrac83\right)\); \(PQ=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}\).

questions.q: Let the area of the triangle formed by a straight line \(L:x+by+c=0\) with co-ordinate axes be \(48\) square units. If the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the line \(L\) makes an angle of \(45^\circ\) with the positive \(x\)-axis, then the value of \(b^2+c^2\) is :
questions.sol: The normal \((1,b)\) is at \(45^\circ\), so \(b=1\). Area \(\tfrac{c^2}2=48\).

questions.q: A line passes through the origin and makes equal angles with the positive coordinate axes. It intersects the lines \(L_1:2x+y+6=0\) and \(L_2:4x+2y-p=0\), \(p>0\), at the points \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. If \(AB=\dfrac9{\sqrt2}\) and the foot of the perpendicular from the point \(A\) on the line \(L_2\) is \(M\), then \(\dfrac{AM}{BM}\) is equal to
questions.sol: On \(y=x\): \(A(-2,-2)\), \(B\left(\tfrac p6,\tfrac p6\right)\); \(AB=\tfrac9{\sqrt2}\) gives \(p=15\). \(AM=\tfrac{27}{\sqrt{20}}\) and \(BM=\sqrt{AB^2-AM^2}=\tfrac9{\sqrt{20}}\).

questions.q: The shortest distance between the curves \(y^2=8x\) and \(x^2+y^2+12y+35=0\) is :
questions.sol: The circle has centre \((0,-6)\), radius \(1\). For \((2t^2,4t)\), \(d^2=4t^4+(4t+6)^2\) is least at \(t=-1\): \(d=2\sqrt2\).

questions.q: Let the equation \(x(x+2)(12-k)=2\) have equal roots. Then the distance of the point \(\left(k,\dfrac k2\right)\) from the line \(3x+4y+5=0\) is
questions.sol: \((12-k)x^2+2(12-k)x-2=0\) has zero discriminant when \(12-k=-2\), so \(k=14\). Distance \(\tfrac{|42+28+5|}5\).

questions.q: Consider the lines \(x(3\lambda+1)+y(7\lambda+2)=17\lambda+5\), \(\lambda\) being a parameter, all passing through a point \(P\). One of these lines (say \(L\)) is farthest from the origin. If the distance of \(L\) from the point \((3,6)\) is \(d\), then the value of \(d^2\) is

For an integer \(n\ge2\), if the arithmetic mean of all coefficients in the binomial expansion of \((x+y)^{2n-3}\) is \(16\), then the distance of the point \(P(2n-1,n^2-4n)\) from the line \(x+y=8\) is

Let \(ABC\) be the triangle such that the equations of lines \(AB\) and \(AC\) be \(3y-x=2\) and \(x+y=2\), respectively, and the points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on \(x\)-axis. If \(P\) is the orthocentre of the triangle \(ABC\), then the area of the triangle \(PBC\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(B(-2,0)\), \(C(2,0)\), \(A(1,1)\). The altitudes \(x=1\) and \(y=x+2\) meet at \(P(1,3)\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot3\).

questions.q: If for \(\theta\in\left[-\dfrac\pi3,0\right]\), the points \((x,y)=\left(3\tan\left(\theta+\dfrac\pi3\right),2\tan\left(\theta+\dfrac\pi6\right)\right)\) lie on \(xy+\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0\), then \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: With \(t=\tfrac y2=\tan\left(\theta+\tfrac\pi6\right)\): \(\tfrac x3=\dfrac{t+\frac1{\sqrt3}}{1-\frac t{\sqrt3}}\), which simplifies to \(xy-2\sqrt3x+3\sqrt3y+6=0\). Value \(12+27+36\).

questions.q: If the orthocenter of the triangle formed by the lines \(y=x+1\), \(y=4x-8\) and \(y=mx+c\) is at \((3,-1)\), then \(m-c\) is :
questions.sol: The first two lines meet at \((3,4)\), so the altitude from there is \(x=3\) and the third side is horizontal: \(m=0\). Its vertices are \((c-1,c)\) and \(\left(\tfrac{c+8}4,c\right)\); the altitude from \((c-1,c)\) (\(\perp y=4x-8\)) through \((3,-1)\) gives \(c=0\).

questions.q: A line passing through the point \(P(a,0)\) makes an acute angle \(\alpha\) with the positive \(x\)-axis. Let this line be rotated about the point \(P\) through an angle \(\dfrac\alpha2\) in the clock-wise direction. If in the new position, the slope of the line is \(2-\sqrt3\) and its distance from the origin is \(\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\), then the value of \(3a^2\tan^2\alpha-2\sqrt3\) is :
questions.sol: The new inclination \(\tfrac\alpha2=15^\circ\), so \(\alpha=30^\circ\). Distance \(|a|\sin15^\circ=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\) gives \(a^2=4+2\sqrt3\). Value \((4+2\sqrt3)-2\sqrt3\).

questions.q: Let \(a\) be the length of a side of a square \(OABC\) with \(O\) being the origin. Its side \(OA\) makes an acute angle \(\alpha\) with the positive \(x\)-axis and the equations of its diagonals are \((\sqrt3+1)x+(\sqrt3-1)y=0\) and \((\sqrt3-1)x-(\sqrt3+1)y+8\sqrt3=0\). Then \(a^2\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The first diagonal passes through \(O\); the distance of \(O\) from the second is \(\tfrac{8\sqrt3}{\sqrt8}=2\sqrt6=\tfrac a{\sqrt2}\).

questions.q: Let the triangle \(PQR\) be the image of the triangle with vertices \((1,3)\), \((3,1)\) and \((2,4)\) in the line \(x+2y=2\). If the centroid of \(\Delta PQR\) is the point \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(15(\alpha-\beta)\) is equal to:
questions.sol: The image of the centroid \(\left(2,\tfrac83\right)\): \(\left(2-\tfrac{32}{15},\tfrac83-\tfrac{64}{15}\right)=\left(-\tfrac2{15},-\tfrac{24}{15}\right)\).

questions.q: A rod of length eight units moves such that its ends \(A\) and \(B\) always lie on the lines \(x-y+2=0\) and \(y+2=0\), respectively. If the locus of the point \(P\), that divides the rod \(AB\) internally in the ratio \(2:1\) is \(9(x^2+\alpha y^2+\beta xy+\gamma x+28y)-76=0\), then \(\alpha-\beta-\gamma\) is equal to:

Let the range of the function \(f(x)=6+16\cos x\cdot\cos\left(\dfrac\pi3-x\right)\cdot\cos\left(\dfrac\pi3+x\right)\cdot\sin3x\cdot\cos6x\), \(x\in\mathbf R\) be \([\alpha,\beta]\). Then the distance of the point \((\alpha,\beta)\) from the line \(3x+4y+12=0\) is:
questions.sol: \(4\cos x\cos\left(\tfrac\pi3-x\right)\cos\left(\tfrac\pi3+x\right)=\cos3x\), so \(f=6+4\cos3x\sin3x\cos6x=6+\sin12x\in[5,7]\). Distance \(\tfrac{15+28+12}5\).

questions.q: Let the lines \(3x-4y-\alpha=0\), \(8x-11y-33=0\), and \(2x-3y+\lambda=0\) be concurrent. If the image of the point \((1,2)\) in the line \(2x-3y+\lambda=0\) is \(\left(\dfrac{57}{13},\dfrac{-40}{13}\right)\), then \(|\alpha\lambda|\) is equal to
questions.sol: The midpoint \(\left(\tfrac{35}{13},-\tfrac7{13}\right)\) lies on the line, so \(\lambda=-7\). The last two lines meet at \((11,5)\), so \(\alpha=33-20=13\).

questions.q: Two equal sides of an isosceles triangle are along \(-x+2y=4\) and \(x+y=4\). If \(m\) is the slope of its third side, then the sum, of all possible distinct values of \(m\), is :
questions.sol: The third side makes equal angles with slopes \(\tfrac12\) and \(-1\): \(\dfrac{2m-1}{2+m}=-\dfrac{m+1}{1-m}\) gives \(m^2-6m-1=0\) (the other sign gives no real \(m\)).

questions.q: The vertices of a triangle are \(A(-1,3)\), \(B(-2,2)\) and \(C(3,-1)\). A new triangle is formed by shifting the sides of the triangle by one unit inwards. Then the equation of the side of the new triangle nearest to origin is
questions.sol: The sides are \(x-y+4=0\), \(3x+5y-4=0\), \(x+y-2=0\); the origin lies outside, beyond \(BC\). Shifted inward: \(AB\) is at distance \(2\sqrt2-1\), \(BC\) moves away from \(O\), and \(CA\) becomes \(x+y=2-\sqrt2\) at distance \(\sqrt2-1\).

questions.q: Let two straight lines drawn from the origin \(O\) intersect the line \(3x+4y=12\) at the points \(P\) and \(Q\) such that \(\Delta OPQ\) is an isosceles triangle and \(\angle POQ=90^\circ\). If \(l=OP^2+PQ^2+QO^2\), then the greatest integer less than or equal to \(l\) is :
questions.sol: The altitude from \(O\) is \(\tfrac{12}5=\tfrac{PQ}2\), so \(PQ=\tfrac{24}5\) and \(l=2PQ^2=46.08\).

questions.q: Let \(A(-1,1)\) and \(B(2,3)\) be two points and \(P\) be a variable point above the line \(AB\) such that the area of \(\Delta PAB\) is \(10\). If the locus of \(P\) is \(ax+by=15\), then \(5a+2b\) is :
questions.sol: \(AB:2x-3y+5=0\), and the area condition gives \(|2x-3y+5|=20\). Above \(AB\) the expression is negative: \(2x-3y=-25\), i.e. \(-\tfrac65x+\tfrac95y=15\).

questions.q: The equations of two sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) of a triangle \(ABC\) are \(4x+y=14\) and \(3x-2y=5\), respectively. The point \(\left(2,-\dfrac43\right)\) divides the third side \(BC\) internally in the ratio \(2:1\), the equation of the side \(BC\) is
The portion of the line \(4x+5y=20\) in the first quadrant is trisected by the lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) passing through the origin. The tangent of an angle between the lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) is :
questions.sol: The trisection points \(\left(\tfrac{10}3,\tfrac43\right)\), \(\left(\tfrac53,\tfrac83\right)\) give slopes \(\tfrac25,\tfrac85\): \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{6/5}{41/25}\).

questions.q: Let \(R\) be the interior region between the lines \(3x-y+1=0\) and \(x+2y-5=0\) containing the origin. The set of all values of \(a\), for which the points \((a^2,a+1)\) lie in \(R\), is :
questions.sol: Same side as \(O\) for both lines: \(3a^2-a>0\) and \(a^2+2a-3<0\).

questions.q: In a \(\Delta ABC\), suppose \(y=x\) is the equation of the bisector of the angle \(B\) and the equation of the side \(AC\) is \(2x-y=2\). If \(2AB=BC\) and the points \(A\) and \(B\) are respectively \((4,6)\) and \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(\alpha+2\beta\) is equal to
questions.sol: The bisector meets \(AC\) at \(D(2,2)\) with \(AD:DC=1:2\), so \(C=(-2,-6)\). The image \(A'(6,4)\) of \(A\) in \(y=x\) lies on \(BC\); line \(CA'\) meets \(y=x\) at \(B(14,14)\).

questions.q: The distance of the point \((2,3)\) from the line \(2x-3y+28=0\), measured parallel to the line \(\sqrt3x-y+1=0\), is equal to
questions.sol: Put \(\left(2+\tfrac r2,3+\tfrac{\sqrt3r}2\right)\) in the line: \(23+r\left(1-\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2\right)=0\), so \(r=\tfrac{46}{3\sqrt3-2}=2(3\sqrt3+2)\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) be the point of intersection of the lines \(3x+2y=14\), \(5x-y=6\) and \(B\) be the point of intersection of the lines \(4x+3y=8\), \(6x+y=5\). The distance of the point \(P(5,-2)\) from the line \(AB\) is
questions.sol: \(A(2,4)\), \(B\left(\tfrac12,2\right)\), \(AB:4x-3y+4=0\). Distance \(\tfrac{30}5\).

questions.q: A line passing through the point \(A(9,0)\) makes an angle of \(30^\circ\) with the positive direction of \(x\)-axis. If this line is rotated about \(A\) through an angle of \(15^\circ\) in the clockwise direction, then its equations in the new position is
questions.sol: The new slope is \(\tan15^\circ=2-\sqrt3\): \(y=(2-\sqrt3)(x-9)\), i.e. \(x+\dfrac y{\sqrt3-2}=9\).

questions.q: If \(x^2-y^2+2hxy+2gx+2fy+c=0\) is the locus of a point, which moves such that it is always equidistant from the lines \(x+2y+7=0\) and \(2x-y+8=0\), then the value of \(g+c+h-f\) equals

Let \(A(a,b)\), \(B(3,4)\) and \(C(-6,-8)\) respectively denote the centroid, circumcentre and orthocentre of a triangle. Then, the distance of the point \(P(2a+3,7b+5)\) from the line \(2x+3y-4=0\) measured parallel to the line \(x-2y-1=0\) is
questions.sol: The centroid is \(\tfrac{2B+C}3=(0,0)\), so \(P=(3,5)\). Along direction \((2,1)\): \((3+2t,5+t)\) meets the line at \(t=-\tfrac{17}7\).

questions.q: The straight lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) pass through the origin and trisect the line segment of the line \(L:9x+5y=45\) between the axes. If \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) are the slopes of the lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\), then the point of intersection of the line \(y=(m_1+m_2)x\) with \(L\) lies on
questions.sol: Trisection points \(\left(\tfrac{10}3,3\right)\), \(\left(\tfrac53,6\right)\): \(m_1+m_2=\tfrac9{10}+\tfrac{18}5=\tfrac92\). The intersection is \(\left(\tfrac{10}7,\tfrac{45}7\right)\).

questions.q: Let \((\alpha,\beta)\) be the centroid of the triangle formed by the lines \(15x-y=82\), \(6x-5y=-4\) and \(9x+4y=17\). Then \(\alpha+2\beta\) and \(2\alpha-\beta\) are the roots of the equation
If \((\alpha,\beta)\) is the orthocenter of the triangle \(ABC\) with vertices \(A(3,-7)\), \(B(-1,2)\) and \(C(4,5)\), then \(9\alpha-6\beta+60\) is equal to
questions.sol: The altitudes \(5x+3y=-6\) and \(x+12y=23\) meet at \(\left(-\tfrac{141}{57},\tfrac{121}{57}\right)\). Then \(9\alpha-6\beta=-35\).

questions.q: The combined equation of the two lines \(ax+by+c=0\) and \(a'x+b'y+c'=0\) can be written as \((ax+by+c)(a'x+b'y+c')=0\). The equation of the angle bisectors of the lines represented by the equation \(2x^2+xy-3y^2=0\) is
questions.sol: Bisectors: \(\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{a-b}=\dfrac{xy}h\) with \(a=2\), \(b=-3\), \(h=\tfrac12\).

questions.q: A light ray emits from the origin making an angle \(30^\circ\) with the positive \(x\)-axis. After getting reflected by the line \(x+y=1\), if this ray intersects \(x\)-axis at \(Q\), then the abscissa of \(Q\) is
questions.sol: The ray meets the mirror at \(\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt3+1},\tfrac1{\sqrt3+1}\right)\). Reflection in \(x+y=1\) turns direction \((\sqrt3,1)\) into \((-1,-\sqrt3)\), which reaches \(y=0\) at \(x=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt3+1}-\tfrac1{\sqrt3(\sqrt3+1)}\).

questions.q: Let \(B\) and \(C\) be the two points on the line \(y+x=0\) such that \(B\) and \(C\) are symmetric with respect to the origin. Suppose \(A\) is a point on \(y-2x=2\) such that \(\Delta ABC\) is an equilateral triangle. Then, the area of the \(\Delta ABC\) is
questions.sol: \(A\) lies on \(y=x\) (the perpendicular bisector of \(BC\)): \(A(-2,-2)\), height \(2\sqrt2\). Area \(=\dfrac{h^2}{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: A straight line cuts off the intercepts \(OA=a\) and \(OB=b\) on the positive directions of \(x\)-axis and \(y\)-axis respectively. If the perpendicular from origin \(O\) to this line makes an angle of \(\dfrac\pi6\) with positive direction of \(y\)-axis and the area of \(\Delta OAB\) is \(\dfrac{98}3\sqrt3\), then \(a^2-b^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: The normal makes \(60^\circ\) with the \(x\)-axis: \(a=2p\), \(b=\tfrac{2p}{\sqrt3}\). Area \(\tfrac{2p^2}{\sqrt3}=\tfrac{98}{\sqrt3}\), so \(p=7\).

questions.q: A line, with the slope greater than one, passes through the point \(A(4,3)\) and intersects the line \(x-y-2=0\) at the point \(B\). If the length of the line segment \(AB\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{29}}3\), then \(B\) also lies on the line :
questions.sol: \(B(t,t-2)\): \((t-4)^2+(t-5)^2=\tfrac{29}9\) gives \(t=\tfrac{10}3\) or \(\tfrac{17}3\); only \(t=\tfrac{10}3\) gives slope \(\tfrac52>1\). \(B\left(\tfrac{10}3,\tfrac43\right)\).

questions.q: Let the point \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) be at a unit distance from each of the two lines \(L_1:3x-4y+12=0\), and \(L_2:8x+6y+11=0\). If \(P\) lies below \(L_1\) and above \(L_2\), then \(100(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to

Let \(A(1,1)\), \(B(-4,3)\), \(C(-2,-5)\) be vertices of a triangle \(ABC\), \(P\) be a point on side \(BC\), and \(\Delta_1\) and \(\Delta_2\) be the areas of triangles \(APB\) and \(ABC\), respectively. If \(\Delta_1:\Delta_2=4:7\), then the area enclosed by the lines \(AP\), \(AC\) and the \(x\)-axis is
questions.sol: \(BP:BC=4:7\), so \(P=\left(-\tfrac{20}7,-\tfrac{11}7\right)\) and \(AP\) has slope \(\tfrac23\), meeting the \(x\)-axis at \(-\tfrac12\). \(AC\) (slope \(2\)) meets it at \(\tfrac12\). The triangle has base \(1\) and height \(1\).

questions.q: The equations of the sides \(AB\), \(BC\) and \(CA\) of a triangle \(ABC\) are \(2x+y=0\), \(x+py=39\) and \(x-y=3\) respectively and \(P(2,3)\) is its circumcentre. Then which of the following is not true ?
questions.sol: \(A(1,-2)\) with \(PA^2=26\); then \(B\left(-\tfrac{13}5,\tfrac{26}5\right)\) and \(C(7,4)\), so \(p=8\), \(AC^2=72\) and the area is \(32.4\).

questions.q: Let the circumcentre of a triangle with vertices \(A(a,3)\), \(B(b,5)\) and \(C(a,b)\), \(ab>0\) be \(P(1,1)\). If the line \(AP\) intersects the line \(BC\) at the point \(Q(k_1,k_2)\), then \(k_1+k_2\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(PA=PC\) gives \((b-1)^2=4\); \(PA=PB\) then gives \((a-1)^2=16\). Non-degenerate with \(ab>0\): \(a=-3\), \(b=-1\). \(AP:x+2y=3\) and \(BC:y=3x+8\) meet at \(\left(-\tfrac{13}7,\tfrac{17}7\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(m_1\), \(m_2\) be the slopes of two adjacent sides of a square of side \(a\) such that \(a^2+11a+3(m_1^2+m_2^2)=220\). If one vertex of the square is \((10(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha),10(\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha))\), where \(\alpha\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) and the equation of one diagonal is \((\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha)x+(\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha)y=10\), then \(72(\sin^4\alpha+\cos^4\alpha)+a^2-3a+13\) is equal to:
questions.sol: The vertex \(V\) is at distance \(10\sqrt2\) along the normal of the given diagonal, which is at distance \(5\sqrt2\); so half the other diagonal is \(5\sqrt2\) and \(a=10\). The sides have slopes \(\tan\alpha\) and \(-\cot\alpha\), so \(\tan^2\alpha+\cot^2\alpha=\tfrac{10}3\) and \(\sin^22\alpha=\tfrac34\). Value \(72\cdot\tfrac58+83\).

questions.q: Let \(R\) be the point \((3,7)\) and let \(P\) and \(Q\) be two points on the line \(x+y=5\) such that \(PQR\) is an equilateral triangle. Then the area of \(\Delta PQR\) is :
questions.sol: The height is \(\tfrac5{\sqrt2}\) and area \(=\tfrac{h^2}{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: In an isosceles triangle \(ABC\), the vertex \(A\) is \((6,1)\) and the equation of the base \(BC\) is \(2x+y=4\). Let the point \(B\) lie on the line \(x+3y=7\). If \((\alpha,\beta)\) is the centroid of \(\Delta ABC\), then \(15(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(B(1,2)\); the foot of \(A\) on \(BC\) is the midpoint \(\left(\tfrac{12}5,-\tfrac45\right)\), so \(C=\left(\tfrac{19}5,-\tfrac{18}5\right)\). Centroid \(\left(\tfrac{18}5,-\tfrac15\right)\).

questions.q: Let a triangle be bounded by the lines \(L_1:2x+5y=10\); \(L_2:-4x+3y=12\) and the line \(L_3\), which passes through the point \(P(2,3)\), intersects \(L_2\) at \(A\) and \(L_1\) at \(B\). If the point \(P\) divides the line-segment \(AB\), internally in the ratio \(1:3\), then the area of the triangle is equal to :
questions.sol: \(P=\tfrac{3A+B}4\) gives \(A\left(\tfrac3{13},\tfrac{56}{13}\right)\), \(B\left(\tfrac{95}{13},-\tfrac{12}{13}\right)\); \(L_1\cap L_2=\left(-\tfrac{15}{13},\tfrac{32}{13}\right)\). The shoelace formula gives \(\tfrac{1716}{169}\).

questions.q: The distance between the two points \(A\) and \(A'\) which lie on \(y=2\) such that both the line segments \(AB\) and \(A'B\) (where \(B\) is the point \((2,3)\)) subtend angle \(\dfrac\pi4\) at the origin, is equal to
The distance of the origin from the centroid of the triangle whose two sides have the equations \(x-2y+1=0\) and \(2x-y-1=0\) and whose orthocenter is \(\left(\dfrac73,\dfrac73\right)\) is :
questions.sol: The sides meet at \(A(1,1)\); \(AH\) is \(y=x\), so \(BC:x+y=k\). Requiring \(BH\perp AC\) gives \(k=5\): \(B(3,2)\), \(C(2,3)\). Centroid \((2,2)\).

questions.q: Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with \(A(-3,1)\) and \(\angle ACB=\theta\), \(0<\theta<\pi/2\). If the equation of the median through \(B\) is \(2x+y-3=0\) and the equation of angle bisector of \(C\) is \(7x-4y-1=0\), then \(\tan\theta\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(C\left(c,\tfrac{7c-1}4\right)\) with the midpoint of \(AC\) on the median gives \(C(3,5)\). The half-angle between \(CA\) (slope \(\tfrac23\)) and the bisector (slope \(\tfrac74\)) has tangent \(\tfrac12\), so \(\tan\theta=\tfrac43\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) be a fixed point \((0,6)\) and \(B\) be a moving point \((2t,0)\). Let \(M\) be the mid-point of \(AB\) and the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\) meets the \(y\)-axis at \(C\). The locus of the mid-point \(P\) of \(MC\) is
questions.sol: \(M(t,3)\) and the perpendicular bisector (slope \(\tfrac t3\)) meets the \(y\)-axis at \(C\left(0,3-\tfrac{t^2}3\right)\). \(P=\left(\tfrac t2,3-\tfrac{t^2}6\right)\).

questions.q: If \(p\) and \(q\) are the lengths of the perpendiculars from the origin on the lines, \(x\operatorname{cosec}\alpha-y\sec\alpha=k\cot2\alpha\) and \(x\sin\alpha+y\cos\alpha=k\sin2\alpha\) respectively, then \(k^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(p=|k\cot2\alpha|\sin\alpha\cos\alpha=\tfrac{|k\cos2\alpha|}2\) and \(q=|k\sin2\alpha|\).

questions.q: Let the equation of the pair of lines, \(y=px\) and \(y=qx\), can be written as \((y-px)(y-qx)=0\). Then the equation of the pair of the angle bisectors of the lines \(x^2-4xy-5y^2=0\) is

Two sides of a parallelogram are along the lines \(4x+5y=0\) and \(7x+2y=0\). If the equation of one of the diagonals of the parallelogram is \(11x+7y=9\), then other diagonal passes through the point
questions.sol: The given diagonal meets the sides at \(\left(\tfrac53,-\tfrac43\right)\) and \(\left(-\tfrac23,\tfrac73\right)\), with midpoint \(\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)\). The other diagonal joins \(O\) to it: \(y=x\).

questions.q:
The point \(P(a,b)\) undergoes the following three transformations successively :
(A) reflection about the line \(y=x\).
(B) translation through \(2\) units along the positive direction of \(x\)-axis.
(C) rotation through angle \(\dfrac\pi4\) about the origin in the anti-clockwise direction.
If the co-ordinates of the final position of the point \(P\) are \(\left(-\dfrac1{\sqrt2},\dfrac7{\sqrt2}\right)\), then the value of \(2a+b\) is equal to
questions.sol: \((a,b)\to(b,a)\to(b+2,a)\to\left(\tfrac{b+2-a}{\sqrt2},\tfrac{b+2+a}{\sqrt2}\right)\), so \(a=4\), \(b=1\).

questions.q: Let \(A(-1,1)\), \(B(3,4)\) and \(C(2,0)\) be given three points. A line \(y=mx\), \(m>0\), intersects lines \(AC\) and \(BC\) at points \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively. Let \(A_1\) and \(A_2\) be the areas of \(\Delta ABC\) and \(\Delta PQC\) respectively, such that \(A_1=3A_2\), then the value of \(m\) is equal to

In a triangle \(PQR\), the co-ordinates of the points \(P\) and \(Q\) are \((-2,4)\) and \((4,-2)\) respectively. If the equation of the perpendicular bisector of \(PR\) is \(2x-y+2=0\), then the centre of the circumcircle of the \(\Delta PQR\) is
questions.sol: The perpendicular bisector of \(PQ\) is \(y=x\); it meets \(2x-y+2=0\) at \((-2,-2)\).

questions.q: The equation of one of the straight lines which passes through the point \((1,3)\) and makes an angle \(\tan^{-1}(\sqrt2)\) with the straight line, \(y+1=3\sqrt2x\) is
questions.sol: \(\left|\dfrac{m-3\sqrt2}{1+3\sqrt2m}\right|=\sqrt2\) gives \(m=-\tfrac{4\sqrt2}5\) or \(\tfrac{2\sqrt2}7\). With the first: \(4\sqrt2x+5y=15+4\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The number of integral values of \(m\) so that the abscissa of point of intersection of lines \(3x+4y=9\) and \(y=mx+1\) is also an integer, is
questions.sol: \(x=\dfrac5{3+4m}\); integral \(m\) needs \(3+4m\in\{-1,-5\}\).

questions.q: A man is walking on a straight line. The arithmetic mean of the reciprocals of the intercepts of this line on the coordinate axes is \(\dfrac14\). Three stones \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are placed at the points \((1,1)\), \((2,2)\) and \((4,4)\) respectively. Then which of these stones is/are on the path of the man?
questions.sol: \(\tfrac1a+\tfrac1b=\tfrac12\) means \(\tfrac xa+\tfrac yb=1\) passes through \((2,2)\).

questions.q: The image of the point \((3,5)\) in the line \(x-y+1=0\), lies on
questions.sol: The image is \((4,4)\).

questions.q: The intersection of three lines \(x-y=0\), \(x+2y=3\) and \(2x+y=6\) is a
questions.sol: With slopes \(1,-\tfrac12,-2\): the angles at the two vertices on \(y=x\) both have tangent \(3\).

questions.q: If a \(\Delta ABC\) has vertices \(A(-1,7)\), \(B(-7,1)\) and \(C(5,-5)\), then its orthocentre has coordinates
questions.sol: The altitudes \(y=-x\) (from \(C\)) and \(y=2x+9\) (from \(A\)) meet at \((-3,3)\).

questions.q: A triangle \(ABC\) lying in the first quadrant has two vertices as \(A(1,2)\) and \(B(3,1)\). If \(\angle BAC=90^\circ\) and \(\text{ar}(\Delta ABC)=5\sqrt5\) sq. units, then the abscissa of the vertex \(C\) is
questions.sol: \(AB=\sqrt5\), so \(AC=10\) along direction \(\tfrac{(1,2)}{\sqrt5}\): \(C=(1+2\sqrt5,2+4\sqrt5)\).

questions.q: If the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points \(P(1,4)\) and \(Q(k,3)\) has \(y\)-intercept equal to \(-4\), then a value of \(k\) is
questions.sol: The bisector \(y-\tfrac72=(k-1)\left(x-\tfrac{1+k}2\right)\) has \(y\)-intercept \(\tfrac{8-k^2}2=-4\).

questions.q: A ray of light coming from the point \((2,2\sqrt3)\) is incident at an angle \(30^\circ\) on the line \(x=1\) at the point \(A\). The ray gets reflected on the line \(x=1\) and meets \(x\)-axis at the point \(B\). Then, the line \(AB\) passes through the point
questions.sol: The incident ray has direction \((-1,-\sqrt3)\), so \(A=(1,\sqrt3)\); after reflection the direction is \((1,-\sqrt3)\): \(AB:y=-\sqrt3x+2\sqrt3\).

questions.q: Let \(L\) denote the line in the \(xy\)-plane with \(x\) and \(y\) intercepts as \(3\) and \(1\) respectively. Then the image of the point \((-1,-4)\) in this line is
The locus of the mid-points of the perpendiculars drawn from points on the line \(x=2y\) to the line \(x=y\) is
questions.sol: From \((2t,t)\) the foot on \(y=x\) is \(\left(\tfrac{3t}2,\tfrac{3t}2\right)\); the midpoint is \(\left(\tfrac{7t}4,\tfrac{5t}4\right)\).

questions.q: The length of the perpendicular from the origin, on the normal to the curve, \(x^2+2xy-3y^2=0\) at the point \((2,2)\) is
questions.sol: \(y'=\dfrac{x+y}{3y-x}=1\) at \((2,2)\); the normal is \(x+y=4\).

questions.q: Let \(C\) be the centroid of the triangle with vertices \((3,-1)\), \((1,3)\) and \((2,4)\). Let \(P\) be the point of intersection of the lines \(x+3y-1=0\) and \(3x-y+1=0\). Then the line passing through the points \(C\) and \(P\) also passes through the point
questions.sol: \(C(2,2)\), \(P\left(-\tfrac15,\tfrac25\right)\); the line \(y-2=\tfrac8{11}(x-2)\) passes through \((-9,-6)\).

questions.q: A point on the straight line, \(3x+5y=15\), which is equidistant from the coordinate axes will lie only in
questions.sol: \(y=x\) gives \(\left(\tfrac{15}8,\tfrac{15}8\right)\) and \(y=-x\) gives \(\left(-\tfrac{15}2,\tfrac{15}2\right)\).

questions.q: Suppose that the points \((h,k)\), \((1,2)\) and \((-3,4)\) lie on the line \(L_1\). If a line \(L_2\) passing through the points \((h,k)\) and \((4,3)\) is perpendicular to \(L_1\), then \(k/h\) equals
questions.sol: \(L_1\) has slope \(-\tfrac12\); \(\tfrac{k-3}{h-4}=2\) with \(k=\tfrac52-\tfrac h2\) gives \((h,k)=(3,1)\).

questions.q: Slope of a line passing through \(P(2,3)\) and intersecting the line, \(x+y=7\) at a distance of \(4\) units from \(P\), is
questions.sol: \((2+4\cos\theta,3+4\sin\theta)\) on the line gives \(\cos\theta+\sin\theta=\tfrac12\), so \(\sin2\theta=-\tfrac34\) and \(3t^2+8t+3=0\): \(t=\tfrac{-4\pm\sqrt7}3\), and \(\tfrac{1-\sqrt7}{1+\sqrt7}=-\tfrac{4-\sqrt7}3\).

questions.q: If the two lines \(x+(a-1)y=1\) and \(2x+a^2y=1\) \((a\in R-\{0,1\})\) are perpendicular, then the distance of their point of intersection from the origin is
questions.sol: \(2+a^2(a-1)=0\) gives \(a=-1\). The lines \(x-2y=1\), \(2x+y=1\) meet at \(\left(\tfrac35,-\tfrac15\right)\).

questions.q: Lines are drawn parallel to the line \(4x-3y+2=0\), at a distance \(\dfrac35\) from the origin. Then which one of the following points lies on any of these lines?
questions.sol: The lines are \(4x-3y=\pm3\); \(\left(-\tfrac14,\tfrac23\right)\) gives \(-3\).

questions.q: The equation \(y=\sin x\sin(x+2)-\sin^2(x+1)\) represents a straight line lying in
questions.sol: \(y=\tfrac{\cos2-\cos(2x+2)}2-\tfrac{1-\cos(2x+2)}2=\tfrac{\cos2-1}2<0\), a horizontal line below the \(x\)-axis.

questions.q: A straight line \(L\) at a distance of \(4\) units from the origin makes positive intercepts on the coordinate axes and the perpendicular from the origin to this line makes an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the line \(x+y=0\). Then an equation of the line \(L\) is
questions.sol: The normal makes \(75^\circ\) or \(15^\circ\) with the \(x\)-axis: \(x\cos75^\circ+y\sin75^\circ=4\) gives (a), and \(15^\circ\) gives (b). (Both (a) and (b) are correct; the book key lists both.)

questions.q: Consider the set of all lines \(px+qy+r=0\) such that \(3p+2q+4r=0\). Which one of the following statements is true?
opts: Each line passes through the origin.
The lines are concurrent at the point \((3/4,1/2)\).
questions.sol: Dividing the condition by \(4\): \(p\cdot\tfrac34+q\cdot\tfrac12+r=0\).

questions.q: Let the equations of two sides of a triangle be \(3x-2y+6=0\) and \(4x+5y-20=0\). If the orthocentre of this triangle is at \((1,1)\), then the equation of its third side is
questions.sol: The given sides meet at \(A\left(\tfrac{10}{23},\tfrac{84}{23}\right)\), so the third side is \(\perp AH\): \(13x-61y=c\). The altitude from \(B\) (\(\perp\) the second side) through \(H\) meets \(3x-2y+6=0\) at \(B\left(-13,-\tfrac{33}2\right)\), giving \(c=\tfrac{1675}2\).

questions.q: If the line \(3x+4y-24=0\) intersects the \(x\)-axis at the point \(A\) and the \(y\)-axis at the point \(B\), then the incentre of the triangle \(OAB\), where \(O\) is the origin, is
questions.sol: Legs \(8,6\), hypotenuse \(10\): \(r=2\).

questions.q: Two vertices of a triangle are \((0,2)\) and \((4,3)\). If its orthocentre is at the origin, then its third vertex lies in which quadrant?
questions.sol: \(OA\) is vertical, so \(BC\) is horizontal: \(k=3\); \(OC\perp AB\): \(4h+k=0\). \(C=\left(-\tfrac34,3\right)\).

questions.q: In a parallelogram \(ABDC\), the coordinates of \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are respectively \((1,2)\), \((3,4)\) and \((2,5)\), then the equation of the diagonal \(AD\) is
If the straight line, \(2x-3y+17=0\) is perpendicular to the line passing through the points \((7,17)\) and \((15,\beta)\), then \(\beta\) equals
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\beta-17}8=-\dfrac32\).

questions.q: If a straight line passing through the point \(P(-3,4)\) is such that its intercepted portion between the coordinate axes is bisected at \(P\), then its equation is
questions.sol: The intercepts are \(-6\) and \(8\).

questions.q: A straight line through a fixed point \((2,3)\) intersects the coordinate axes at distinct points \(P\) and \(Q\). If \(O\) is the origin and the rectangle \(OPRQ\) is completed, then the locus of \(R\) is
questions.sol: \(R=(a,b)\) with \(\tfrac2a+\tfrac3b=1\).

questions.q: The sides of a rhombus \(ABCD\) are parallel to the lines, \(x-y+2=0\) and \(7x-y+3=0\). If the diagonals of the rhombus intersect at \(P(1,2)\) and the vertex \(A\) (different from the origin) is on the \(y\)-axis, then the ordinate of \(A\) is
questions.sol: The diagonals bisect the angles between the side directions: slopes \(2\) and \(-\tfrac12\). Through \(P\) the slope-\(2\) diagonal passes through the origin, so \(A\) is on the other: \(y-2=-\tfrac12(x-1)\) at \(x=0\).

questions.q: The foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin on the line, \(3x+y=\lambda\) \((\lambda\ne0)\) is \(P\). If the line meets \(x\)-axis at \(A\) and \(y\)-axis at \(B\), then the ratio \(BP:PA\) is
questions.sol: \(P=\tfrac\lambda{10}(3,1)\), \(A\left(\tfrac\lambda3,0\right)\), \(B(0,\lambda)\): \(P=A+\tfrac1{10}(B-A)\).

questions.q: Let \(k\) be an integer such that triangle with vertices \((k,-3k)\), \((5,k)\) and \((-k,2)\) has area \(28\) sq. units. Then the orthocentre of this triangle is at the point
A line drawn through the point \(P(4,7)\) cuts the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Then \(PA\cdot PB\) is equal to
Two sides of a rhombus are along the lines, \(x-y+1=0\) and \(7x-y-5=0\). If its diagonals intersect at \((-1,-2)\), then which one of the following is a vertex of this rhombus?
questions.sol: The sides meet at \((1,2)\); the opposite vertex is \((-3,-6)\), with sides \(x-y-3=0\) and \(7x-y+15=0\). The remaining vertices are \(\left(\tfrac13,-\tfrac83\right)\) and \(\left(-\tfrac73,-\tfrac43\right)\).

questions.q: If a variable line drawn through the intersection of the lines \(\dfrac x3+\dfrac y4=1\) and \(\dfrac x4+\dfrac y3=1\), meets the coordinate axes at \(A\) and \(B\), \((A\ne B)\), then the locus of the midpoint of \(AB\) is
questions.sol: The lines meet at \(\left(\tfrac{12}7,\tfrac{12}7\right)\), so \(\tfrac{12}7\left(\tfrac1{2h}+\tfrac1{2k}\right)=1\), i.e. \(6(h+k)=7hk\).

questions.q: The point \((2,1)\) is translated parallel to the line \(L:x-y=4\) by \(2\sqrt3\) units. If the new point \(Q\) lies in the third quadrant, then the equation of the line passing through \(Q\) and perpendicular to \(L\) is
A straight line through origin \(O\) meets the lines \(3y=10-4x\) and \(8x+6y+5=0\) at points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively. Then \(O\) divides the segment \(AB\) in the ratio

A ray of light is incident along a line which meets another line, \(7x-y+1=0\), at the point \((0,1)\). The ray is then reflected from this point along the line, \(y+2x=1\). Then the equation of the line of incidence of the ray of light is
questions.sol: The mirror (slope \(7\)) bisects the angle: \(\dfrac{m-7}{1+7m}=\dfrac{7+2}{1-14}\), so \(m=\tfrac{41}{38}\).
Both consecutive slopes equal \(\tfrac13\).

questions.q: Let \(L\) be the line passing through the point \(P(1,2)\) such that its intercepted segment between the co-ordinate axes is bisected at \(P\). If \(L_1\) is the line perpendicular to \(L\) and passing through the point \((-2,1)\), then the point of intersection of \(L\) and \(L_1\) is
A straight line \(L\) through the point \((3,-2)\) is inclined at an angle of \(60^\circ\) to the line \(\sqrt3x+y=1\). If \(L\) also intersects the \(x\)-axis, then the equation of \(L\) is
questions.sol: The given line has inclination \(120^\circ\); \(L\) has inclination \(60^\circ\) (the other choice, \(0^\circ\), would be parallel to the \(x\)-axis). \(y+2=\sqrt3(x-3)\).

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\) and \(d\) be non-zero numbers. If the point of intersection of the lines \(4ax+2ay+c=0\) and \(5bx+2by+d=0\) lies in the fourth quadrant and is equidistant from the two axes, then
questions.sol: At \((k,-k)\): \(2ak+c=0\) and \(3bk+d=0\), so \(\tfrac c{2a}=\tfrac d{3b}\).

questions.q: Let \(PS\) be the median of the triangle whose vertices \(P(2,2)\), \(Q(6,-1)\) and \(R(7,3)\). The equation of the line passing through \((1,-1)\) and parallel to \(PS\) is
questions.sol: \(S=\left(\tfrac{13}2,1\right)\), so \(PS\) has slope \(-\tfrac29\).

questions.q: A ray of light along \(x+\sqrt3y=\sqrt3\) gets reflected upon reaching \(x\)-axis, the equation of the reflected ray is
questions.sol: The ray meets the axis at \((\sqrt3,0)\) and its slope \(-\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\) changes sign.

questions.q: If two vertices of a triangle are \((5,-1)\) and \((-2,3)\) and its orthocentre is at \((0,0)\), then the third vertex is

A line is drawn through the point \((1,2)\) to meet the coordinate axes at \(P\) and \(Q\) such that it forms a triangle \(OPQ\), where \(O\) is the origin. If the area of the triangle \(OPQ\) is least, then the slope of the line \(PQ\) is
questions.sol: The area is least when \((1,2)\) bisects \(PQ\): intercepts \(2\) and \(4\).

questions.q:
The lines \(L_1:y-x=0\) and \(L_2:2x+y=0\) intersect the line \(L_3:y+2=0\) at \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively. The bisector of the acute angle between \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) intersects \(L_3\) at \(R\).
Statement-1 : The ratio \(PR:RQ\) equals \(2\sqrt2:\sqrt5\).
Statement-2 : In any triangle, bisector of an angle divides the triangle into two similar triangles.
opts: Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is false.
Statement-1 is false, Statement-2 is true.
Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is true; Statement-2 is a correct explanation for Statement-1.
Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is true; Statement-2 is not a correct explanation for Statement-1.
questions.sol: \(P(-2,-2)\), \(Q(1,-2)\), and \(\angle POQ\) is the acute angle. By the angle-bisector theorem \(PR:RQ=OP:OQ=2\sqrt2:\sqrt5\). Statement-2 is false in general.

questions.q: The equation of the tangent to the curve \(y=x+\dfrac4{x^2}\), that is parallel to the \(x\)-axis, is

The line \(L\) given by \(\dfrac x5+\dfrac yb=1\) passes through the point \((13,32)\). The line \(K\) is parallel to \(L\) and has the equation \(\dfrac xc+\dfrac y3=1\). Then the distance between \(L\) and \(K\) is
The perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining \(P(1,4)\) and \(Q(k,3)\) has \(y\)-intercept \(-4\). Then a possible value of \(k\) is
questions.sol: The \(y\)-intercept of the bisector is \(\tfrac{8-k^2}2\).

questions.q: If one of the lines of \(my^2+(1-m^2)xy-mx^2=0\) is a bisector of the angle between the lines \(xy=0\), then \(m\) is
questions.sol: The pair factors as \((my+x)(y-mx)=0\); \(y=mx\) is \(y=\pm x\) for \(m=\pm1\).

questions.q: Let \(P=(-1,0)\), \(Q=(0,0)\) and \(R=(3,3\sqrt3)\) be three points. The equation of the bisector of the angle \(PQR\) is
questions.sol: \(QP\) is at \(180^\circ\) and \(QR\) at \(60^\circ\); the bisector is at \(120^\circ\).

questions.q: If \((a,a^2)\) falls inside the angle made by the lines \(y=\dfrac x2\), \(x>0\) and \(y=3x\), \(x>0\), then \(a\) belongs to
questions.sol: We need \(a>0\) and \(\tfrac a2<a^2<3a\).

questions.q: A straight line through the point \(A(3,4)\) is such that its intercept between the axes is bisected at \(A\). Its equation is
questions.sol: The intercepts are \(6\) and \(8\).

questions.q: If non-zero numbers \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) are in H.P., then the straight line \(\dfrac xa+\dfrac yb+\dfrac1c=0\) always passes through a fixed point. That point is
questions.sol: \(\tfrac1a-\tfrac2b+\tfrac1c=0\).

questions.q: The line parallel to the \(x\)-axis and passing through the intersection of the lines \(ax+2by+3b=0\) and \(bx-2ay-3a=0\), where \((a,b)\ne(0,0)\) is
opts: below the \(x\)-axis at a distance of \(2/3\) from it
below the \(x\)-axis at a distance of \(3/2\) from it
above the \(x\)-axis at a distance of \(2/3\) from it
above the \(x\)-axis at a distance of \(3/2\) from it
questions.sol: \(a\cdot\)(first) \(+\,b\cdot\)(second) gives \((a^2+b^2)x=0\), so \(x=0\) and \(y=-\tfrac32\).

questions.q: If one of the lines given by \(6x^2-xy+4cy^2=0\) is \(3x+4y=0\), then \(c\) equals
If the sum of the slopes of the lines given by \(x^2-2cxy-7y^2=0\) is four times their product, then \(c\) has the value
questions.sol: The slopes satisfy \(7m^2+2cm-1=0\): \(-\tfrac{2c}7=-\tfrac47\).

questions.q: The equation of the straight line passing through the point \((4,3)\) and making intercepts on the co-ordinate axes whose sum is \(-1\) is
The normal to the curve \(x=a(1+\cos\theta)\), \(y=a\sin\theta\) at \(\theta\) always passes through the fixed point
questions.sol: The curve is the circle \((x-a)^2+y^2=a^2\); every normal passes through its centre.

questions.q: If the pairs of straight lines \(x^2-2pxy-y^2=0\) and \(x^2-2qxy-y^2=0\) be such that each pair bisects the angle between the other pair, then
questions.sol: The bisectors of the first pair are \(\tfrac{x^2-y^2}2=\tfrac{xy}{-p}\), i.e. \(x^2+\tfrac2pxy-y^2=0\); matching gives \(-2q=\tfrac2p\).

questions.q: A square of side \(a\) lies above the \(x\)-axis and has one vertex at the origin. The side passing through the origin makes an angle \(\alpha\) \((0<\alpha<\pi/4)\) with the positive direction of \(x\)-axis. The equation of its diagonal not passing through the origin is
questions.sol: The diagonal joins \((a\cos\alpha,a\sin\alpha)\) and \((-a\sin\alpha,a\cos\alpha)\).

questions.q: A triangle with vertices \((4,0)\), \((-1,-1)\), \((3,5)\) is
questions.sol: The squared sides are \(26,26,52\).

questions.q: Locus of mid point of the portion between the axes of \(x\cos\alpha+y\sin\alpha=p\) where \(p\) is constant is
questions.sol: The midpoint is \(\left(\tfrac p{2\cos\alpha},\tfrac p{2\sin\alpha}\right)\).

questions.q: The point of lines represented by \(3ax^2+5xy+(a^2-2)y^2=0\) and \(\perp\) to each other for
questions.sol: Perpendicular when \(3a+a^2-2=0\), which has two real roots.

questions.q: If the pair of lines \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\) intersect on the \(y\)-axis, then
questions.sol: The intersection point has \(x=0\), so \(\dfrac{hf-bg}{ab-h^2}=0\) gives \(hf=bg\). Putting \(x=0\), \(by^2+2fy+c=0\) must have a double root: \(f^2=bc\). Combining, \(bg^2+ch^2=\tfrac{h^2f^2}b+ch^2=2ch^2=2fgh\).

questions.q: Let the distance between two parallel lines be \(5\) units and a point \(P\) lie between the lines at a unit distance from one of them. An equilateral triangle \(PQR\) is formed such that \(Q\) lies on one of the parallel lines, while \(R\) lies on the other. Then \((QR)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: Take the lines \(y=0\), \(y=5\) and \(P(0,1)\). Rotating \(Q(q,0)\) about \(P\) by \(60^\circ\) must land on \(y=5\): \(\tfrac{\sqrt3q}2-\tfrac12=4\), so \(q=3\sqrt3\) and \(QR^2=PQ^2=q^2+1\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha=1+\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^6(-3)^{r-1}\,{}^{12}C_{2r-1}\), then the distance of the point \((12,\sqrt3)\) from the line \(\alpha x-\sqrt3y+1=0\) is ______.
questions.sol: The sum is \(\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\,\text{Im}(1+i\sqrt3)^{12}=\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\,\text{Im}(4096)=0\), so \(\alpha=1\). Distance \(\tfrac{|12-3+1|}2\).

questions.q: Consider a triangle \(ABC\) having the vertices \(A(1,2)\), \(B(\alpha,\beta)\) and \(C(\gamma,\delta)\) and angles \(\angle ABC=\dfrac\pi6\) and \(\angle BAC=\dfrac{2\pi}3\). If the points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on the line \(y=x+4\), then \(\alpha^2+\gamma^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The triangle is isosceles with altitude \(\tfrac3{\sqrt2}\) from \(A\); the foot is \(M\left(-\tfrac12,\tfrac72\right)\) and \(MB=MC=\tfrac3{\sqrt2}\cot30^\circ\). So \(\alpha,\gamma=-\tfrac12\pm\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2\).

questions.q: Let a ray of light passing through the point \((3,10)\) reflects on the line \(2x+y=6\) and the reflected ray passes through the point \((7,2)\). If the equation of the incident ray is \(ax+by+1=0\), then \(a^2+b^2+3ab\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The incident ray passes through the image of \((7,2)\), which is \((7,2)-4(2,1)=(-1,-2)\). Through \((3,10)\) and \((-1,-2)\): \(3x-y+1=0\).

questions.q: Let \(ABC\) be an isosceles triangle in which \(A\) is at \((-1,0)\), \(\angle A=\dfrac{2\pi}3\), \(AB=AC\) and \(B\) is on the positive \(x\)-axis. If \(BC=4\sqrt3\) and the line \(BC\) intersects the line \(y=x+3\) at \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(\dfrac{\beta^4}{\alpha^2}\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(AB=\tfrac{BC}{2\sin60^\circ}=4\), so \(B(3,0)\) and \(C(-3,2\sqrt3)\). \(BC:y=-\tfrac{x-3}{\sqrt3}\) meets \(y=x+3\) at \(\alpha=3(\sqrt3-2)\), \(\beta=3(\sqrt3-1)\); then \(\tfrac{\beta^4}{\alpha^2}=9\cdot\tfrac{28-16\sqrt3}{7-4\sqrt3}=36\).

questions.q: If the sum of squares of all real values of \(\alpha\), for which the lines \(2x-y+3=0\), \(6x+3y+1=0\) and \(\alpha x+2y-2=0\) do not form a triangle is \(p\), then the greatest integer less than or equal to \(p\) is ______.
questions.sol: Parallel to one of the first two: \(\alpha=\pm4\). Concurrent (through \(\left(-\tfrac56,\tfrac43\right)\)): \(\alpha=\tfrac45\). \(p=32+\tfrac{16}{25}\).

questions.q: Let for any three distinct consecutive terms \(a,b,c\) of an A.P., the lines \(ax+by+c=0\) be concurrent at the point \(P\) and \(Q(\alpha,\beta)\) be a point such that the system of equations \(x+y+z=6\), \(2x+5y+\alpha z=\beta\) and \(x+2y+3z=4\), has infinitely many solutions. Then \((PQ)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(a-2b+c=0\) gives \(P(1,-2)\). The determinant is \(8-\alpha=0\), and consistency (second \(=-\)first\(+3\cdot\)third) gives \(\beta=6\). \(PQ^2=49+64\).

questions.q: Let the equations of two adjacent sides of a parallelogram \(ABCD\) be \(2x-3y=-23\) and \(5x+4y=23\). If the equation of its one diagonal \(AC\) is \(3x+7y=23\) and the distance of \(A\) from the other diagonal is \(d\), then \(50d^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The given sides meet at \(B(-1,7)\); the diagonal meets them at \(A(-4,5)\) and \(C(3,2)\). \(BD\) passes through \(B\) and the midpoint \(\left(-\tfrac12,\tfrac72\right)\): \(7x+y=0\). \(d=\tfrac{23}{\sqrt{50}}\).

questions.q: If the line \(l_1:3y-2x=3\) is the angular bisector of the lines \(l_2:x-y+1=0\) and \(l_3:\alpha x+\beta y+17=0\), then \(\alpha^2+\beta^2-\alpha-\beta\) is equal to ______.

The equations of the sides \(AB\), \(BC\) and \(CA\) of a triangle \(ABC\) are : \(2x+y=0\), \(x+py=21a\), \((a\ne0)\) and \(x-y=3\) respectively. Let \(P(2,a)\) be the centroid of \(\Delta ABC\). Then \((BC)^2\) is equal to ______.

A triangle is formed by \(X\)-axis, \(Y\)-axis and the line \(3x+4y=60\). Then the number of points \(P(a,b)\) which lie strictly inside the triangle, where \(a\) is an integer and \(b\) is a multiple of \(a\), is ______.

A triangle is formed by the tangents at the point \((2,2)\) on the curves \(y^2=2x\) and \(x^2+y^2=4x\), and the line \(x+y+2=0\). If \(r\) is the radius of its circumcircle, then \(r^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The tangents are \(x-2y+2=0\) and \(y=2\). Vertices \((2,2),(-4,2),(-2,0)\): sides \(6,\sqrt8,\sqrt{20}\), area \(6\), so \(R=\tfrac{6\sqrt8\sqrt{20}}{24}=\sqrt{10}\).

questions.q: The equations of the sides \(AB\), \(BC\) and \(CA\) of a triangle \(ABC\) are \(2x+y=0\), \(x+py=15a\) and \(x-y=3\) respectively. If its orthocentre is \((2,a)\), \(-\dfrac12<a<2\), then \(p\) is equal to ______.

Let \(A\left(\dfrac3{\sqrt a},\sqrt a\right)\), \(a>0\), be a fixed point in the \(xy\)-plane. The image of \(A\) in \(y\)-axis be \(B\) and the image of \(B\) in \(x\)-axis be \(C\). If \(D(3\cos\theta,a\sin\theta)\) is a point in the fourth quadrant such that the maximum area of \(\Delta ACD\) is \(12\) square units, then \(a\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(C=\left(-\tfrac3{\sqrt a},-\sqrt a\right)\); the area is \(3\sqrt a|\cos\theta-\sin\theta|\), with maximum \(3\sqrt{2a}=12\) in the fourth quadrant. (The book prints the maximum area as 2; the exam paper has 12.)

questions.q: A ray of light passing through the point \(P(2,3)\) reflects on the \(x\)-axis at point \(A\) and the reflected ray passes through the point \(Q(5,4)\). Let \(R\) be the point that divides the line segment \(AQ\) internally into the ratio \(2:1\). Let the co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular \(M\) from \(R\) on the bisector of the angle \(PAQ\) be \((\alpha,\beta)\). Then, the value of \(7\alpha+3\beta\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(A\left(\tfrac{23}7,0\right)\) (on the line from \((2,-3)\) to \(Q\)). The bisector is the normal \(x=\tfrac{23}7\), and \(R=\left(\tfrac{31}7,\tfrac83\right)\), so \(M=\left(\tfrac{23}7,\tfrac83\right)\).

questions.q: Let the points of intersections of the lines \(x-y+1=0\), \(x-2y+3=0\) and \(2x-5y+11=0\) are the mid points of the sides of a triangle \(ABC\). Then the area of the triangle \(ABC\) is ______.
questions.sol: The midpoints \((1,2),(2,3),(7,5)\) form a triangle of area \(\tfrac32\); \(ABC\) is \(4\) times larger.

questions.q: A man starts walking from the point \(P(-3,4)\), touches the \(x\)-axis at \(R\), and then turns to reach at the point \(Q(0,2)\). The man is walking at a constant speed. If the man reaches the point \(Q\) in the minimum time, then \(50((PR)^2+(RQ)^2)\) is equal to ______.

Consider a triangle having vertices \(A(-2,3)\), \(B(1,9)\) and \(C(3,8)\). If a line \(L\) passing through the circum-center of triangle \(ABC\), bisects line \(BC\), and intersects \(y\)-axis at point \(\left(0,\dfrac\alpha2\right)\), then the value of real number \(\alpha\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(L\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(BC\): through \(\left(2,\tfrac{17}2\right)\) with slope \(2\), meeting the \(y\)-axis at \(\tfrac92\).

questions.q: If the four distinct points \((4,6)\), \((-1,5)\), \((0,0)\) and \((k,3k)\) lie on a circle of radius \(r\), then \(10k+r^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: The circle through the first three is \(x^2+y^2-4x-6y=0\) (\(r^2=13\)). Then \(10k^2-22k=0\) gives \(k=\tfrac{11}5\).

questions.q: Let \(C_1\) be the circle in the third quadrant of radius \(3\), that touches both coordinate axes. Let \(C_2\) be the circle with centre \((1,3)\) that touches \(C_1\) externally at the point \((\alpha,\beta)\). If \((\beta-\alpha)^2=\dfrac mn\), \(\gcd(m,n)=1\), then \(m+n\) is equal to
questions.sol: The centres are \((-3,-3)\) and \((1,3)\), at distance \(2\sqrt{13}\). The contact point is \((-3,-3)+\tfrac3{2\sqrt{13}}(4,6)\), so \(\beta-\alpha=\tfrac3{\sqrt{13}}\).

questions.q: A circle \(C\) of radius \(2\) lies in the second quadrant and touches both the coordinate axes. Let \(r\) be the radius of a circle that has centre at the point \((2,5)\) and intersects the circle \(C\) at exactly two points. If the set of all possible values of \(r\) is the interval \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(3\beta-2\alpha\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(C\) has centre \((-2,2)\); the centres are \(5\) apart, so \(|r-2|<5<r+2\), i.e. \(3<r<7\).

questions.q: Let circle \(C\) be the image of \(x^2+y^2-2x+4y-4=0\) in the line \(2x-3y+5=0\) and \(A\) be the point on \(C\) such that \(OA\) is parallel to \(x\)-axis and \(A\) lies on the right hand side of the centre \(O\) of \(C\). If \(B(\alpha,\beta)\), with \(\beta<4\), lies on \(C\) such that the length of the arc \(AB\) is \((1/6)^{\text{th}}\) of the perimeter of \(C\), then \(\beta-\sqrt3\alpha\) is equal to
questions.sol: The image of the centre \((1,-2)\) is \(O(-3,4)\); \(r=3\) and \(A(0,4)\). Arc \(AB\) subtends \(60^\circ\): \(B=\left(-\tfrac32,4-\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2\right)\).

questions.q: Let the equation of the circle, which touches \(x\)-axis at the point \((a,0)\), \(a>0\) and cuts off an intercept of length \(b\) on \(y\)-axis be \(x^2+y^2-\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0\). If the circle lies below \(x\)-axis, then the ordered pair \((2a,b^2)\) is equal to
questions.sol: Centre \((a,-r)\): \(\alpha=2a\), \(\beta=2r\), \(\gamma=a^2\), and \(b^2=4(r^2-a^2)=\beta^2-4\gamma\).

questions.q: Let the line \(x+y=1\) meet the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\). If the line perpendicular to \(AB\) and passing through the mid point of the chord \(AB\) intersects the circle at \(C\) and \(D\), then the area of the quadrilateral \(ADBC\) is equal to:
questions.sol: \(CD\) is a diameter (\(4\)) perpendicular to \(AB=2\sqrt{4-\frac12}=\sqrt{14}\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot\sqrt{14}\).

questions.q: Let a circle \(C\) pass through the points \((4,2)\) and \((0,2)\), and its centre lie on \(3x+2y+2=0\). Then the length of the chord, of the circle \(C\), whose mid-point is \((1,2)\), is :
questions.sol: The centre is \((2,-4)\) and \(r^2=40\). The midpoint is \(\sqrt{37}\) from the centre, so the half-chord is \(\sqrt3\).

questions.q: A square is inscribed in the circle \(x^2+y^2-10x-6y+30=0\). One side of this square is parallel to \(y=x+3\). If \((x_i,y_i)\) are the vertices of the square, then \(\sum(x_i^2+y_i^2)\) is equal to
questions.sol: The circle has centre \((5,3)\), radius \(2\); the diagonals are horizontal and vertical, so the vertices are \((7,3),(3,3),(5,5),(5,1)\).

questions.q: Let \(C\) be a circle with radius \(\sqrt{10}\) units and centre at the origin. Let the line \(x+y=2\) intersects the circle \(C\) at the points \(P\) and \(Q\). Let \(MN\) be a chord of \(C\) of length \(2\) units and slope \(-1\). Then, a distance (in units) between the chord \(PQ\) and the chord \(MN\) is
questions.sol: \(PQ\) is \(\sqrt2\) from \(O\) and \(MN\) is \(\sqrt{10-1}=3\) from \(O\).

questions.q: Let a circle \(C\) of radius \(1\) and closer to the origin be such that the lines passing through the point \((3,2)\) and parallel to the coordinate axes touch it. Then the shortest distance of the circle \(C\) from the point \((5,5)\) is :
questions.sol: The centre is \((2,1)\), at distance \(5\) from \((5,5)\).

questions.q: Let the circle \(C_1:x^2+y^2-2(x+y)+1=0\) and \(C_2\) be a circle having centre at \((-1,0)\) and radius \(2\). If the line of the common chord of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) intersects the \(y\)-axis at the point \(P\), then the square of the distance of \(P\) from the centre of \(C_1\) is :
questions.sol: \(C_2:x^2+y^2+2x-3=0\); the common chord is \(2x+y=2\), so \(P(0,2)\); the centre of \(C_1\) is \((1,1)\).

questions.q: Let \(ABCD\) and \(AEFG\) be squares of sides \(4\) and \(2\) units respectively. The point \(E\) is on the line segment \(AB\) and the point \(F\) is on the diagonal \(AC\). Then the radius \(r\) of the circle passing through the point \(F\) and touching the line segments \(BC\) and \(CD\) satisfies :
questions.sol: With \(A\) at the origin, \(C(4,4)\) and \(F(2,2)\); the centre is \((4-r,4-r)\), so \(2(2-r)^2=r^2\).

questions.q: Let the circles \(C_1:(x-\alpha)^2+(y-\beta)^2=r_1^2\) and \(C_2:(x-8)^2+\left(y-\dfrac{15}2\right)^2=r_2^2\) touch each other externally at the point \((6,6)\). If the point \((6,6)\) divides the line segment joining the centres of the circles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) internally in the ratio \(2:1\), then \((\alpha+\beta)+4(r_1^2+r_2^2)\) equals
questions.sol: \((6,6)=\tfrac{(\alpha,\beta)+2\left(8,\frac{15}2\right)}3\) gives \((\alpha,\beta)=(2,3)\); \(r_1=5\), \(r_2=\tfrac52\).

questions.q: If the image of the point \((-4,5)\) in the line \(x+2y=2\) lies on the circle \((x+4)^2+(y-3)^2=r^2\), then \(r\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The image is \(\left(-\tfrac{28}5,\tfrac95\right)\), at distance \(\sqrt{\tfrac{64+36}{25}}\) from \((-4,3)\).

questions.q: Let a circle passing through \((2,0)\) have its centre at the point \((h,k)\). Let \((x_c,y_c)\) be the point of intersection of the lines \(3x+5y=1\) and \((2+c)x+5c^2y=1\). If \(h=\displaystyle\lim_{c\to1}x_c\) and \(k=\displaystyle\lim_{c\to1}y_c\), then the equation of the circle is :
questions.sol: \(x_c=\tfrac{1+c}{2+3c}\to\tfrac25\) and \(y_c\to-\tfrac1{25}\). The circle \(x^2+y^2-\tfrac45x+\tfrac2{25}y+c_0=0\) through \((2,0)\) has \(c_0=-\tfrac{12}5\).

questions.q: Let \(C:x^2+y^2=4\) and \(C':x^2+y^2-4\lambda x+9=0\) be two circles. If the set of all values of \(\lambda\) so that the circles \(C\) and \(C'\) intersect at two distinct points, is \(R-[a,b]\), then the point \((8a+12,16b-20)\) lies on the curve :
questions.sol: With \(d=2|\lambda|\) and \(r'=\sqrt{d^2-9}\), two intersections need \(d-2<r'\), i.e. \(d>\tfrac{13}4\): \(|\lambda|>\tfrac{13}8\). The point is \((-1,6)\).

questions.q: Let the locus of the midpoints of the chords of the circle \(x^2+(y-1)^2=1\) drawn from the origin intersect the line \(x+y=1\) at \(P\) and \(Q\). Then, the length of \(PQ\) is :
questions.sol: The locus is \(x^2+y^2-y=0\); it meets \(x+y=1\) at \((0,1)\) and \(\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)\).

questions.q: Four distinct points \((2k,3k)\), \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\) and \((0,0)\) lie on a circle for \(k\) equal to :
If the circles \((x+1)^2+(y+2)^2=r^2\) and \(x^2+y^2-4x-4y+4=0\) intersect at exactly two distinct points, then
questions.sol: The centres \((-1,-2)\), \((2,2)\) are \(5\) apart and the second radius is \(2\): \(|r-2|<5<r+2\).

questions.q: If one of the diameters of the circle \(x^2+y^2-10x+4y+13=0\) is a chord of another circle \(C\), whose center is the point of intersection of the lines \(2x+3y=12\) and \(3x-2y=5\), then the radius of the circle \(C\) is :
questions.sol: The given circle has centre \((5,-2)\), radius \(4\); \(C\) has centre \((3,2)\), at distance \(\sqrt{20}\), so its radius is \(\sqrt{20+16}\).

questions.q: Let a variable line passing through the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2-16x-4y=0\), meet the positive co-ordinate axes at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Then the minimum value of \(OA+OB\), where \(O\) is the origin, is equal to
questions.sol: The line passes through \((8,2)\); the minimum of \(a+b\) with \(\tfrac8a+\tfrac2b=1\) is \((\sqrt8+\sqrt2)^2\).

questions.q: If the tangents at the point \(P\) and \(Q\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x+y=5\) meet at the point \(R\left(\dfrac94,2\right)\), then the area of the triangle \(PQR\) is
questions.sol: \(r=\tfrac52\) and the tangent length is \(L=\tfrac54\). Area \(=\dfrac{rL^3}{r^2+L^2}=\dfrac{\frac52\cdot\frac{125}{64}}{\frac{125}{16}}\).

questions.q: Let \(O\) be the origin and \(OP\) and \(OQ\) be the tangents to the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x+4y+8=0\) at the points \(P\) and \(Q\) on it. If the circumcircle of the triangle \(OPQ\) passes through the point \(\left(\alpha,\dfrac12\right)\), then a value of \(\alpha\) is
questions.sol: The circumcircle has diameter \(OC\), \(C(3,-2)\): \(x(x-3)+y(y+2)=0\). At \(y=\tfrac12\): \(\alpha^2-3\alpha+\tfrac54=0\).

questions.q: A line segment \(AB\) of length \(\lambda\) moves such that the points \(A\) and \(B\) remain on the periphery of a circle of radius \(\lambda\). Then the locus of the point, that divides the line segment \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:3\), is a circle of radius
questions.sol: The chord is at distance \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\lambda\) from the centre and the point is \(\tfrac\lambda{10}\) from its midpoint: \(OP^2=\tfrac34\lambda^2+\tfrac{\lambda^2}{100}\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) be the point \((1,2)\) and \(B\) be any point on the curve \(x^2+y^2=16\). If the centre of the locus of the point \(P\), which divides the line segment \(AB\) in the ratio \(3:2\) is the point \(C(\alpha,\beta)\), then the length of the line segment \(AC\) is
questions.sol: \(P=\tfrac{2A+3B}5\), so \(C=\tfrac25A=\left(\tfrac25,\tfrac45\right)\).

questions.q: Let the centre of a circle \(C\) be \((\alpha,\beta)\) and its radius \(r<8\). Let \(3x+4y=24\) and \(3x-4y=32\) be two tangents and \(4x+3y=1\) be a normal to \(C\). Then \((\alpha-\beta+r)\) is equal to
questions.sol: The centre lies on a bisector of the tangents (\(y=-1\) or \(x=\tfrac{28}3\)) and on the normal. \((1,-1)\) gives \(r=5\); the other choice gives \(r>8\).

questions.q: The number of common tangents, to the circles \(x^2+y^2-18x-15y+131=0\) and \(x^2+y^2-6x-6y-7=0\), is
questions.sol: Centres \(\left(9,\tfrac{15}2\right)\), \((3,3)\), radii \(\tfrac52\), \(5\); distance \(\tfrac{15}2=r_1+r_2\) (external contact).

questions.q: The area enclosed by the closed curve \(C\) given by the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{x+a}{y-2}=0\), \(y(1)=0\) is \(4\pi\). Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be the points of intersection of the curve \(C\) and the \(y\)-axis. If normals at \(P\) and \(Q\) on the curve \(C\) intersect \(x\)-axis at points \(R\) and \(S\) respectively, then the length of the line segment \(RS\) is
questions.sol: \(C\) is the circle \((x+a)^2+(y-2)^2=r^2\) with \(r=2\); \(y(1)=0\) gives \(a=-1\). \(P,Q=(0,2\pm\sqrt3)\), and the normals through \((1,2)\) meet the \(x\)-axis at \(\tfrac{2+\sqrt3}{\sqrt3}\) and \(\tfrac{\sqrt3-2}{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: The locus of the mid points of the chords of the circle \(C_1:(x-4)^2+(y-5)^2=4\) which subtend an angle \(\theta_i\) at the centre of the circle \(C_1\), is a circle of radius \(r_i\). If \(\theta_1=\dfrac\pi3\), \(\theta_3=\dfrac{2\pi}3\) and \(r_1^2=r_2^2+r_3^2\), then \(\theta_2\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(r_i=2\cos\tfrac{\theta_i}2\): \(3=4\cos^2\tfrac{\theta_2}2+1\).

questions.q: The points of intersection of the line \(ax+by=0\), \((a\ne b)\) and the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x=0\) are \(A(\alpha,0)\) and \(B(1,\beta)\). The image of the circle with \(AB\) as a diameter in the line \(x+y+2=0\) is
questions.sol: The line passes through \(O\), so \(A=O\) and \(B=(1,\pm1)\). With \(B(1,1)\) the circle has centre \(\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)\) and \(r^2=\tfrac12\); the image centre is \(\left(-\tfrac52,-\tfrac52\right)\).

questions.q: Let the tangents at the points \(A(4,-11)\) and \(B(8,-5)\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2-3x+10y-15=0\), intersect at the point \(C\). Then the radius of the circle, whose centre is \(C\) and the line joining \(A\) and \(B\) is its tangent, is equal to
questions.sol: The tangents \(5x-12y=152\) and \(x=8\) meet at \(C\left(8,-\tfrac{28}3\right)\); its distance from \(AB:3x-2y-34=0\) is \(\dfrac{26/3}{\sqrt{13}}\).

questions.q: Let \(y=x+2\), \(4y=3x+6\) and \(3y=4x+1\) be three tangent lines to the circle \((x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\). Then \(h+k\) is equal to
questions.sol: The triangle has vertices \((-2,0)\), \((5,7)\), \((2,3)\) with opposite sides \(5,5,7\sqrt2\). The incentre has \(h+k=\dfrac{5(-2)+5(12)+7\sqrt2(5)}{10+7\sqrt2}=5\).

questions.q: Let a circle \(C_1\) be obtained on rolling the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x-6y+11=0\) upwards \(4\) units on the tangent \(T\) to it at the point \((3,2)\). Let \(C_2\) be the image of \(C_1\) in \(T\). Let \(A\) and \(B\) be the centers of circles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) respectively, and \(M\) and \(N\) be respectively the feet of perpendiculars drawn from \(A\) and \(B\) on the \(x\)-axis. Then the area of the trapezium \(AMNB\) is :
questions.sol: Centre \((2,3)\), \(T:y=x-1\). \(A=(2+2\sqrt2,3+2\sqrt2)\) and its image \(B=(4+2\sqrt2,1+2\sqrt2)\). Area \(\tfrac12(4+4\sqrt2)\cdot2\).

questions.q: The set of all values of \(a^2\) for which the line \(x+y=0\) bisects two distinct chords drawn from a point \(P\left(\dfrac{1+a}2,\dfrac{1-a}2\right)\) on the circle \(2x^2+2y^2-(1+a)x-(1-a)y=0\), is equal to
questions.sol: A midpoint \(M(t,-t)\) of a chord through \(P\) satisfies \((M-\text{centre})\cdot(M-P)=0\), i.e. \(8t^2-6at+1+a^2=0\); two distinct \(t\) need \(a^2>8\).

questions.q: A point \(P\) moves so that the sum of squares of its distances from the points \((1,2)\) and \((-2,1)\) is \(14\). Let \(f(x,y)=0\) be the locus of \(P\), which intersects the \(x\)-axis at the points \(A\), \(B\) and the \(y\)-axis at the points \(C\), \(D\). Then the area of the quadrilateral \(ACBD\) is equal to
questions.sol: The locus is \(x^2+y^2+x-3y-2=0\): \(AB=3\) (roots \(1,-2\)) and \(CD=\sqrt{17}\), perpendicular diagonals. Area \(\tfrac12\cdot3\sqrt{17}\). (The book key prints (a).)

questions.q: Let the abscissae of the two points \(P\) and \(Q\) on a circle be the roots of \(x^2-4x-6=0\) and the ordinates of \(P\) and \(Q\) be the roots of \(y^2+2y-7=0\). If \(PQ\) is a diameter of the circle \(x^2+y^2+2ax+2by+c=0\), then the value of \((a+b-c)\) is
If the circle \(x^2+y^2-2gx+6y-19c=0\), \(g,c\in R\) passes through the point \((6,1)\) and its centre lies on the line \(x-2cy=8\), then the length of intercept made by the circle on \(x\)-axis is

A circle \(C_1\) passes through the origin \(O\) and has diameter \(4\) on the positive \(x\)-axis. The line \(y=2x\) gives a chord \(OA\) of a circle \(C_1\). Let \(C_2\) be the circle with \(OA\) as a diameter. If the tangent to \(C_2\) at the point \(A\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(P\) and \(y\)-axis at \(Q\), then \(QA:AP\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(A\left(\tfrac45,\tfrac85\right)\); the tangent (\(\perp OA\)) is \(y-\tfrac85=-\tfrac12\left(x-\tfrac45\right)\), giving \(P(4,0)\) and \(Q(0,2)\).

questions.q: For \(t\in(0,2\pi)\), if \(ABC\) is an equilateral triangle with vertices \(A(\sin t,-\cos t)\), \(B(\cos t,\sin t)\) and \(C(a,b)\) such that its orthocentre lies on a circle with centre \(\left(1,\dfrac13\right)\) then \((a^2-b^2)\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The orthocentre is the centroid \(\left(\tfrac{\sin t+\cos t+a}3,\tfrac{\sin t-\cos t+b}3\right)\), which runs on a circle centred \(\left(\tfrac a3,\tfrac b3\right)\). So \(a=3\), \(b=1\).

questions.q: Let \(C\) be the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2-x+2y=\dfrac{11}4\) and \(P\) be a point on the circle. A line passes through the point \(C\), makes an angle of \(\dfrac\pi4\) with the line \(CP\) and intersects the circle at the points \(Q\) and \(R\). Then the area of the triangle \(PQR\) (in unit\(^2\)) is
questions.sol: \(r=2\) and \(QR\) is a diameter, so \(\angle P=90^\circ\) with \(PQ=4\sin\tfrac\pi8\), \(PR=4\cos\tfrac\pi8\). Area \(8\sin\tfrac\pi8\cos\tfrac\pi8\).

questions.q: Let the tangents at two points \(A\) and \(B\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x+3=0\) meet at origin \(O(0,0)\). Then the area of the triangle \(OAB\) is :
questions.sol: \(r=1\), tangent length \(L=\sqrt3\); area \(=\dfrac{rL^3}{r^2+L^2}\).

questions.q: Let a line \(L\) pass through the point of intersection of the lines \(bx+10y-8=0\) and \(2x-3y=0\), \(b\in R-\left\{\dfrac43\right\}\). If the line \(L\) also passes through the point \((1,1)\) and touches the circle \(17(x^2+y^2)=16\), then the eccentricity of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}5+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) is :
Let \(x^2+y^2+Ax+By+C=0\) be a circle passing through \((0,6)\) and touching the parabola \(y=x^2\) at \((2,4)\). Then, \(A+C\) is equal to ______.

Let a circle \(C\) touch the lines \(L_1:4x-3y+K_1=0\) and \(L_2:4x-3y+K_2=0\), \(K_1,K_2\in R\). If a line passing through the centre of the circle \(C\) intersects \(L_1\) at \((-1,2)\) and \(L_2\) at \((3,-6)\), then the equation of the circle \(C\) is
questions.sol: The centre is the midpoint \((1,-2)\); \(K_1=10\), \(K_2=-30\), so the lines are \(8\) apart and \(r=4\).

questions.q: A circle touches both the \(y\)-axis and the line \(x+y=0\). Then the locus of its center is
questions.sol: \(|h|=\tfrac{|h+k|}{\sqrt2}\) gives \(h^2-2hk-k^2=0\).

questions.q: Let \(C\) be a circle passing through the points \(A(2,-1)\) and \(B(3,4)\). The line segment \(AB\) is not a diameter of \(C\). If \(r\) is the radius of \(C\) and its centre lies on the circle \((x-5)^2+(y-1)^2=\dfrac{13}2\), then \(r^2\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The centre lies on \(x+5y=10\) and on the given circle: \(y=\tfrac32\) (the midpoint, excluded) or \(y=\tfrac12\), \(x=\tfrac{15}2\).

questions.q: The set of values of \(k\), for which the circle \(C:4x^2+4y^2-12x+8y+k=0\) lies inside the fourth quadrant and the point \(\left(1,-\dfrac13\right)\) lies on or inside the circle \(C\), is
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(\tfrac32,-1\right)\), \(r^2=\tfrac{13-k}4<1\) gives \(k>9\); the point condition gives \(\tfrac k4\le\tfrac{23}9\).

questions.q: If the tangents drawn at the points \(O(0,0)\) and \(P(1+\sqrt5,2)\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-4y=0\) intersect at the point \(Q\), then the area of the triangle \(OPQ\) is equal to
questions.sol: The tangents are \(x+2y=0\) and \(x=1+\sqrt5\), meeting at \(Q\left(1+\sqrt5,-\tfrac{1+\sqrt5}2\right)\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{5+\sqrt5}2\cdot(1+\sqrt5)\).

questions.q: Let the tangent to the circle \(C_1:x^2+y^2=2\) at the point \(M(-1,1)\) intersect the circle \(C_2:(x-3)^2+(y-2)^2=5\), at two distinct points \(A\) and \(B\). If the tangents to \(C_2\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\) intersect at \(N\), then the area of the triangle \(ANB\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The tangent is \(y-x=2\), at distance \(\tfrac3{\sqrt2}\) from \((3,2)\): \(AB=\sqrt2\). \(N\) is at distance \(\tfrac{r^2}d=\tfrac{5\sqrt2}3\) from the centre, so \(\tfrac1{3\sqrt2}\) from \(AB\).

questions.q: Let a triangle \(ABC\) be inscribed in the circle \(x^2-\sqrt2(x+y)+y^2=0\) such that \(\angle BAC=\dfrac\pi2\). If the length of side \(AB\) is \(\sqrt2\), then the area of the \(\Delta ABC\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The radius is \(1\), so \(BC=2\), \(AC=\sqrt2\) and the area is \(1\), which is not among the options. The book marks this question bonus.

questions.q: A circle \(C\) touches the line \(x=2y\) at the point \((2,1)\) and intersects the circle \(C_1:x^2+y^2+2y-5=0\) at two points \(P\) and \(Q\) such that \(PQ\) is a diameter of \(C_1\). Then the diameter of \(C\) is

Let \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) be the radii of the largest and smallest circles, respectively, which pass through the point \((-4,1)\) and having their centres on the circumference of the circle \(x^2+y^2+2x+4y-4=0\). If \(\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}=a+b\sqrt2\), then \(a+b\) is equal to
questions.sol: The point is \(3\sqrt2\) from the centre and \(r=3\): \(\dfrac{3\sqrt2+3}{3\sqrt2-3}=3+2\sqrt2\).

questions.q: Let the circle \(S:36x^2+36y^2-108x+120y+C=0\) be such that it neither intersects nor touches the co-ordinate axes. If the point of intersection of the lines, \(x-2y=4\) and \(2x-y=5\) lies inside the circle \(S\), then
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(\tfrac32,-\tfrac53\right)\), \(r^2=\tfrac94+\tfrac{25}9-\tfrac C{36}<\tfrac94\) gives \(C>100\); \((2,-1)\) inside gives \(C<156\).

questions.q: Two tangents are drawn from the point \(P(-1,1)\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-6y+6=0\). If these tangents touch the circle at points \(A\) and \(B\), and if \(D\) is a point on the circle such that length of the segments \(AB\) and \(AD\) are equal, then the area of the triangle \(ABD\) is equal to
questions.sol: Centre \((1,3)\), \(r=2\), \(PC=2\sqrt2\), \(L=2\): \(AB=\tfrac{2rL}{PC}=2\sqrt2\), subtending \(90^\circ\) at the centre. So \(\angle B=\angle D=45^\circ\), \(\angle A=90^\circ\) and the area is \(\tfrac12(2\sqrt2)^2\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be two distinct points on a circle which has center at \(C(2,3)\) and which passes through origin \(O\). If \(OC\) is perpendicular to both the line segments \(CP\) and \(CQ\), then the set \(\{P,Q\}\) is equal to
