Consider a circle \(C\) which touches the \(y\)-axis at \((0,6)\) and cuts off an intercept \(6\sqrt5\) on the \(x\)-axis. Then the radius of the circle \(C\) is equal to

Let the lengths of intercepts on \(x\)-axis and \(y\)-axis made by the circle \(x^2+y^2+ax+2ay+c=0\), \((a<0)\) be \(2\sqrt2\) and \(2\sqrt5\), respectively. Then the shortest distance from origin to a tangent to this circle which is perpendicular to the line \(x+2y=0\), is equal to
questions.sol: \(\tfrac{a^2}4-c=2\), \(a^2-c=5\) give \(a=-2\), \(c=-1\): centre \((1,2)\), \(r=\sqrt6\). Tangents \(2x-y+k=0\) need \(\tfrac{|k|}{\sqrt5}=\sqrt6\), which is also their distance from \(O\).

questions.q:
Choose the incorrect statement about the two circles whose equations are given below :
\(x^2+y^2-10x-10y+41=0\) and \(x^2+y^2-16x-10y+80=0\)
opts: Both circles pass through the centre of each other.
Both circles' centres lie inside region of one another.
Distance between two centres is the average of radii of both the circles.
questions.sol: Centres \((5,5)\), \((8,5)\), both radii \(3\), distance \(3\): each centre lies on (not inside) the other circle.

questions.q: The line \(2x-y+1=0\) is a tangent to the circle at the point \((2,5)\) and the centre of the circle lies on \(x-2y=4\). Then, the radius of the circle is
questions.sol: The centre \((2+2t,5-t)\) on \(x-2y=4\) gives \(t=3\): centre \((8,2)\).

questions.q: Let the tangent to the circle \(x^2+y^2=25\) at the point \(R(3,4)\) meet \(x\)-axis and \(y\)-axis at points \(P\) and \(Q\), respectively. If \(r\) is the radius of the circle passing through the origin \(O\) and having centre at the incentre of the triangle \(OPQ\), then \(r^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(P\left(\tfrac{25}3,0\right)\), \(Q\left(0,\tfrac{25}4\right)\); the inradius is \(\tfrac{25}{12}\), so the incentre is \(\left(\tfrac{25}{12},\tfrac{25}{12}\right)\) and \(r^2=2\left(\tfrac{25}{12}\right)^2\).

questions.q: Two tangents are drawn from a point \(P\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-4y+4=0\), such that the angle between these tangents is \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}5\right)\), where \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}5\right)\in(0,\pi)\). If the centre of the circle is denoted by \(C\) and these tangents touch the circle at points \(A\) and \(B\), then the ratio of the areas of \(\Delta PAB\) and \(\Delta CAB\) is
questions.sol: \(r=1\), \(\tan\tfrac\theta2=\tfrac23\), so \(L=\tfrac32\). \([PAB]=\tfrac12L^2\sin\theta=\tfrac{27}{26}\) and \([CAB]=\tfrac12r^2\sin\theta=\tfrac{12}{26}\).

questions.q:
For the four circles \(M\), \(N\), \(O\) and \(P\), following four equations are given :
Circle \(M:x^2+y^2=1\)
Circle \(N:x^2+y^2-2x=0\)
Circle \(O:x^2+y^2-2x-2y+1=0\)
Circle \(P:x^2+y^2-2y=0\)
If the centre of circle \(M\) is joined with centre of the circle \(N\), further centre of circle \(N\) is joined with centre of circle \(O\), centre of circle \(O\) is joined with the centre of circle \(P\) and lastly, centre of circle \(P\) is joined with centre of circle \(M\), then these lines form the sides of a

Choose the correct statement about two circles whose equations are given below :
\(x^2+y^2-10x-10y+41=0\)
\(x^2+y^2-22x-10y+137=0\)
opts: circles have only one meeting point
questions.sol: Centres \((5,5)\), \((11,5)\), radii \(3,3\): the distance \(6\) equals \(r_1+r_2\).

questions.q: Let \(S_1:x^2+y^2=9\) and \(S_2:(x-2)^2+y^2=1\). Then the locus of centre of a variable circle \(S\) which touches \(S_1\) internally and \(S_2\) externally always passes through the points
questions.sol: The distances to \((0,0)\) and \((2,0)\) sum to \((3-r)+(1+r)=4\): the ellipse \(\tfrac{(x-1)^2}4+\tfrac{y^2}3=1\).

questions.q: In the circle given below, let \(OA=1\) unit, \(OB=13\) unit and \(PQ\perp OB\). Then, the area of the triangle \(PQB\) (in square units) is (In the figure, \(OB\) is a diameter of the circle, \(A\) lies on \(OB\), and the chord \(PQ\) passes through \(A\).)
questions.sol: \(PA^2=OA\cdot AB=12\), so \(PQ=4\sqrt3\) and the area is \(\tfrac12\cdot4\sqrt3\cdot12\).

questions.q: Let \(A(1,4)\) and \(B(1,-5)\) be two points. Let \(P\) be a point on the circle \((x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=1\) such that \((PA)^2+(PB)^2\) have maximum value, then the points \(P\), \(A\) and \(B\) lie on
questions.sol: \(PA^2+PB^2=2PM^2+\tfrac{AB^2}2\) with \(M\left(1,-\tfrac12\right)\); the farthest point is \(P(1,2)\), on the line \(x=1\).

questions.q: If the locus of the mid-point of the line segment from the point \((3,2)\) to a point on the circle, \(x^2+y^2=1\) is a circle of radius \(r\), then \(r\) is equal to
questions.sol: The midpoint is \(\tfrac{(3,2)+P}2\), a half-size copy of the circle.

questions.q: The circle passing through the intersection of the circles, \(x^2+y^2-6x=0\) and \(x^2+y^2-4y=0\), having its centre on the line, \(2x-3y+12=0\), also passes through the point
questions.sol: \(x^2+y^2-6x+\lambda(-6x+4y)=0\) has centre \((3+3\lambda,-2\lambda)\); the line gives \(\lambda=-\tfrac32\): \(x^2+y^2+3x-6y=0\).

questions.q: If the length of the chord of the circle, \(x^2+y^2=r^2\) \((r>0)\) along the line, \(y-2x=3\) is \(r\), then \(r^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: The distance \(\tfrac3{\sqrt5}\) equals \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}2r\).

questions.q: Let the tangents drawn from the origin to the circle, \(x^2+y^2-8x-4y+16=0\) touch it at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Then \((AB)^2\) is equal to

If a line, \(y=mx+c\) is a tangent to the circle, \((x-3)^2+y^2=1\) and it is perpendicular to a line \(L_1\), where \(L_1\) is the tangent to the circle, \(x^2+y^2=1\) at the point \(\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt2},\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)\); then
questions.sol: \(L_1\) has slope \(-1\), so \(m=1\); tangency: \(\tfrac{|3+c|}{\sqrt2}=1\).

questions.q: A circle touches the \(y\)-axis at the point \((0,4)\) and passes through the point \((2,0)\). Which of the following lines is not a tangent to this circle?
questions.sol: Centre \((5,4)\), \(r=5\); the line in (c) is at distance \(\tfrac{24}5\).

questions.q: The sum of the squares of the lengths of the chords intercepted on the circle, \(x^2+y^2=16\), by the lines, \(x+y=n\), \(n\in N\), where \(N\) is the set of all natural numbers, is
questions.sol: Chords exist for \(n=1,\dots,5\), each of squared length \(4\left(16-\tfrac{n^2}2\right)\).

questions.q: The tangent and the normal lines at the point \((\sqrt3,1)\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) and the \(x\)-axis form a triangle. The area of this triangle (in square units) is
questions.sol: The tangent meets the \(x\)-axis at \(\tfrac4{\sqrt3}\) and the normal passes through \(O\); the height is \(1\).

questions.q: If a tangent to the circle \(x^2+y^2=1\) intersects the coordinate axes at distinct points \(P\) and \(Q\), then the locus of the mid-point of \(PQ\) is
questions.sol: The midpoint is \(\left(\tfrac1{2\cos\theta},\tfrac1{2\sin\theta}\right)\).

questions.q: The common tangent to the circles \(x^2+y^2=4\) and \(x^2+y^2+6x+8y-24=0\) also passes through the point
questions.sol: The circles touch internally (\(d=5=7-2\)); the common tangent is the radical axis \(3x+4y=10\).

questions.q: A rectangle is inscribed in a circle with a diameter lying along the line \(3y=x+7\). If the two adjacent vertices of the rectangle are \((-8,5)\) and \((6,5)\), then the area of the rectangle (in sq. units) is
questions.sol: The centre is on \(x=-1\) and the line: \((-1,2)\). The other vertices are \((6,-1)\) and \((-8,-1)\): \(14\times6\).

questions.q: If the circles \(x^2+y^2+5Kx+2y+K=0\) and \(2(x^2+y^2)+2Kx+3y-1=0\) \((K\in R)\), intersect at the points \(P\) and \(Q\), then the line \(4x+5y-K=0\) passes through \(P\) and \(Q\), for
questions.sol: The common chord is \(8Kx+y+2K+1=0\); matching \(4x+5y-K=0\) needs \(K=\tfrac1{40}\) and \(K=-\tfrac5{11}\) simultaneously.

questions.q: The line \(x=y\) touches a circle at the point \((1,1)\). If the circle also passes through the point \((1,-3)\), then its radius is
The locus of the centres of the circles, which touch the circle, \(x^2+y^2=1\) externally, also touch the \(y\)-axis and lie in the first quadrant, is
If the angle of intersection at a point where the two circles with radii \(5\) cm and \(12\) cm intersect is \(90^\circ\), then the length (in cm) of their common chord is
questions.sol: \(d=13\) and the half-chord is \(\tfrac{5\cdot12}{13}\).

questions.q: A circle touching the \(x\)-axis at \((3,0)\) and making an intercept of length \(8\) on the \(y\)-axis passes through the point
questions.sol: Centre \((3,r)\) with \(r^2-9=16\): centre \((3,5)\), radius \(5\).

questions.q: Three circles of radii \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) \((a<b<c)\) touch each other externally. If they have \(x\)-axis as a common tangent, then
opts: \(\sqrt a,\sqrt b,\sqrt c\) are in A.P.
questions.sol: Touching circles on a line have contact points \(2\sqrt{rs}\) apart; the smallest lies between: \(2\sqrt{bc}=2\sqrt{ab}+2\sqrt{ac}\).

questions.q: If the circles \(x^2+y^2-16x-20y+164=r^2\) and \((x-4)^2+(y-7)^2=36\) intersect at two distinct points, then
If a circle \(C\) passing through the point \((4,0)\) touches the circle \(x^2+y^2+4x-6y=12\) externally at the point \((1,-1)\), then the radius of \(C\) is
questions.sol: The centre of \(C\) is \((1,-1)+r\left(\tfrac35,-\tfrac45\right)\); passing through \((4,0)\) gives \(10-2r=0\).

questions.q: If the area of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle, \(x^2+y^2+10x+12y+c=0\) is \(27\sqrt3\) sq. units, then \(c\) is equal to
A square is inscribed in the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x+8y-103=0\) with its sides parallel to the coordinate axes. Then the distance of the vertex of this square which is nearest to the origin is
questions.sol: Centre \((3,-4)\), \(r=8\sqrt2\); the vertices are \((3\pm8,-4\pm8)\), nearest \((-5,4)\).

questions.q: The straight line \(x+2y=1\) meets the coordinate axes at \(A\) and \(B\). A circle is drawn through \(A\), \(B\) and the origin. Then the sum of perpendicular distances from \(A\) and \(B\) on the tangent to the circle at the origin is
questions.sol: The circle is \(x^2+y^2-x-\tfrac y2=0\), with tangent \(2x+y=0\) at \(O\). Distances \(\tfrac2{\sqrt5}+\tfrac{1/2}{\sqrt5}\).

questions.q: Two circles with equal radii are intersecting at the points \((0,1)\) and \((0,-1)\). The tangent at the point \((0,1)\) to one of the circles passes through the centre of the other circle. Then the distance between the centres of these circle is
questions.sol: Centres \((\pm h,0)\); the radius to \((0,1)\) from \((h,0)\) is perpendicular to the segment to \((-h,0)\): \(h^2=1\).

questions.q: A circle cuts a chord of length \(4a\) on the \(x\)-axis and passes through a point on the \(y\)-axis, distant \(2b\) from the origin. Then the locus of the centre of this circle is

Let \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be the centres of the circles \(x^2+y^2-2x-2y-2=0\) and \(x^2+y^2-6x-6y+14=0\) respectively. If \(P\) and \(Q\) are the points of intersection of these circles, then the area (in sq. units) of the quadrilateral \(PC_1QC_2\) is
questions.sol: Both radii are \(2\) and \(C_1C_2=2\sqrt2\), so \(PQ=2\sqrt2\) too. Area \(\tfrac12(2\sqrt2)^2\).

questions.q: If a variable line, \(3x+4y-\lambda=0\) is such that the two circles \(x^2+y^2-2x-2y+1=0\) and \(x^2+y^2-18x-2y+78=0\) are on its opposite sides, then the set of all values of \(\lambda\) is the interval
questions.sol: Centres \((1,1)\) and \((9,1)\), radii \(1\) and \(2\): \(\lambda-7\ge5\) and \(31-\lambda\ge10\).

questions.q: If a circle of radius \(R\) passes through the origin \(O\) and intersects the coordinate axes at \(A\) and \(B\), then the locus of the foot of perpendicular from \(O\) on \(AB\) is
questions.sol: \(AB\) is a diameter: \(a^2+b^2=4R^2\). With foot \((h,k)\), \(a=\tfrac{h^2+k^2}h\) and \(b=\tfrac{h^2+k^2}k\).

questions.q: If the tangent at \((1,7)\) to the curve \(x^2=y-6\) touches the circle \(x^2+y^2+16x+12y+c=0\), then the value of \(c\) is
questions.sol: The tangent \(y=2x+5\) is at distance \(\sqrt5\) from \((-8,-6)\), so \(100-c=5\).

questions.q: Let the orthocentre and centroid of a triangle be \(A(-3,5)\) and \(B(3,3)\) respectively. If \(C\) is the circumcentre of this triangle, then the radius of the circle having line segment \(AC\) as diameter, is
questions.sol: \(C=\tfrac{3B-A}2=(6,2)\), and \(\tfrac{AC}2=\tfrac{\sqrt{90}}2\).

questions.q: The tangent to the circle \(C_1:x^2+y^2-2x-1=0\) at the point \((2,1)\) cuts off a chord of length \(4\) from a circle \(C_2\) whose centre is \((3,-2)\). The radius of \(C_2\) is

If a circle \(C\), whose radius is \(3\), touches externally the circle, \(x^2+y^2+2x-4y-4=0\) at the point \((2,2)\), then the length of the intercept cut by this circle \(C\), on the \(x\)-axis is equal to
questions.sol: The given circle has centre \((-1,2)\), radius \(3\), so \(C\) has centre \((5,2)\): intercept \(2\sqrt{9-4}\).

questions.q: A circle passes through the points \((2,3)\) and \((4,5)\). If its centre lies on the line, \(y-4x+3=0\), then its radius is equal to
questions.sol: The perpendicular bisector \(x+y=7\) meets \(y=4x-3\) at \((2,5)\).

questions.q: The radius of a circle, having minimum area, which touches the curve \(y=4-x^2\) and the lines, \(y=|x|\) is
questions.sol: Centre \((0,k)\): \(r=\tfrac k{\sqrt2}\) (to \(y=|x|\)) and \(r=4-k\) (touching the vertex from below). So \(r=\tfrac4{1+\sqrt2}\).

questions.q: If two parallel chords of a circle, having diameter \(4\) units, lie on the opposite sides of the centre and subtend angles \(\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac17\right)\) and \(\sec^{-1}(7)\) at the centre respectively, then the distance between these chords, is
questions.sol: Both angles equal \(\cos^{-1}\tfrac17\), so each chord is \(2\cos\tfrac\theta2=2\cdot\tfrac2{\sqrt7}\) from the centre.

questions.q: If a point \(P\) has co-ordinates \((0,-2)\) and \(Q\) is any point on the circle, \(x^2+y^2-5x-y+5=0\), then the maximum value of \((PQ)^2\) is
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(\tfrac52,\tfrac12\right)\), \(r^2=\tfrac32\), \(PC=\tfrac5{\sqrt2}\): \(\left(\tfrac5{\sqrt2}+\sqrt{\tfrac32}\right)^2\).

questions.q: If one of the diameters of the circle, given by the equation, \(x^2+y^2-4x+6y-12=0\), is a chord of a circle \(S\), whose centre is at \((-3,2)\), then the radius of \(S\) is
questions.sol: The given circle has centre \((2,-3)\), \(r=5\); \(r_S^2=50+25\).

questions.q: A circle passes through \((-2,4)\) and touches the \(y\)-axis at \((0,2)\). Which one of the following equations can represent a diameter of this circle?
questions.sol: Centre \((h,2)\) with \((h+2)^2+4=h^2\): \(h=-2\). Only (a) passes through \((-2,2)\).

questions.q: Equation of the tangent to the circle, at the point \((1,-1)\), whose centre is the point of intersection of the straight lines \(x-y=1\) and \(2x+y=3\) is
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(\tfrac43,\tfrac13\right)\); the radius direction is \((1,4)\).

questions.q: Locus of the image of the point \((2,3)\) in the line \((2x-3y+4)+k(x-2y+3)=0\), \(k\in R\), is a
questions.sol: All the lines pass through \((1,2)\), so every image is at distance \(\sqrt2\) from \((1,2)\).

questions.q: The number of common tangents to the circles \(x^2+y^2-4x-6y-12=0\) and \(x^2+y^2+6x+18y+26=0\), is
questions.sol: Centres \((2,3)\), \((-3,-9)\), radii \(5,8\), distance \(13\): external contact.

questions.q: If the incentre of an equilateral triangle is \((1,1)\) and the equation of its one side is \(3x+4y+3=0\), then the equation of the circumcircle of this triangle is
questions.sol: The inradius is \(\tfrac{10}5=2\), so \(R=4\).

questions.q: If \(y+3x=0\) is the equation of a chord of the circle, \(x^2+y^2-30x=0\), then the equation of the circle with this chord as diameter is
questions.sol: The chord joins \((0,0)\) and \((3,-9)\).

questions.q: If a circle passing through the point \((-1,0)\) touches \(y\)-axis at \((0,2)\), then the length of the chord of the circle along the \(x\)-axis is
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(-\tfrac52,2\right)\), \(r=\tfrac52\): chord \(2\sqrt{r^2-4}\).

questions.q: If the point \((1,4)\) lies inside the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x-10y+p=0\) and the circle does not touch or intersect the coordinate axes, then the set of all possible values of \(p\) is the interval
questions.sol: Centre \((3,5)\), \(r^2=34-p<9\); the point inside: \(p<29\).

questions.q: Let \(C\) be the circle with centre at \((1,1)\) and radius \(=1\). If \(T\) is the circle centred at \((0,y)\), passing through origin and touching the circle \(C\) externally, then the radius of \(T\) is equal to
If the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x-8y+(25-a^2)=0\) touches the axis of \(x\), then \(a\) equals
questions.sol: Centre \((3,4)\), radius \(|a|=4\).

questions.q: The circle passing through \((1,-2)\) and touching the axis of \(x\) at \((3,0)\) also passes through the point
The length of the diameter of the circle which touches the \(x\)-axis at the point \((1,0)\) and passes through the point \((2,3)\) is
The two circles \(x^2+y^2=ax\) and \(x^2+y^2=c^2\) \((c>0)\) touch each other if
questions.sol: The first circle has centre \(\left(\tfrac a2,0\right)\) and passes through \(O\); it touches the second internally when \(\tfrac{|a|}2=c-\tfrac{|a|}2\).

questions.q: The circle \(x^2+y^2=4x+8y+5\) intersects the line \(3x-4y=m\) at two distinct points if
If \(P\) and \(Q\) are the points of intersection of the circles \(x^2+y^2+3x+7y+2p-5=0\) and \(x^2+y^2+2x+2y-p^2=0\), then there is a circle passing through \(P\), \(Q\) and \((1,1)\) for
questions.sol: Such a circle fails to exist only if \((1,1)\) lies on the common chord \(x+5y+p^2+2p-5=0\), i.e. \((p+1)^2=0\).

questions.q: The point diametrically opposite to the point \(P(1,0)\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2+2x+4y-3=0\) is
questions.sol: The centre is \((-1,-2)\).

questions.q: Consider a family of circles which are passing through the point \((-1,1)\) and are tangent to \(x\)-axis. If \((h,k)\) are the coordinate of the centre of the circles, then the set of values of \(k\) is given by the interval
Let \(C\) be the circle with centre \((0,0)\) and radius \(3\) units. The equation of the locus of the mid points of chord of the circle \(C\) that subtend an angle of \(2\pi/3\) at its centre is
questions.sol: The midpoints are at distance \(3\cos\tfrac\pi3=\tfrac32\).

questions.q: If the lines \(3x-4y-7=0\) and \(2x-3y-5=0\) are two diameters of a circle of area \(49\pi\) square units, then the equation of the circle is
questions.sol: The centre is \((1,-1)\) and \(r=7\).

questions.q: If the pair of lines \(ax^2+2(a+b)xy+by^2=0\) lie along diameters of a circle and divide the circle into four sectors such that the area of one of the sectors is thrice the area of another sector, then
questions.sol: The angle between the lines is \(\tfrac\pi4\): \(\dfrac{2\sqrt{(a+b)^2-ab}}{|a+b|}=1\).

questions.q: If a circle passes through the point \((a,b)\) and cuts the circle \(x^2+y^2=p^2\) orthogonally, then the equation of the locus of its centre is
questions.sol: Orthogonality gives constant term \(p^2\); passing through \((a,b)\): \(a^2+b^2-2ah-2bk+p^2=0\).

questions.q: If the circles \(x^2+y^2+2ax+cy+a=0\) and \(x^2+y^2-3ax+dy-1=0\) intersect in two distinct points \(P\) and \(Q\), then the line \(5x+by-a=0\) passes through \(P\) and \(Q\) for
questions.sol: The common chord \(5ax+(c-d)y+a+1=0\) matches only if \(a=-\tfrac{a+1}a\), i.e. \(a^2+a+1=0\).

questions.q: The intercept on the line \(y=x\) by the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x=0\) is \(AB\). Equation of the circle on \(AB\) as a diameter is
If the lines \(2x+3y+1=0\) and \(3x-y-4=0\) lie along diameters of a circle of circumference \(10\pi\), then the equation of the circle is
questions.sol: The centre is \((1,-1)\) and \(r=5\).

questions.q: A variable circle passes through the fixed point \(A(p,q)\) and touches \(x\)-axis. The locus of the other end of the diameter through \(A\) is
questions.sol: With other end \((h,k)\), the radius \(\tfrac{|q+k|}2\) equals half the diameter: \((h-p)^2+(k-q)^2=(k+q)^2\).

questions.q: If a circle passes through the point \((a,b)\) and cuts the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) orthogonally, then the locus of its centre is
questions.sol: As in the general case with \(p^2=4\).

questions.q: The lines \(2x-3y=5\) and \(3x-4y=7\) are diameters of a circle having area as \(154\) sq. units. Then the equation of the circle is
questions.sol: The centre is \((1,-1)\) and \(\pi r^2=154\) gives \(r=7\).

questions.q: If the two circles \((x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=r^2\) and \(x^2+y^2-8x+2y+8=0\) intersect in two distinct points, then
questions.sol: The second circle has centre \((4,-1)\), radius \(3\); the centres are \(5\) apart: \(|r-3|<5<r+3\).

questions.q: If the chord \(y=mx+1\) of the circle \(x^2+y^2=1\) subtends an angle of measure \(45^\circ\) at the major segment of the circle, then value of \(m\) is
questions.sol: The chord subtends \(90^\circ\) at the centre, so its distance from \(O\) is \(\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\): \(\tfrac1{\sqrt{1+m^2}}=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\), \(m=\pm1\). (The book key prints (c).)

questions.q: The equation of a circle with origin as a centre and passing through equilateral triangle whose median is of length \(3a\) is
questions.sol: The circumradius is \(\tfrac23\) of the median.

questions.q: The centre of the circle passing through \((0,0)\) and \((1,0)\) and touching the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) is
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(\tfrac12,k\right)\) with \(r=\sqrt{\tfrac14+k^2}\) (it passes through \(O\)) and internal contact \(3-r=r\): \(r=\tfrac32\), \(k=\pm\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The centres of a set of circles, each of radius \(3\), lie on the circle \(x^2+y^2=25\). The locus of any point in the set is
questions.sol: Points within \(3\) of a point at distance \(5\) from \(O\) have \(2\le|P|\le8\).

questions.q: The absolute difference between the squares of the radii of the two circles passing through the point \((-9,4)\) and touching the lines \(x+y=3\) and \(x-y=3\), is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The centres lie on the bisector \(y=0\): \((h,0)\) with \(r=\tfrac{|h-3|}{\sqrt2}\). Then \((h+9)^2+16=\tfrac{(h-3)^2}2\) gives \(h=-5\) or \(-37\): \(r^2=32\) or \(800\).

questions.q: Let \(r\) be the radius of the circle, which touches \(x\)-axis at point \((a,0)\), \(a<0\) and the parabola \(y^2=9x\) at the point \((4,6)\). Then \(r\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The centre is on the normal at \((4,6)\): \((4+3t,6-4t)\) with radius \(5|t|\) equal to its height. \(t<0\) gives \(6-4t=-5t\), \(t=-6\): centre \((-14,30)\).

questions.q: Let the maximum and minimum values of \(\left(\sqrt{8x-x^2-12}-4\right)^2+(x-7)^2\), \(x\in\mathbf R\) be \(M\) and \(m\), respectively. Then, \(M^2-m^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: This is the squared distance from \((7,4)\) to a point on the upper semicircle \((x-4)^2+y^2=4\), \(y\ge0\). Minimum \((5-2)^2=9\); maximum at the end \((2,0)\): \(25+16=41\).

questions.q: Let the centre of a circle, passing through the points \((0,0)\), \((1,0)\) and touching the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\), be \((h,k)\). Then for all possible values of the coordinates of the centre \((h,k)\), \(4(h^2+k^2)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(h=\tfrac12\) and \(r=\sqrt{h^2+k^2}=3-r\), so \(h^2+k^2=\tfrac94\).

questions.q: Consider a circle \((x-\alpha)^2+(y-\beta)^2=50\), where \(\alpha,\beta>0\). If the circle touches the line \(y+x=0\) at the point \(P\), whose distance from the origin is \(4\sqrt2\), then \((\alpha+\beta)^2\) is equal to ______.

Equations of two diameters of a circle are \(2x-3y=5\) and \(3x-4y=7\). The line joining the points \(\left(-\dfrac{22}7,-4\right)\) and \(\left(-\dfrac17,3\right)\) intersects the circle at only one point \(P(\alpha,\beta)\). Then, \(17\beta-\alpha\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The centre is \((1,-1)\) and the tangent line is \(7x-3y+10=0\). The foot of the centre on it is \(P=(1,-1)-\tfrac{20}{58}(7,-3)=\left(-\tfrac{41}{29},\tfrac1{29}\right)\).

questions.q: Consider two circles \(C_1:x^2+y^2=25\) and \(C_2:(x-\alpha)^2+y^2=16\), where \(\alpha\in(5,9)\). Let the angle between the two radii (one to each circle) drawn from one of the intersection points of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be \(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{63}}8\right)\). If the length of common chord of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) is \(\beta\), then the value of \((\alpha\beta)^2\) equals ______.
questions.sol: The triangle of the centres and an intersection point has sides \(5,4,\alpha\) and area \(\tfrac12\cdot20\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt{63}}8\). The half-chord is \(\tfrac{2\,\text{Area}}\alpha\), so \(\alpha\beta=4\,\text{Area}=5\sqrt{63}\).

questions.q: Let the point \((p,p+1)\) lie inside the region \(E=\left\{(x,y):3-x\le y\le\sqrt{9-x^2},0\le x\le3\right\}\). If the set of all values of \(p\) is the interval \((a,b)\), then \(b^2+b-a^2\) is equal to ______.

A circle passing through the point \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) in the first quadrant touches the two coordinate axes at the points \(A\) and \(B\). The point \(P\) is above the line \(AB\). The point \(Q\) on the line segment \(AB\) is the foot of perpendicular from \(P\) on \(AB\). If \(PQ\) is equal to \(11\) units, then the value of \(\alpha\beta\) is ______.
questions.sol: Centre \((r,r)\), \(AB:x+y=r\), so \(\alpha+\beta=r+11\sqrt2\). From the circle, \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=2r(\alpha+\beta)-r^2\), hence \(\alpha\beta=\tfrac{(\alpha+\beta-r)^2}2=121\).

questions.q: Consider a circle \(C_1:x^2+y^2-4x-2y=\alpha-5\). Let its mirror image in the line \(y=2x+1\) be another circle \(C_2:5x^2+5y^2-10fx-10gy+36=0\). Let \(r\) be the radius of \(C_2\). Then \(\alpha+r\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The image of \((2,1)\) is \(\left(-\tfrac65,\tfrac{13}5\right)=(f,g)\), so \(r^2=f^2+g^2-\tfrac{36}5=1\). Also \(r^2=\alpha\) for \(C_1\).

questions.q: Two circles in the first quadrant of radii \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) touch the coordinate axes. Each of them cuts off an intercept of \(2\) units with the line \(x+y=2\). Then \(r_1^2+r_2^2-r_1r_2\) is equal to ______.

Points \(P(-3,2)\), \(Q(9,10)\) and \(R(\alpha,4)\) lie on a circle \(C\) with \(PR\) as its diameter. The tangents to \(C\) at the points \(Q\) and \(R\) intersect at the point \(S\). If \(S\) lies on the line \(2x-ky=1\), then \(k\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(\angle PQR=90^\circ\) gives \(\alpha=13\); centre \((5,3)\), \(r^2=65\). The tangents \(4x+7y=106\) and \(8x+y=108\) meet at \(S\left(\tfrac{25}2,8\right)\).

questions.q: A circle with centre \((2,3)\) and radius \(4\) intersects the line \(x+y=3\) at the points \(P\) and \(Q\). If the tangents at \(P\) and \(Q\) intersect at the point \(S(\alpha,\beta)\), then \(4\alpha-7\beta\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(x+y=3\) is the polar of \(S\): \((\alpha-2)(x-2)+(\beta-3)(y-3)=16\). Matching gives \(\alpha-2=\beta-3=-8\).

questions.q: Let \(P(a_1,b_1)\) and \(Q(a_2,b_2)\) be two distinct points on a circle with center \(C(\sqrt2,\sqrt3)\). Let \(O\) be the origin and \(OC\) be perpendicular to both \(CP\) and \(CQ\). If the area of the triangle \(OCP\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{35}}2\), then \(a_1^2+a_2^2+b_1^2+b_2^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12\sqrt5\,r=\tfrac{\sqrt{35}}2\) gives \(r=\sqrt7\), and \(P,Q=C\pm\sqrt7\,u\) with \(u\perp OC\): \(|P|^2+|Q|^2=2(5+7)\).

questions.q: If the circles \(x^2+y^2+6x+8y+16=0\) and \(x^2+y^2+2(3-\sqrt3)x+2(4-\sqrt6)y=k+6\sqrt3+8\sqrt6\), \(k>0\), touch internally at the point \(P(\alpha,\beta)\), then \((\alpha+\sqrt3)^2+(\beta+\sqrt6)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The centres \((-3,-4)\) and \((\sqrt3-3,\sqrt6-4)\) are \(3\) apart; \(r_1=3\), \(r_2^2=34+k\). Internal contact needs \(r_2=6\). \(P\) lies on the line of centres beyond \(C_1\): \(P=(-3-\sqrt3,-4-\sqrt6)\).

questions.q: Let the mirror image of a circle \(c_1:x^2+y^2-2x-6y+\alpha=0\) in line \(y=x+1\) be \(c_2:5x^2+5y^2+10gx+10fy+38=0\). If \(r\) is the radius of circle \(c_2\), then \(\alpha+6r^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The image of \((1,3)\) is \((2,2)\), so \(r^2=8-\tfrac{38}5=\tfrac25\). Also \(r^2=10-\alpha\), so \(\alpha=\tfrac{48}5\).

questions.q: Let \(AB\) be a chord of length \(12\) of the circle \((x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=\dfrac{169}4\). If tangents drawn to the circle at points \(A\) and \(B\) intersect at the point \(P\), then five times the distance of point \(P\) from chord \(AB\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The chord is \(d=\tfrac52\) from the centre and \(P\) is \(\tfrac{r^2}d=\tfrac{169}{10}\) from the centre, so \(\tfrac{72}5\) from \(AB\).

questions.q: Let a circle \(C:(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\), \(k>0\), touch the \(x\)-axis at \((1,0)\). If the line \(x+y=0\) intersects the circle \(C\) at \(P\) and \(Q\) such that the length of the chord \(PQ\) is \(2\), then the value of \(h+k+r\) is equal to ______.

Let the abscissae of the two points \(P\) and \(Q\) be the roots of \(2x^2-rx+p=0\) and the ordinates of \(P\) and \(Q\) be the roots of \(x^2-sx-q=0\). If the equation of the circle described on \(PQ\) as diameter is \(2(x^2+y^2)-11x-14y-22=0\), then \(2r+s-2q+p\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The circle is \(2\left(x^2-\tfrac r2x+\tfrac p2\right)+2(y^2-sy-q)=0\): \(r=11\), \(s=7\), \(p-2q=-22\).

questions.q: A rectangle \(R\) with end points of one of its sides as \((1,2)\) and \((3,6)\) is inscribed in a circle. If the equation of a diameter of the circle is \(2x-y+4=0\), then the area of \(R\) is ______.
questions.sol: The centre lies on the diameter and on the perpendicular bisector of the side: \(\left(\tfrac25,\tfrac{24}5\right)\). The adjacent side runs from \((3,6)\) to the reflection of \((1,2)\), \(\left(-\tfrac15,\tfrac{38}5\right)\), of length \(\tfrac8{\sqrt5}\). Area \(2\sqrt5\cdot\tfrac8{\sqrt5}\).

questions.q: Let a circle \(C\) of radius \(5\) lie below the \(x\)-axis. The line \(L_1:4x+3y+2=0\) passes through the centre \(P\) of the circle \(C\) and intersects the line \(L_2:3x-4y-11=0\) at \(Q\). The line \(L_2\) touches \(C\) at the point \(Q\). Then the distance of \(P\) from the line \(5x-12y+51=0\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(P\left(t,\tfrac{-2-4t}3\right)\) at distance \(5\) from \(L_2\): \(|25t-25|=75\), and below the axis \(t=4\): \(P(4,-6)\). Distance \(\tfrac{143}{13}\).

questions.q: Let the lines \(y+2x=\sqrt{11}+7\sqrt7\) and \(2y+x=2\sqrt{11}+6\sqrt7\) be normal to a circle \(C:(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\). If the line \(\sqrt{11}y-3x=\dfrac{5\sqrt{77}}3+11\) is tangent to the circle \(C\), then the value of \((5h-8k)^2+5r^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The normals meet at the centre \(\left(\tfrac{8\sqrt7}3,\sqrt{11}+\tfrac{5\sqrt7}3\right)\). The distance to the tangent gives \(r^2=\tfrac{64\cdot7}{20}\), and \(5h-8k=-8\sqrt{11}\). Value \(704+112\).

questions.q: If one of the diameters of the circle \(x^2+y^2-2\sqrt2x-6\sqrt2y+14=0\) is a chord of the circle \((x-2\sqrt2)^2+(y-2\sqrt2)^2=r^2\), then the value of \(r^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The first circle has centre \((\sqrt2,3\sqrt2)\) and radius\(^2\) \(6\); its centre is \(2\) from \((2\sqrt2,2\sqrt2)\). \(r^2=4+6\).

questions.q: The locus of a point, which moves such that the sum of squares of its distances from the points \((0,0)\), \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\), \((1,1)\) is \(18\) units, is a circle of diameter \(d\). Then \(d^2\) is equal to ______.
Let the equation \(x^2+y^2+px+(1-p)y+5=0\) represent circles of varying radius \(r\in(0,5]\). Then the number of elements in the set \(S=\{q:q=p^2\text{ and }q\text{ is an integer}\}\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(r^2=\tfrac{2p^2-2p-19}4\in(0,25]\) gives \(p\in\left[\tfrac{1-\sqrt{239}}2,\tfrac{1-\sqrt{39}}2\right)\cup\left(\tfrac{1+\sqrt{39}}2,\tfrac{1+\sqrt{239}}2\right]\). Then \(p^2\) fills \((6.88,67.73]\), containing the integers \(7\) to \(67\).

questions.q: Two circles each of radius \(5\) units touch each other at the point \((1,2)\). If the equation of their common tangent is \(4x+3y=10\), and \(C_1(\alpha,\beta)\) and \(C_2(\gamma,\delta)\), \(C_1\ne C_2\) are their centres, then \(|(\alpha+\beta)(\gamma+\delta)|\) is equal to ______.

If the variable line \(3x+4y=\alpha\) lies between the two circles \((x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=1\) and \((x-9)^2+(y-1)^2=4\), without intercepting a chord on either circle, then the sum of all the integral values of \(\alpha\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(\alpha-7\ge5\) and \(31-\alpha\ge10\), so \(\alpha\in[12,21]\).

questions.q: Let \(B\) be the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x+4y+1=0\). Let the tangents at two points \(P\) and \(Q\) on the circle intersect at the point \(A(3,1)\). Then \(8\cdot\left(\dfrac{\text{area }\Delta APQ}{\text{area }\Delta BPQ}\right)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(B(1,-2)\), \(r=2\), \(AB=\sqrt{13}\). \(B\) is \(\tfrac{r^2}{AB}=\tfrac4{\sqrt{13}}\) from \(PQ\) and \(A\) is \(\tfrac9{\sqrt{13}}\) from it.

questions.q: The minimum distance between any two points \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) while considering point \(P_1\) on one circle and point \(P_2\) on the other circle for the given circles' equations \(x^2+y^2-10x-10y+41=0\) and \(x^2+y^2-24x-10y+160=0\) is ______.
If one of the diameters of the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-6y+6=0\) is a chord of another circle '\(C\)', whose centre is at \((2,1)\), then its radius is ______.
questions.sol: Centre \((1,3)\), radius \(2\), at distance \(\sqrt5\) from \((2,1)\): \(r^2=5+4\).

questions.q: If the area of the triangle formed by the positive \(x\)-axis, the normal and the tangent to the circle \((x-2)^2+(y-3)^2=25\) at the point \((5,7)\) is \(A\), then \(24A\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The normal (through \((2,3)\)) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(-\tfrac14\) and the tangent (slope \(-\tfrac34\)) at \(\tfrac{43}3\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{175}{12}\cdot7\).

questions.q: Let a point \(P\) be such that its distance from the point \((5,0)\) is thrice the distance of \(P\) from the point \((-5,0)\). If the locus of the point \(P\) is a circle of radius \(r\), then \(4r^2\) is equal to ______.

Let the normals at all the points on a given curve pass through a fixed point \((a,b)\). If the curve passes through \((3,-3)\) and \((4,-2\sqrt2)\), and given that \(a-2\sqrt2b=3\), then \((a^2+b^2+ab)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The curve is a circle centred \((a,b)\). Equal distances give \(2a+(6-4\sqrt2)b=6\); with \(a=3+2\sqrt2b\) this forces \(b=0\), \(a=3\).

questions.q: The number of integral values of \(k\) for which the line, \(3x+4y=k\) intersects the circle, \(x^2+y^2-2x-4y+4=0\) at two distinct points is ______.
The diameter of the circle, whose centre lies on the line \(x+y=2\) in the first quadrant and which touches both the lines \(x=3\) and \(y=2\), is ______.
questions.sol: Centre \((h,2-h)\): \(|3-h|=|h|\), so \(h=\tfrac32\) and \(r=\tfrac32\).

questions.q: Let \(PQ\) be a diameter of the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\). If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the lengths of the perpendiculars from \(P\) and \(Q\) on the straight line, \(x+y=2\) respectively, then the maximum value of \(\alpha\beta\) is ______.
questions.sol: With \(u=3(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)\in[-3\sqrt2,3\sqrt2]\): \(\alpha\beta=\tfrac{|u-2||u+2|}2=\tfrac{|u^2-4|}2\le\tfrac{14}2\).

questions.q: If the curves, \(x^2-6x+y^2+8=0\) and \(x^2-8y+y^2+16-k=0\), \((k>0)\) touch each other at a point, then the largest value of \(k\) is ______.

Let the focal chord \(PQ\) of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) make an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the positive \(x\)-axis, where \(P\) lies in the first quadrant. If the circle, whose one diameter is \(PS\), \(S\) being the focus of the parabola, touches the \(y\)-axis at the point \((0,\alpha)\), then \(5\alpha^2\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(P(t^2,2t)\) with \(\tfrac{2t}{t^2-1}=\sqrt3\): \(t=\sqrt3\), \(P(3,2\sqrt3)\). The circle on \(PS\) has centre \((2,\sqrt3)\) and radius \(2\), touching the \(y\)-axis at \((0,\sqrt3)\).

questions.q: Let the point \(P\) of the focal chord \(PQ\) of the parabola \(y^2=16x\) be \((1,-4)\). If the focus of the parabola divides the chord \(PQ\) in the ratio \(m:n\), \(\gcd(m,n)=1\), then \(m^2+n^2\) is equal to :
The radius of the smallest circle which touches the parabolas \(y=x^2+2\) and \(x=y^2+2\) is
questions.sol: The parabolas are mirror images in \(y=x\); the least distance from \(y=x^2+2\) to \(y=x\) is \(\tfrac{7/4}{\sqrt2}\) (at \(x=\tfrac12\)), which is the radius.

questions.q: The axis of a parabola is the line \(y=x\) and its vertex and focus are in the first quadrant at distances \(\sqrt2\) and \(2\sqrt2\) units from the origin, respectively. If the point \((1,k)\) lies on the parabola, then a possible value of \(k\) is :
Let \(P\) be the parabola, whose focus is \((-2,1)\) and directrix is \(2x+y+2=0\). Then the sum of the ordinates of the points on \(P\), whose abscissa is \(-2\), is

Let the parabola \(y=x^2+px-3\), meet the coordinate axes at the points \(P\), \(Q\) and \(R\). If the circle \(C\) with centre at \((-1,-1)\) passes through the points \(P\), \(Q\) and \(R\), then the area of \(\Delta PQR\) is :
questions.sol: The \(x\)-intercepts are symmetric about \(x=-1\), so \(p=2\): roots \(1,-3\); \(R(0,-3)\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot3\).

questions.q: Let \(P(4,4\sqrt3)\) be a point on the parabola \(y^2=4ax\) and \(PQ\) be a focal chord of the parabola. If \(M\) and \(N\) are the foot of perpendiculars drawn from \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively on the directrix of the parabola, then the area of the quadrilateral \(PQMN\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(a=3\), \(P\) at \(t=\tfrac2{\sqrt3}\), \(Q\) at \(-\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\): \(Q\left(\tfrac94,-3\sqrt3\right)\). The trapezium has parallel sides \(PM=7\), \(QN=\tfrac{21}4\) and height \(7\sqrt3\).

questions.q: If the line \(3x-2y+12=0\) intersects the parabola \(4y=3x^2\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\), then at the vertex of the parabola, the line segment \(AB\) subtends an angle equal to
questions.sol: \(A(4,12)\), \(B(-2,3)\); \(OA\cdot OB>0\) and \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{3+\frac32}{\left|1-\frac92\right|}\).

questions.q: Let the shortest distance from \((a,0)\), \(a>0\), to the parabola \(y^2=4x\) be \(4\). Then the equation of the circle passing through the point \((a,0)\) and the focus of the parabola, and having its centre on the axis of the parabola is:
questions.sol: For \(a>2\) the squared distance \((x-a)^2+4x\) is least at \(x=a-2\), giving \(4a-4=16\), so \(a=5\) (for \(a\le2\) the distance would be \(a<4\)). The circle on the segment from \((1,0)\) to \((5,0)\) as diameter is \(x^2+y^2-6x+5=0\).

questions.q: If the equation of the parabola with vertex \(V\left(\dfrac32,3\right)\) and the directrix \(x+2y=0\) is \(\alpha x^2+\beta y^2-\gamma xy-30x-60y+225=0\), then \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The focus is \(V\) shifted by its distance from the directrix along the normal: \((3,6)\). \((x-3)^2+(y-6)^2=\tfrac{(x+2y)^2}5\) gives \(4x^2+y^2-4xy-30x-60y+225=0\).

questions.q: Let \(ABCD\) be a trapezium whose vertices lie on the parabola \(y^2=4x\). Let the sides \(AD\) and \(BC\) of the trapezium be parallel to \(y\)-axis. If the diagonal \(AC\) is of length \(\dfrac{25}4\) and it passes through the point \((1,0)\), then the area of \(ABCD\) is
questions.sol: \(AC\) is a focal chord: \(\left(t+\tfrac1t\right)^2=\tfrac{25}4\), \(t=2\). \(A(4,4)\), \(C\left(\tfrac14,-1\right)\), \(D(4,-4)\), \(B\left(\tfrac14,1\right)\). Area \(\tfrac{8+2}2\cdot\tfrac{15}4\).

questions.q: Two parabolas have the same focus \((4,3)\) and their directrices are the \(x\)-axis and the \(y\)-axis, respectively. If these parabolas intersects at the points \(A\) and \(B\), then \((AB)^2\) is equal to :
questions.sol: Intersections satisfy \(|x|=|y|\). On \(y=x\): \((x-4)^2+(x-3)^2=x^2\) gives \(x=7\pm2\sqrt6\); \(y=-x\) gives no real point. \(AB^2=2(4\sqrt6)^2\).

questions.q: Let \(PQ\) be a chord of the parabola \(y^2=12x\) and the midpoint of \(PQ\) be at \((4,1)\). Then, which of the following point lies on the line passing through the points \(P\) and \(Q\)?
Let \(C\) be the circle of minimum area touching the parabola \(y=6-x^2\) and the lines \(y=\sqrt3|x|\). Then, which one of the following points lies on the circle \(C\)?
questions.sol: The centre is \((0,k)\) with \(r=\tfrac k2\). The circle cannot touch at the vertex (its radius would exceed the vertex's radius of curvature \(\tfrac12\)), so it touches where the squared distance \(u+(6-k-u)^2\) (\(u=x^2\)) is least: \(r^2=6-k-\tfrac14\). This gives \(k=3\sqrt3-2\), and none of the listed points lies on the circle. The book marks this question as having no correct option.

questions.q: If the shortest distance of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) from the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x-16y+64=0\) is \(d\), then \(d^2\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The normal \(y=-tx+2t+t^3\) through \((2,8)\) gives \(t=2\): the nearest point is \((4,4)\).

questions.q: Let \(R\) be the focus of the parabola \(y^2=20x\) and the line \(y=mx+c\) intersect the parabola at two points \(P\) and \(Q\). Let the point \(G(10,10)\) be the centroid of the triangle \(PQR\). If \(c-m=6\), then \((PQ)^2\) is

Let \(A(0,1)\), \(B(1,1)\) and \(C(1,0)\) be the mid-points of the sides of a triangle with incentre at the point \(D\). If the focus of the parabola \(y^2=4ax\) passing through \(D\) is \((\alpha+\beta\sqrt2,0)\), where \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are rational numbers, then \(\dfrac\alpha{\beta^2}\) is equal to
questions.sol: The triangle is \((0,0),(2,0),(0,2)\) with incentre \((2-\sqrt2,2-\sqrt2)\). So \(4a=2-\sqrt2\) and the focus is \(\tfrac12-\tfrac{\sqrt2}4\).

questions.q: Let \(PQ\) be a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=36x\) of length \(100\), making an acute angle with the positive \(x\)-axis. Let the ordinate of \(P\) be positive and \(M\) be the point on the line segment \(PQ\) such that \(PM:MQ=3:1\). Then which of the following points does NOT lie on the line passing through \(M\) and perpendicular to the line \(PQ\)?
questions.sol: \(9\left(t+\tfrac1t\right)^2=100\) with positive slope gives \(t=3\): \(P(81,54)\), \(Q(1,-6)\), \(M=\tfrac{P+3Q}4=(21,9)\). The line is \(4x+3y=111\).

questions.q: Let a tangent to the curve \(y^2=24x\) meet the curve \(xy=2\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Then the mid points of such line segments \(AB\) lie on a parabola with the
questions.sol: The tangent \(y=mx+\tfrac6m\) meets \(xy=2\) where \(mx^2+\tfrac6mx-2=0\), so the midpoint is \(\left(-\tfrac3{m^2},\tfrac3m\right)\): the locus is \(y^2=-3x\).

questions.q: The equations of the sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) of a triangle \(ABC\) are \((\lambda+1)x+\lambda y=4\) and \(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y+\lambda=0\) respectively. Its vertex \(A\) is on the \(y\)-axis and its orthocentre is \((1,2)\). The length of the tangent from the point \(C\) to the part of the parabola \(y^2=6x\) in the first quadrant is
questions.sol: \(A\) on the \(y\)-axis forces \(\lambda=2\): \(AB:3x+2y=4\), \(AC:y=2x+2\). \(CH\perp AB\) gives \(C\left(-\tfrac12,1\right)\). The tangents \(y=mx+\tfrac3{2m}\) through \(C\) have \(m=1\) or \(-3\); \(m=1\) touches at \(\left(\tfrac32,3\right)\), at distance \(2\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The equations of two sides of a variable triangle are \(x=0\) and \(y=3\), and its third side is a tangent to the parabola \(y^2=6x\). The locus of its circumcentre is
questions.sol: The triangle is right-angled at \((0,3)\), so the circumcentre is the midpoint of the other two vertices \(\left(0,\tfrac3{2m}\right)\) and \(\left(\tfrac{3-3/(2m)}m,3\right)\). Eliminating \(m\) gives \(4k^2-18k+3h+18=0\).

questions.q: If the tangent at a point \(P\) on the parabola \(y^2=3x\) is parallel to the line \(x+2y=1\) and the tangents at the points \(Q\) and \(R\) on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}1=1\) are perpendicular to the line \(x-y=2\), then the area of the triangle \(PQR\) is
questions.sol: \(P=(3,-3)\). The tangents \(y=-x\pm\sqrt5\) touch at \(\pm\left(\tfrac4{\sqrt5},\tfrac1{\sqrt5}\right)\). Area \(=|x_Py_Q-y_Px_Q|=\tfrac{15}{\sqrt5}\).

questions.q: If \(P(h,k)\) be a point on the parabola \(x=4y^2\), which is nearest to the point \(Q(0,33)\), then the distance of \(P\) from the directrix of the parabola \(y^2=4(x+y)\) is equal to
The parabolas : \(ax^2+2bx+cy=0\) and \(dx^2+2ex+fy=0\) intersect on the line \(y=1\). If \(a,b,c,d,e,f\) are positive real numbers and \(a,b,c\) are in G.P., then
opts: \(\dfrac da,\dfrac eb,\dfrac fc\) are in G.P.
\(\dfrac da,\dfrac eb,\dfrac fc\) are in A.P.
questions.sol: At \(y=1\), \(ax^2+2bx+c=0\) has the double root \(-\tfrac ba\) (since \(b^2=ac\)). Substituting into the second: \(\tfrac da+\tfrac fc=\tfrac{2e}b\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) be a point on the \(x\)-axis. Common tangents are drawn from \(A\) to the curves \(x^2+y^2=8\) and \(y^2=16x\). If one of these tangents touches the two curves at \(Q\) and \(R\), then \((QR)^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac4m\) at distance \(\sqrt8\) from \(O\) gives \(m^2=1\). For \(y=x+4\): \(Q(-2,2)\) and \(R(4,8)\).

questions.q: Let \(y=f(x)\) represent a parabola with focus \(\left(-\dfrac12,0\right)\) and directrix \(y=-\dfrac12\). Then \(S=\left\{x\in R:\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{f(x)}\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{f(x)+1}\right)=\dfrac\pi2\right\}\) :
questions.sol: \(\left(x+\tfrac12\right)^2+y^2=\left(y+\tfrac12\right)^2\) gives \(f(x)=x^2+x\). The equation needs \(f\ge0\) and \(f+1\le1\), so \(f=0\), which holds (and checks) at \(x=0\) and \(x=-1\).

questions.q: Let the locus of the centre \((\alpha,\beta)\), \(\beta>0\), of the circle which touches the circle \(x^2+(y-1)^2=1\) externally and also touches the \(x\)-axis be \(L\). Then the area bounded by \(L\) and the line \(y=4\) is :
questions.sol: \(\alpha^2+(\beta-1)^2=(\beta+1)^2\) gives \(L:x^2=4y\). Area \(2\displaystyle\int_0^4\left(4-\tfrac{x^2}4\right)dx\).

questions.q: The tangents at the points \(A(1,3)\) and \(B(1,-1)\) on the parabola \(y^2-2x-2y=1\) meet at the point \(P\). Then the area (in unit\(^2\)) of the triangle \(PAB\) is :
questions.sol: The tangents \(2y-x=5\) and \(2y+x=-1\) meet at \(P(-3,1)\); \(AB=4\) at distance \(4\) from \(P\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be any points on the curves \((x-1)^2+(y+1)^2=1\) and \(y=x^2\), respectively. The distance between \(P\) and \(Q\) is minimum for some value of the abscissa of \(P\) in the interval
questions.sol: The nearest point \(Q\) of the parabola to the centre \((1,-1)\) satisfies \(2x^3+3x-1=0\), \(x\approx0.32\); \(P\) lies on the segment from the centre towards \(Q\), with abscissa \(\approx0.47\).

questions.q: The equation of a common tangent to the parabolas \(y=x^2\) and \(y=-(x-2)^2\) is
questions.sol: Tangents to \(y=x^2\) are \(y=mx-\tfrac{m^2}4\); tangency to the second needs \((m-4)^2=16-m^2\), so \(m=4\) (or \(0\)).

questions.q: Let \(P(a,b)\) be a point on the parabola \(y^2=8x\) such that the tangent at \(P\) passes through the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2-10x-14y+65=0\). Let \(A\) be the product of all possible values of \(a\) and \(B\) be the product of all possible values of \(b\). Then the value of \(A+B\) is equal to
If the length of the latus rectum of a parabola, whose focus is \((a,a)\) and the tangent at its vertex is \(x+y=a\), is \(16\), then \(|a|\) is equal to
questions.sol: The focus is \(\tfrac{|a|}{\sqrt2}\) from the vertex tangent, and the latus rectum is \(4\) times that.

questions.q: If the tangents drawn at the points \(P\) and \(Q\) on the parabola \(y^2=2x-3\) intersect at the point \(R(0,1)\), then the orthocentre of the triangle \(PQR\) is :
questions.sol: The chord of contact \(y=x-3\) gives \(P(2,-1)\), \(Q(6,3)\); \(RP\perp PQ\), so the orthocentre is \(P\).

questions.q: If \(y=m_1x+c_1\) and \(y=m_2x+c_2\), \(m_1\ne m_2\) are two common tangents of circle \(x^2+y^2=2\) and parabola \(y^2=x\), then the value of \(8|m_1m_2|\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac1{4m}\) at distance \(\sqrt2\) from \(O\): \(32m^4+32m^2-1=0\), so \(m^2=\tfrac{3\sqrt2-4}8\) and \(m_1m_2=-m^2\).

questions.q: Let \(x=2t\), \(y=\dfrac{t^2}3\) be a conic. Let \(S\) be the focus and \(B\) be the point on the axis of the conic such that \(SA\perp BA\), where \(A\) is any point on the conic. If \(k\) is the ordinate of the centroid of the \(\Delta SAB\), then \(\displaystyle\lim_{t\to1}k\) is equal to
questions.sol: The conic is \(x^2=12y\) with \(S(0,3)\). At \(t=1\), \(A\left(2,\tfrac13\right)\) and \(B(0,b)\) with \(4+\tfrac83\left(b-\tfrac13\right)=0\), so \(b=-\tfrac76\). The centroid ordinate is \(\tfrac13\left(3+\tfrac13-\tfrac76\right)\).

questions.q: If the line \(y=4+kx\), \(k>0\), is the tangent to the parabola \(y=x-x^2\) at the point \(P\) and \(V\) is the vertex of the parabola, then the slope of the line through \(P\) and \(V\) is
questions.sol: \(x^2+(k-1)x+4=0\) has a double root for \(k=5\): \(P(-2,-6)\). \(V\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac14\right)\).

questions.q: Let the normal at the point \(P\) on the parabola \(y^2=6x\) pass through the point \((5,-8)\). If the tangent at \(P\) to the parabola intersects its directrix at the point \(Q\), then the ordinate of the point \(Q\) is :
questions.sol: \(a=\tfrac32\); the normal \(y=-tx+3t+\tfrac32t^3\) through \((5,-8)\) gives \(t=-2\): \(P(6,-6)\). The tangent \(-6y=3(x+6)\) meets \(x=-\tfrac32\) at \(y=-\tfrac94\).

questions.q: If the equation of the parabola, whose vertex is at \((5,4)\) and the directrix is \(3x+y-29=0\), is \(x^2+ay^2+bxy+cx+dy+k=0\), then \(a+b+c+d+k\) is equal to
If vertex of a parabola is \((2,-1)\) and the equation of its directrix is \(4x-3y=21\), then the length of its latus rectum is
questions.sol: The vertex is \(\tfrac{|8+3-21|}5=2\) from the directrix, so \(a=2\).

questions.q: Let \(P:y^2=4ax\), \(a>0\) be a parabola with focus \(S\). Let the tangents to the parabola \(P\) make an angle of \(\dfrac\pi4\) with the line \(y=3x+5\) touch the parabola \(P\) at \(A\) and \(B\). Then the value of \(a\) for which \(A\), \(B\) and \(S\) are collinear is
questions.sol: The slopes are \(-2\) and \(\tfrac12\) (product \(-1\)), so \(AB\) is a focal chord for every \(a\): \(A\left(\tfrac a4,-a\right)\), \(B(4a,4a)\), \(S(a,0)\).

questions.q: Consider the parabola with vertex \(\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac34\right)\) and the directrix \(y=\dfrac12\). Let \(P\) be the point where the parabola meets the line \(x=-\dfrac12\). If the normal to the parabola at \(P\) intersects the parabola again at the point \(Q\), then \((PQ)^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: The parabola is \(y=x^2-x+1\), \(P\left(-\tfrac12,\tfrac74\right)\), and the normal \(y=\tfrac74+\tfrac12\left(x+\tfrac12\right)\) meets it again at \(Q(2,3)\).

questions.q: If a line along a chord of the circle \(4x^2+4y^2+120x+675=0\), passes through the point \((-30,0)\) and is tangent to the parabola \(y^2=30x\), then the length of this chord is
questions.sol: \(y=m(x+30)\) is tangent when \(30m=\tfrac{15}{2m}\), i.e. \(m^2=\tfrac14\). The circle has centre \((-15,0)\), \(r=\tfrac{15}2\); the line is \(\tfrac{15}{\sqrt5}\) from the centre, so the chord is \(2\sqrt{\tfrac{225}4-45}\).

questions.q: A tangent and a normal are drawn at the point \(P(2,-4)\) on the parabola \(y^2=8x\), which meet the directrix of the parabola at the points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively. If \(Q(a,b)\) is a point such that \(AQBP\) is a square, then \(2a+b\) is equal to
If two tangents drawn from a point \(P\) to the parabola \(y^2=16(x-3)\) are at right angles, then the locus of point \(P\) is
questions.sol: Perpendicular tangents meet on the directrix, \(x=3-4\).

questions.q: The length of the latus rectum of a parabola, whose vertex and focus are on the positive \(x\)-axis at a distance \(R\) and \(S\) \((>R)\) respectively from the origin, is

Let the tangent to the parabola \(S:y^2=2x\) at the point \(P(2,2)\) meet the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\) and normal at it meet the parabola \(S\) at the point \(R\). Then the area (in sq. units) of the triangle \(PQR\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(P\) is \(t=2\) (with \(a=\tfrac12\)): \(Q(-2,0)\), and the normal meets again at \(t=-3\): \(R\left(\tfrac92,-3\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a variable point on the parabola \(y=4x^2+1\). Then, the locus of the mid-point of the point \(P\) and the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point \(P\) to the line \(y=x\) is
questions.sol: For \(P(t,4t^2+1)\) the midpoint has \(3h-k=2t\) and \(h-3k=-8t^2-2\).

questions.q: Let a parabola \(P\) be such that its vertex and focus lie on the positive \(x\)-axis at a distance \(2\) and \(4\) units from the origin, respectively. If tangents are drawn from \(O(0,0)\) to the parabola \(P\) which meet \(P\) at \(S\) and \(R\), then the area (in sq. units) of \(\Delta SOR\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(P:y^2=8(x-2)\). Tangents \(y=m(x-2)+\tfrac2m\) through \(O\) need \(m=\pm1\), touching at \((4,\pm4)\).

questions.q: If the three normals drawn to the parabola, \(y^2=2x\) pass through the point \((a,0)\), \(a\ne0\), then '\(a\)' must be greater than
questions.sol: Normals \(y=mx-m-\tfrac{m^3}2\) through \((a,0)\): \(m=0\) or \(m^2=2(a-1)\).

questions.q: Let \(C\) be the locus of the mirror image of a point on the parabola \(y^2=4x\) with respect to the line \(y=x\). Then the equation of tangent to \(C\) at \(P(2,1)\) is
The locus of the mid-point of the line segment joining the focus of the parabola \(y^2=4ax\) to a moving point of the parabola, is another parabola whose directrix is
questions.sol: The midpoint \(\left(\tfrac{a+at^2}2,at\right)\) traces \(y^2=2a\left(x-\tfrac a2\right)\), with directrix \(x=\tfrac a2-\tfrac a2\).

questions.q: If \(P\) is a point on the parabola \(y=x^2+4\) which is closest to the straight line \(y=4x-1\), then the co-ordinates of \(P\) are
questions.sol: The tangent slope \(2x=4\).

questions.q: A tangent is drawn to the parabola \(y^2=6x\) which is perpendicular to the line \(2x+y=1\). Which of the following points does not lie on it?
questions.sol: The tangent of slope \(\tfrac12\) is \(y=\tfrac x2+3\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a point on the parabola, \(y^2=12x\) and \(N\) be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from \(P\) on the axis of the parabola. A line is now drawn through the mid-point \(M\) of \(PN\), parallel to its axis which meets the parabola at \(Q\). If the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(NQ\) is \(\dfrac43\), then
questions.sol: \(P(3t^2,6t)\), \(M(3t^2,3t)\), \(Q\left(\tfrac34t^2,3t\right)\). Line \(NQ\) has \(y\)-intercept \(4t=\tfrac43\), so \(t=\tfrac13\) and \(MQ=\tfrac94t^2\).

questions.q: Let the latus rectum of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) be the common chord to the circles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) each of them having radius \(2\sqrt5\). Then, the distance between the centres of the circles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) is
questions.sol: The chord has length \(4\), so each centre is \(\sqrt{20-4}\) from it.

questions.q: If the common tangent to the parabolas, \(y^2=4x\) and \(x^2=4y\) also touches the circle, \(x^2+y^2=c^2\), then \(c\) is equal to
questions.sol: The common tangent is \(x+y+1=0\).

questions.q: Let \(L_1\) be a tangent to the parabola \(y^2=4(x+1)\) and \(L_2\) be a tangent to the parabola \(y^2=8(x+2)\) such that \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) intersect at right angles. Then \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) meet on the straight line
questions.sol: \(L_1:y=m(x+1)+\tfrac1m\) and \(L_2:y=-\tfrac1m(x+2)-2m\). Equating: \(x\left(m+\tfrac1m\right)=-3\left(m+\tfrac1m\right)\).

questions.q: If \(y=mx+4\) is a tangent to both the parabolas, \(y^2=4x\) and \(x^2=2by\), then \(b\) is equal to
questions.sol: Tangency to \(y^2=4x\): \(4=\tfrac1m\). Then \(x^2-\tfrac b2x-8b=0\) has a double root: \(\tfrac{b^2}4+32b=0\).

questions.q: The locus of a point which divides the line segment joining the point \((0,-1)\) and a point on the parabola, \(x^2=4y\), internally in the ratio \(1:2\), is
questions.sol: The point is \(\left(\tfrac{2t}3,\tfrac{t^2-2}3\right)\).

questions.q: If one end of a focal chord \(AB\) of the parabola \(y^2=8x\) is at \(A\left(\dfrac12,-2\right)\), then the equation of the tangent to it at \(B\) is
The shortest distance between the line \(y=x\) and the curve \(y^2=x-2\) is
questions.sol: The tangent of slope \(1\) touches at \(\left(\tfrac94,\tfrac12\right)\).

questions.q: The tangent to the parabola \(y^2=4x\) at the point where it intersects the circle \(x^2+y^2=5\) in the first quadrant, passes through the point
questions.sol: They meet at \((1,2)\), where the tangent is \(y=x+1\).

questions.q: If one end of a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=16x\) is at \((1,4)\), then length of this focal chord is
questions.sol: \(t=\tfrac12\): length \(a\left(t+\tfrac1t\right)^2=4\cdot\tfrac{25}4\).

questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the smaller of the two circles that touch the parabola, \(y^2=4x\) at the point \((1,2)\) and the \(x\)-axis is
questions.sol: The centre lies on the normal \((1+k,2-k)\) with radius \(\sqrt2k=2-k\): \(r=2(2-\sqrt2)\).

questions.q: If the line \(ax+y=c\), touches both the curves \(x^2+y^2=1\) and \(y^2=4\sqrt2x\), then \(|c|\) is equal to
questions.sol: Tangency to the parabola: \(c=-\tfrac{\sqrt2}a\); to the circle: \(c^2=1+a^2\). So \(a^4+a^2-2=0\), \(a^2=1\).

questions.q: The equation of a common tangent to the curves, \(y^2=16x\) and \(xy=-4\), is
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac4m\) meets \(xy=-4\) in \(mx^2+\tfrac4mx+4=0\); a double root needs \(m^3=1\).

questions.q: The tangents to the curve \(y=(x-2)^2-1\) at its points of intersection with the line \(x-y=3\), intersect at the point
questions.sol: The points are \((2,-1)\) and \((3,0)\), with tangents \(y=-1\) and \(y=2x-6\).

questions.q: Axis of a parabola lies along \(x\)-axis. If its vertex and focus are at distances \(2\) and \(4\) respectively from the origin, on the positive \(x\)-axis, then which of the following points does not lie on it?
questions.sol: The parabola is \(y^2=8(x-2)\); \((8,6)\) gives \(36\ne48\).

questions.q: Equation of a common tangent to the circle, \(x^2+y^2-6x=0\) and the parabola, \(y^2=4x\), is
The shortest distance between the point \(\left(\dfrac32,0\right)\) and the curve \(y=\sqrt x\), \((x>0)\), is
questions.sol: \(\left(x-\tfrac32\right)^2+x\) is least at \(x=1\).

questions.q: If the parabolas \(y^2=4b(x-c)\) and \(y^2=8ax\) have a common normal, then which one of the following is a valid choice for the ordered triad \((a,b,c)\)?
questions.sol: Equating the normals \(y=mx-4am-2am^3\) and \(y=m(x-c)-2bm-bm^3\): \(m^2(2a-b)=c+2b-4a\), which needs a positive value. \((1,1,3)\) gives \(m^2=1\); for (b) the value is negative, and (c), (d) have \(2a=b\). (The book key accepts all four, presumably counting \(m=0\), the axis, as a common normal.)

questions.q: The length of the chord of the parabola \(x^2=4y\) having equation \(x-\sqrt2y+4\sqrt2=0\) is
questions.sol: \(x^2-2\sqrt2x-16=0\) gives \(|x_1-x_2|=6\sqrt2\), and the chord is \(6\sqrt2\sqrt{1+\tfrac12}\).

questions.q: If the area of the triangle whose one vertex is at the vertex of the parabola, \(y^2+4(x-a^2)=0\) and the other two vertices are the points of intersection of the parabola and \(y\)-axis, is \(250\) sq. units, then a value of \(a\) is
questions.sol: The vertex is \((a^2,0)\) and the \(y\)-intercepts are \(\pm2a\): area \(2|a|^3\).

questions.q: The equation of a tangent to the parabola, \(x^2=8y\), which makes an angle \(\theta\) with the positive direction of \(x\)-axis is
questions.sol: Tangents to \(x^2=8y\) are \(y=mx-2m^2\); with \(m=\tan\theta\) this is (c).

questions.q: Tangent and normal are drawn at \(P(16,16)\) on the parabola \(y^2=16x\), which intersect the axis of the parabola at \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. If \(C\) is the centre of the circle through the points \(P\), \(A\) and \(B\) and \(\angle CPB=\theta\), then a value of \(\tan\theta\) is
questions.sol: \(A(-16,0)\), \(B(24,0)\); \(\angle APB=90^\circ\), so \(C=(4,0)\). Slopes \(PC=\tfrac43\), \(PB=-2\): \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{\frac43+2}{\left|1-\frac83\right|}\).

questions.q: Two parabolas with a common vertex and with axes along \(x\)-axis and \(y\)-axis, respectively, intersect each other in the first quadrant. If the length of the latus rectum of each parabola is \(3\), then the equation of the common tangent to the two parabolas is
questions.sol: \(y^2=3x\) and \(x^2=3y\); by symmetry the common tangent has slope \(-1\): \(y=-x-\tfrac34\).

questions.q: Tangents drawn from the point \((-8,0)\) to the parabola \(y^2=8x\) touch the parabola at \(P\) and \(Q\). If \(F\) is the focus of the parabola, then the area of the triangle \(PFQ\) (in sq. units) is equal to
questions.sol: The chord of contact is \(x=8\): \(P,Q=(8,\pm8)\), \(F(2,0)\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a point on the parabola, \(x^2=4y\). If the distance of \(P\) from the centre of the circle, \(x^2+y^2+6x+8=0\) is minimum, then the equation of the tangent to the parabola at \(P\), is
If the common tangents to the parabola, \(x^2=4y\) and the circle, \(x^2+y^2=4\) intersect at the point \(P\), then the distance of \(P\) from the origin, is
questions.sol: Tangents \(y=mx-m^2\) with \(\tfrac{m^2}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}=2\): \(m^2=2+2\sqrt2\). The pair meets at \((0,-m^2)\). (Options (a) and (c) are equal.)

questions.q: If \(y=mx+c\) is the normal at a point on the parabola \(y^2=8x\) whose focal distance is \(8\) units, then \(|c|\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(x+2=8\) gives \(t=\pm\sqrt3\); the normal \(y=-tx+4t+2t^3\) has \(|c|=4\sqrt3+6\sqrt3\).

questions.q: The centres of those circles which touch the circle, \(x^2+y^2-8x-8y-4=0\), externally and also touch the \(x\)-axis, lie on
opts: an ellipse which is not a circle
questions.sol: The given circle has centre \((4,4)\), \(r=6\): \(\sqrt{(h-4)^2+(k-4)^2}=k+6\), a parabola.

questions.q: Let \(P\) be the point on the parabola, \(y^2=8x\) which is at a minimum distance from the centre \(C\) of the circle, \(x^2+(y+6)^2=1\). Then the equation of the circle, passing through \(C\) and having its centre at \(P\) is
The minimum distance of a point on the curve \(y=x^2-4\) from the origin is

\(P\) and \(Q\) are two distinct points on the parabola, \(y^2=4x\), with parameters \(t\) and \(t_1\) respectively. If the normal at \(P\) passes through \(Q\), then the minimum value of \(t_1^2\) is
Let \(O\) be the vertex and \(Q\) be any point on the parabola, \(x^2=8y\). If the point \(P\) divides the line segment \(OQ\) internally in the ratio \(1:3\), then the locus of \(P\) is
If the tangent to the conic, \(y-6=x^2\) at \((2,10)\) touches the circle, \(x^2+y^2+8x-2y=k\) (for some fixed \(k\)) at a point \((\alpha,\beta)\); then \((\alpha,\beta)\) is
questions.sol: The tangent \(4x-y+2=0\); the contact point is the foot of the centre \((-4,1)\) on it.

questions.q: Let \(PQ\) be a double ordinate of the parabola, \(y^2=-4x\), where \(P\) lies in the second quadrant. If \(R\) divides \(PQ\) in the ratio \(2:1\), then the locus of \(R\) is
Two tangents are drawn from a point \((-2,-1)\) to the curve, \(y^2=4x\). If \(\alpha\) is the angle between them, then \(|\tan\alpha|\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(-1=-2m+\tfrac1m\) gives \(m=1,-\tfrac12\).

questions.q: The slope of the line touching both the parabolas \(y^2=4x\) and \(x^2=-32y\) is

Given : A circle, \(2x^2+2y^2=5\) and a parabola \(y^2=4\sqrt5x\).
Statement-1 : An equation of a common tangent to these curves is \(y=x+\sqrt5\).
Statement-2 : If the line, \(y=mx+\dfrac{\sqrt5}m\) \((m\ne0)\) is their common tangent, then \(m\) satisfies \(m^4-3m^2+2=0\).
opts: Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is true, Statement-2 is not a correct explanation for Statement-1.
Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is false.
Statement-1 is false, Statement-2 is true.
Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is true, Statement-2 is a correct explanation for Statement-1.
questions.sol: Tangency to the circle: \(\dfrac{5}{m^2(1+m^2)}=\dfrac52\), so \(m^4+m^2-2=0\), \(m^2=1\). Thus \(y=x+\sqrt5\) is a common tangent, and \(m^2=1\) also satisfies \(m^4-3m^2+2=0\), though that equation is not the condition.

questions.q: The shortest distance between line \(y-x=1\) and curve \(x=y^2\) is
questions.sol: The tangent of slope \(1\) touches at \(\left(\tfrac14,\tfrac12\right)\), at distance \(\dfrac{3/4}{\sqrt2}\).

questions.q: If two tangents drawn from a point \(P\) to the parabola \(y^2=4x\) are at right angles, then the locus of \(P\) is
questions.sol: Perpendicular tangents meet on the directrix.

questions.q: A parabola has the origin as its focus and the line \(x=2\) as the directrix. Then the vertex of the parabola is at
questions.sol: The vertex is midway between the focus and the directrix.

questions.q: The equation of a tangent to the parabola \(y^2=8x\) is \(y=x+2\). The point on this line from which the other tangent to the parabola is perpendicular to the given tangent is
questions.sol: Perpendicular tangents meet on the directrix \(x=-2\).

questions.q: The locus of the vertices of the family of parabolas \(y=\dfrac{a^3x^2}3+\dfrac{a^2x}2-2a\) is
questions.sol: The vertex is at \(x=-\tfrac3{4a}\), \(y=-\tfrac{35a}{16}\).

questions.q: A circle touches the \(x\)-axis and also touches the circle with centre at \((0,3)\) and radius \(2\). The locus of the centre of the circle is
questions.sol: \(\sqrt{h^2+(k-3)^2}=|k|+2\) is a parabola.

questions.q: Let \(P\) be the point \((1,0)\) and \(Q\) a point on the locus \(y^2=8x\). The locus of mid point of \(PQ\) is
questions.sol: The midpoint is \(\left(\tfrac{1+2t^2}2,2t\right)\).

questions.q: If \(a\ne0\) and the line \(2bx+3cy+4d=0\) passes through the points of intersection of the parabolas \(y^2=4ax\) and \(x^2=4ay\), then
questions.sol: The parabolas meet at \((0,0)\) and \((4a,4a)\), so \(d=0\) and \(2b+3c=0\).

questions.q: A point on the parabola \(y^2=18x\) at which the ordinate increases at twice the rate of the abscissa is
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac9y=2\).

questions.q: The normal at the point \((bt_1^2,2bt_1)\) on a parabola meets the parabola again in the point \((bt_2^2,2bt_2)\), then
questions.sol: Standard result for \(y^2=4bx\).

questions.q: Two common tangents to the circle \(x^2+y^2=2a^2\) and parabola \(y^2=8ax\) are
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac{2a}m\) at distance \(\sqrt2a\) from \(O\): \(m^4+m^2-2=0\).

questions.q: The focus of the parabola \(y^2=4x+16\) is the centre of the circle \(C\) of radius \(5\). If the values of \(\lambda\), for which \(C\) passes through the point of intersection of the lines \(3x-y=0\) and \(x+\lambda y=4\), are \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\), \(\lambda_1<\lambda_2\), then \(12\lambda_1+29\lambda_2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The focus is \((-3,0)\). The intersection is \((4u,12u)\) with \(u=\tfrac1{1+3\lambda}\): \((4u+3)^2+144u^2=25\) gives \(u=\tfrac14\) or \(-\tfrac25\), i.e. \(\lambda=1\) or \(-\tfrac76\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be the two points of intersection of the line \(y+5=0\) and the mirror image of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) with respect to the line \(x+y+4=0\). If \(d\) denotes the distance between \(A\) and \(B\), and \(a\) denotes the area of \(\Delta SAB\), where \(S\) is the focus of the parabola \(y^2=4x\), then the value of \((a+d)\) is ______.

Let \(y^2=12x\) be the parabola and \(S\) be its focus. Let \(PQ\) be a focal chord of the parabola such that \((SP)(SQ)=\dfrac{147}4\). Let \(C\) be the circle described taking \(PQ\) as a diameter. If the equation of a circle \(C\) is \(64x^2+64y^2-\alpha x-64\sqrt3y=\beta\), then \(\beta-\alpha\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(9\left(t+\tfrac1t\right)^2=\tfrac{147}4\). The circle \((x-3t^2)(x-\tfrac3{t^2})+(y-6t)(y+\tfrac6t)=0\) is \(x^2+y^2-3\left(t^2+\tfrac1{t^2}\right)x-6\left(t-\tfrac1t\right)y-27=0\) with \(t^2+\tfrac1{t^2}=\tfrac{25}{12}\), \(t-\tfrac1t=\tfrac1{2\sqrt3}\). Times \(64\): \(\alpha=400\), \(\beta=1728\).

questions.q: Let the length of the focal chord \(PQ\) of the parabola \(y^2=12x\) be \(15\) units. If the distance of \(PQ\) from the origin is \(p\), then \(10p^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(3\left(t+\tfrac1t\right)^2=15\) gives \(\left(t-\tfrac1t\right)^2=1\), slope \(\pm2\): \(y=\pm2(x-3)\), at distance \(\tfrac6{\sqrt5}\) from \(O\).

questions.q: Suppose \(AB\) is a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=12x\) of length \(l\) and slope \(m<\sqrt3\). If the distance of the chord \(AB\) from the origin is \(d\), then \(ld^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: For slope \(m\): \(l=\dfrac{12(1+m^2)}{m^2}\) and \(d=\dfrac{3|m|}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}\).

questions.q: Let a line perpendicular to the line \(2x-y=10\) touch the parabola \(y^2=4(x-9)\) at the point \(P\). The distance of the point \(P\) from the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2-14x-8y+56=0\) is ______.
questions.sol: The tangent of slope \(-\tfrac12\) touches at \(\left(9+\tfrac1{m^2},\tfrac2m\right)=(13,-4)\); the centre is \((7,4)\).

questions.q: Let \(L_1\), \(L_2\) be the lines passing through the point \(P(0,1)\) and touching the parabola \(9x^2+12x+18y-14=0\). Let \(Q\) and \(R\) be the points on the lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) such that the \(\Delta PQR\) is an isosceles triangle with base \(QR\). If the slopes of the lines \(QR\) are \(m_1\) and \(m_2\), then \(16(m_1^2+m_2^2)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The parabola is \(\left(x+\tfrac23\right)^2=-2(y-1)\); the tangents through \(P\) have slopes \(0\) and \(-\tfrac43\). The angle bisectors have slopes \(2\) and \(-\tfrac12\), and \(QR\) is perpendicular to one of them: \(m=-\tfrac12\) or \(2\).

questions.q: Let a conic \(C\) pass through the point \((4,-2)\) and \(P(x,y)\), \(x\ge3\), be any point on \(C\). Let the slope of the line touching the conic \(C\) only at a single point \(P\) be half the slope of the line joining the points \(P\) and \((3,-5)\). If the focal distance of the point \((7,1)\) on \(C\) is \(d\), then \(12d\) equals ______.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y+5}{2(x-3)}\) gives \((y+5)^2=9(x-3)\). Its directrix is \(x=3-\tfrac94\), so the focal distance of \((7,1)\) is \(\tfrac{25}4\).

questions.q: Let \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) be three points on the parabola \(y^2=6x\) and let the line segment \(AB\) meet the line \(L\) through \(C\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis at the point \(D\). Let \(M\) and \(N\) respectively be the feet of the perpendiculars from \(A\) and \(B\) on \(L\). Then \(\left(\dfrac{AM\cdot BN}{CD}\right)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: With parameters \(t_1,t_2,t_3\) (\(a=\tfrac32\)): \(AM=2a|t_1-t_3|\), \(BN=2a|t_2-t_3|\), and \(CD=a|(t_1-t_3)(t_2-t_3)|\). The ratio is \(4a=6\).

questions.q: Consider the circle \(C:x^2+y^2=4\) and the parabola \(P:y^2=8x\). If the set of all values of \(\alpha\), for which three chords of the circle \(C\) on three distinct lines passing through the point \((\alpha,0)\) are bisected by the parabola \(P\) is the interval \((p,q)\), then \((2q-p)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: A midpoint \(M(2t^2,4t)\) of a chord through \((\alpha,0)\) satisfies \(M\cdot\left((\alpha,0)-M\right)=0\): \(t=0\) or \(\alpha=2t^2+8\). \(M\) inside the circle needs \(t^2<\sqrt5-2\), so \(\alpha\in(8,4+2\sqrt5)\).

questions.q: Let the line \(L:\sqrt2x+y=\alpha\) pass through the point of the intersection \(P\) (in the first quadrant) of the circle \(x^2+y^2=3\) and the parabola \(x^2=2y\). Let the line \(L\) touch two circles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) of equal radius \(2\sqrt3\). If the centres \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) of the circle \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) lie on the \(y\)-axis, then the square of the areas of the triangle \(PQ_1Q_2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(P(\sqrt2,1)\), so \(\alpha=3\). Centres \((0,k)\) with \(\tfrac{|k-3|}{\sqrt3}=2\sqrt3\): \(k=9,-3\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot12\cdot\sqrt2=6\sqrt2\). (The book key prints 36; the official answer is 72.)

questions.q: Let \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) be a point on the parabola \(y^2=4x\). If \(P\) also lies on the chord of the parabola \(x^2=8y\) whose mid point is \(\left(1,\dfrac54\right)\), then \((\alpha-28)(\beta-8)\) is equal to ______.

Let the tangent to the curve \(x^2+2x-4y+9=0\) at the point \(P(1,3)\) on it meet the \(y\)-axis at \(A\). Let the line passing through \(P\) and parallel to the line \(x-3y=6\) meet the parabola \(y^2=4x\) at \(B\). If \(B\) lies on the line \(2x-3y=8\), then \((AB)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The tangent \(y=x+2\) gives \(A(0,2)\). The line \(x=3y-8\) meets \(y^2=4x\) at \(y=4,8\); only \((16,8)\) is on \(2x-3y=8\).

questions.q: The ordinates of the points \(P\) and \(Q\) on the parabola with focus \((3,0)\) and directrix \(x=-3\) are in the ratio \(3:1\). If \(R(\alpha,\beta)\) is the point of intersection of the tangents to the parabola at \(P\) and \(Q\), then \(\dfrac{\beta^2}\alpha\) is equal to ______.
Let a common tangent to the curves \(y^2=4x\) and \((x-4)^2+y^2=16\) touch the curves at the points \(P\) and \(Q\). Then \((PQ)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac1m\) at distance \(4\) from \((4,0)\) gives \(m^2=\tfrac18\). Contacts: \(P(8,4\sqrt2)\) and the foot \(Q\left(\tfrac83,\tfrac{8\sqrt2}3\right)\).

questions.q: If the \(x\)-intercept of a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=8x+4y+4\) is \(3\), then the length of this chord is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \((y-2)^2=8(x+1)\) has focus \((1,2)\); the chord through \((3,0)\) has slope \(-1\), so \(t-\tfrac1t=-2\) and the length is \(2\left(t+\tfrac1t\right)^2=2\cdot8\).

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the set of all \(a\in N\) such that the area of the triangle formed by the tangent at the point \(P(b,c)\), \(b,c\in N\), on the parabola \(y^2=2ax\) and the lines \(x=b\), \(y=0\) is \(16\) unit\(^2\), then \(\displaystyle\sum_{a\in S}a\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The tangent meets \(y=0\) at \(x=-b\), so the area is \(bc=16\) with \(a=\tfrac{c^2}{2b}\). Natural values: \(a=128,16,2\).

questions.q: The sum of diameters of the circles that touch (i) the parabola \(75x^2=64(5y-3)\) at the point \(\left(\dfrac85,\dfrac65\right)\) and (ii) the \(y\)-axis, is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The tangent slope there is \(\tfrac34\); centres \(\left(\tfrac85+3k,\tfrac65-4k\right)\) with radius \(5|k|\) equal to the abscissa: \(k=\tfrac45\) (\(r=4\)) or \(k=-\tfrac15\) (\(r=1\)).

questions.q: Two tangent lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) are drawn from the point \((2,0)\) to the parabola \(2y^2=-x\). If the lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) are also tangent to the circle \((x-5)^2+y^2=r\), then \(17r\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(y=mx-\tfrac1{8m}\) through \((2,0)\): \(m=\pm\tfrac14\), i.e. \(x\mp4y-2=0\), at distance \(\tfrac3{\sqrt{17}}\) from \((5,0)\).

questions.q: Let \(P_1\) be a parabola with vertex \((3,2)\) and focus \((4,4)\) and \(P_2\) be its mirror image with respect to the line \(x+2y=6\). Then the directrix of \(P_2\) is \(x+2y=\) ______.
questions.sol: The directrix of \(P_1\) is \(x+2y=2\); its mirror image in \(x+2y=6\) is \(x+2y=10\).

questions.q: A circle of radius \(2\) unit passes through the vertex and the focus of the parabola \(y^2=2x\) and touches the parabola \(y=\left(x-\dfrac14\right)^2+\alpha\), where \(\alpha>0\). Then \((4\alpha-8)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The centre is \(\left(\tfrac14,k\right)\) with \(k^2=\tfrac{63}{16}\), on the axis of the second parabola, which it touches at its vertex: \(|\alpha-k|=2\).

questions.q: A tangent line \(L\) is drawn at the point \((2,-4)\) on the parabola \(y^2=8x\). If the line \(L\) is also tangent to the circle \(x^2+y^2=a\), then '\(a\)' is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(L:x+y+2=0\), at distance \(\sqrt2\) from \(O\).

questions.q: Let \(y=mx+c\), \(m>0\) be the focal chord of \(y^2=-64x\), which is tangent to \((x+10)^2+y^2=4\). Then the value of \(4\sqrt2(m+c)\) is equal to ______.
If the point on the curve \(y^2=6x\), nearest to the point \(\left(3,\dfrac32\right)\) is \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(2(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The normal \(y=-tx+3t+\tfrac32t^3\) through \(\left(3,\tfrac32\right)\) gives \(t=1\): \(\left(\tfrac32,3\right)\).

questions.q: A line is a common tangent to the circle \((x-3)^2+y^2=9\) and the parabola \(y^2=4x\). If the two points of contact \((a,b)\) and \((c,d)\) are distinct and lie in the first quadrant, then \(2(a+c)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The tangent \(y=\tfrac x{\sqrt3}+\sqrt3\) touches the parabola at \((3,2\sqrt3)\) and the circle at the foot \(\left(\tfrac32,\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2\right)\).

questions.q: Let a line \(y=mx\) \((m>0)\) intersect the parabola, \(y^2=x\) at a point \(P\), other than the origin. Let the tangent to it at \(P\) meet the \(x\)-axis at a point \(Q\). If area \((\Delta OPQ)=4\) sq. units, then \(m\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(P\left(\tfrac1{m^2},\tfrac1m\right)\); the tangent meets the \(x\)-axis at \(-\tfrac1{m^2}\). Area \(\tfrac1{2m^3}=4\).

questions.q: If \(S\) and \(S'\) are the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{18}+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) and \(P\) be a point on the ellipse, then \(\min(SP\cdot S'P)+\max(SP\cdot S'P)\) is equal to :
If the length of the minor axis of an ellipse is equal to one fourth of the distance between the foci, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is :

A line passing through the point \(P(\sqrt5,\sqrt5)\) intersects the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{36}+\dfrac{y^2}{25}=1\) at \(A\) and \(B\) such that \((PA)\cdot(PB)\) is maximum. Then \(5(PA^2+PB^2)\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(PA\cdot PB=\dfrac{595}{25\cos^2\theta+36\sin^2\theta}\) is largest for a horizontal line, \(y=\sqrt5\), which meets the ellipse at \(x^2=\tfrac{144}5\). So \(PA^2+PB^2=2\left(\tfrac{144}5+5\right)\). (The book prints the ellipse as \(\tfrac{x^2}{36}+\tfrac{y^2}{16}=1\); the exam paper has \(25\).)

questions.q: Let \(C\) be the circle of minimum area enclosing the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) with eccentricity \(\dfrac12\) and foci \((\pm2,0)\). Let \(PQR\) be a variable triangle, whose vertex \(P\) is on the circle \(C\) and the side \(QR\) of length \(2a\) is parallel to the major axis of \(E\) and contains the point of intersection of \(E\) with the negative \(y\)-axis. Then the maximum area of the triangle \(PQR\) is :
questions.sol: \(a=4\), \(b=2\sqrt3\), and \(C\) is \(x^2+y^2=16\). \(QR=8\) lies on \(y=-2\sqrt3\), and the farthest point of \(C\) is \(4+2\sqrt3\) above it.

questions.q: The length of the latus-rectum of the ellipse, whose foci are \((2,5)\) and \((2,-3)\) and eccentricity is \(\dfrac45\), is
questions.sol: \(ae=4\), so \(a=5\), \(b^2=9\), and the latus rectum is \(\tfrac{2b^2}a\).

questions.q: The centre of a circle \(C\) is at the centre of the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\). Let \(C\) pass through the foci \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) of \(E\) such that the circle \(C\) and the ellipse \(E\) intersect at four points. Let \(P\) be one of these four points. If the area of the triangle \(PF_1F_2\) is \(30\) and the length of the major axis of \(E\) is \(17\), then the distance between the foci of \(E\) is :
questions.sol: \(\angle F_1PF_2=90^\circ\), so the area is \(b^2=30\). Then \(a^2e^2=\tfrac{289}4-30=\tfrac{169}4\).

questions.q: Let for two distinct values of \(p\) the lines \(y=x+p\) touch the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{4^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{3^2}=1\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Let the line \(y=x\) intersect \(E\) at the points \(C\) and \(D\). Then the area of the quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is equal to :
questions.sol: \(p=\pm5\), touching at \(\pm\left(-\tfrac{16}5,\tfrac95\right)\); \(y=x\) meets \(E\) at \(\pm\left(\tfrac{12}5,\tfrac{12}5\right)\). The diagonals pass through \(O\): area \(\tfrac12|\vec{AB}\times\vec{CD}|=\tfrac12\cdot48\).

questions.q:
Let the system of equations
\(x+5y-z=1\)
\(4x+3y-3z=7\)
\(24x+y+\lambda z=\mu\)
\(\lambda,\mu\in\mathbf R\), have infinitely many solutions. Then the number of the solutions of this system, if \(x,y,z\) are integers and satisfy \(7\le x+y+z\le77\), is :
questions.sol: The determinant vanishes for \(\lambda=-17\), and \(R_3=-4R_1+7R_2\) gives \(\mu=45\). The solutions are \(x=4+12y\), \(z=3+17y\), with \(x+y+z=7+30y\), so \(y=0,1,2\).

questions.q: Let \(p\) be the number of all triangles that can be formed by joining the vertices of a regular polygon \(P\) of \(n\) sides and \(q\) be the number of all quadrilaterals that can be formed by joining the vertices of \(P\).
