If \(p+q=126\), then the eccentricity of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}n=1\) is:

Let the ellipse \(3x^2+py^2=4\) pass through the centre \(C\) of the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-4y-11=0\) of radius \(r\). Let \(f_1,f_2\) be the focal distances of the point \(C\) on the ellipse. Then \(6f_1f_2-r\) is equal to
The length of the chord of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}2=1\), whose mid-point is \(\left(1,\dfrac12\right)\), is:
questions.sol: \(T=S_1\): \(x+y=\tfrac32\). Then \(3x^2-6x+\tfrac12=0\), \(|x_1-x_2|=\tfrac{\sqrt{30}}3\), and the chord is \(\sqrt2\) times that.

questions.q: Let the product of the focal distances of the point \(\left(\sqrt3,\dfrac12\right)\) on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \((a>b)\), be \(\dfrac74\). Then the absolute difference of the eccentricities of two such ellipses is
questions.sol: \(a^2-3e^2=\tfrac74\) with \(\tfrac3{a^2}+\tfrac1{4b^2}=1\) gives \(4a^4-31a^2+60=0\): \((a^2,b^2)=(4,1)\) or \(\left(\tfrac{15}4,\tfrac54\right)\), so \(e=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\) or \(\sqrt{\tfrac23}\).

questions.q: The equation of the chord, of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\), whose mid-point is \((3,1)\) is :
If the midpoint of a chord of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) is \(\left(\sqrt2,\dfrac43\right)\), and the length of the chord is \(\dfrac{2\sqrt\alpha}3\), then \(\alpha\) is:
questions.sol: The chord \(\sqrt2x+3y=6\) meets the ellipse at \((0,2)\) and \(\left(2\sqrt2,\tfrac23\right)\): length\(^2=8+\tfrac{16}9=\tfrac{88}9\).

questions.q: Let the ellipse \(E_1:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\) and \(E_2:\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{B^2}=1\), \(A<B\) have same eccentricity \(\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\). Let the product of their lengths of latus rectums be \(\dfrac{32}{\sqrt3}\), and the distance between the foci of \(E_1\) be \(4\). If \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) meet at \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\), then the area of the quadrilateral \(ABCD\) equals :
questions.sol: \(E_1\): \(a^2=12\), \(b^2=8\), latus rectum \(\tfrac8{\sqrt3}\). So \(E_2\) has latus rectum \(4=\tfrac{2A^2}B\) with \(A^2=\tfrac23B^2\): \(B^2=9\), \(A^2=6\). Solving, \(x^2=\tfrac65\), \(y^2=\tfrac{36}5\); the rectangle has area \(4|xy|\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha x+\beta y=109\) is the equation of the chord of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\), whose mid point is \(\left(\dfrac52,\dfrac12\right)\), then \(\alpha+\beta\) is equal to :

Let the line \(2x+3y-k=0\), \(k>0\), intersect the \(x\)-axis and \(y\)-axis at the points \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. If the equation of the circle having the line segment \(AB\) as a diameter is \(x^2+y^2-3x-2y=0\) and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse \(x^2+9y^2=k^2\) is \(\dfrac mn\), where \(m\) and \(n\) are coprime, then \(2m+n\) is equal to
questions.sol: The circle is \(x^2+y^2-\tfrac k2x-\tfrac k3y=0\), so \(k=6\). \(\tfrac{x^2}{36}+\tfrac{y^2}4=1\) has latus rectum \(\tfrac43\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=x^2+9\), \(g(x)=\dfrac x{x-9}\) and \(a=fog(10)\), \(b=gof(3)\). If \(e\) and \(l\) denote the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}a+\dfrac{y^2}b=1\), then \(8e^2+l^2\) is equal to

Let \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\) be an ellipse, whose eccentricity is \(\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\) and the length of the latusrectum is \(\sqrt{14}\). Then the square of the eccentricity of \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) is :
questions.sol: \(\tfrac{b^2}{a^2}=\tfrac12\), so the hyperbola has \(e^2=1+\tfrac12\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a point on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\). Let the line passing through \(P\) and parallel to \(y\)-axis meet the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) at point \(Q\) such that \(P\) and \(Q\) are on the same side of the \(x\)-axis. Then, the eccentricity of the locus of the point \(R\) on \(PQ\) such that \(PR:RQ=4:3\) as \(P\) moves on the ellipse, is :
questions.sol: \(P(3\cos\theta,2\sin\theta)\), \(Q(3\cos\theta,3\sin\theta)\), \(R=\tfrac{3P+4Q}7=\left(3\cos\theta,\tfrac{18}7\sin\theta\right)\): \(e^2=1-\tfrac{36}{49}\).

questions.q: The length of the chord of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\), whose mid point is \(\left(1,\dfrac25\right)\), is equal to :
questions.sol: The chord \(8x+5y=10\) gives \(4x^2-8x-15=0\): \(|x_1-x_2|=\tfrac{\sqrt{304}}4\), and the chord is \(|x_1-x_2|\sqrt{1+\tfrac{64}{25}}\).

questions.q: If the length of the minor axis of an ellipse is equal to half of the distance between the foci, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is

Let \(A(\alpha,0)\) and \(B(0,\beta)\) be the points on the line \(5x+7y=50\). Let the point \(P\) divide the line segment \(AB\) internally in the ratio \(7:3\). Let \(3x-25=0\) be a directrix of the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) and the corresponding focus be \(S\). If from \(S\), the perpendicular on the \(x\)-axis passes through \(P\), then the length of the latus rectum of \(E\) is equal to,

Let \(P\) be a parabola with vertex \((2,3)\) and directrix \(2x+y=6\). Let an ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\) of eccentricity \(\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\) pass through the focus of the parabola \(P\). Then the square of the length of the latus rectum of \(E\) is
questions.sol: The focus is \(\left(\tfrac{12}5,\tfrac{16}5\right)\). With \(b^2=\tfrac{a^2}2\): \(a^2=x^2+2y^2=\tfrac{656}{25}\), and the latus rectum \(\tfrac{2b^2}a=a\).

questions.q: In a group of \(100\) persons, \(75\) speak English and \(40\) speak Hindi. Each person speaks at least one of the two languages. If the number of persons who speak only English is \(\alpha\) and the number of persons who speak only Hindi is \(\beta\), then the eccentricity of the ellipse \(25(\beta^2x^2+\alpha^2y^2)=\alpha^2\beta^2\) is

Let the ellipse \(E:x^2+9y^2=9\) intersect the positive \(x\)- and \(y\)-axes at the points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively. Let the major axis of \(E\) be a diameter of the circle \(C\). Let the line passing through \(A\) and \(B\) meet the circle \(C\) at the point \(P\). If the area of the triangle with vertices \(A\), \(P\) and the origin \(O\) is \(\dfrac mn\), where \(m\) and \(n\) are coprime, then \(m-n\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(AB:x+3y=3\) meets \(x^2+y^2=9\) again at \(P\left(-\tfrac{12}5,\tfrac95\right)\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot\tfrac95\).

questions.q: Let a circle of radius \(4\) be concentric to the ellipse \(15x^2+19y^2=285\). Then the common tangents are inclined to the minor axis of the ellipse at the angle
questions.sol: \(19m^2+15=16(1+m^2)\) gives \(m=\pm\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\): \(30^\circ\) with the \(x\)-axis, \(60^\circ\) with the minor axis.

questions.q: Consider ellipses \(E_k:kx^2+k^2y^2=1\), \(k=1,2,\dots,20\). Let \(C_k\) be the circle which touches the four chords joining the end points (one on minor axis and another on major axis) of the ellipse \(E_k\). If \(r_k\) is the radius of the circle \(C_k\), then the value of \(\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{20}\dfrac1{r_k^2}\) is
If the radius of the largest circle with centre \((2,0)\) inscribed in the ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=36\) is \(r\), then \(12r^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: The squared distance from \((2,0)\) is \(\tfrac34x^2-4x+13\), least at \(x=\tfrac83\): \(\tfrac{23}3\).

questions.q: Let \(P\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{\sqrt7},\dfrac6{\sqrt7}\right)\), \(Q\), \(R\) and \(S\) be four points on the ellipse \(9x^2+4y^2=36\). Let \(PQ\) and \(RS\) be mutually perpendicular and pass through the origin. If \(\dfrac1{(PQ)^2}+\dfrac1{(RS)^2}=\dfrac pq\), where \(p\) and \(q\) are coprime, then \(p+q\) is equal to
questions.sol: For perpendicular semi-diameters, \(\tfrac1{OP^2}+\tfrac1{OR^2}=\tfrac14+\tfrac19=\tfrac{13}{36}\). Since \(PQ=2OP\), \(RS=2OR\), the sum is \(\tfrac{13}{144}\).

questions.q: Let the tangent and normal at the point \((3\sqrt3,1)\) on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{36}+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) meet the \(y\)-axis at the points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively. Let the circle \(C\) be drawn taking \(AB\) as a diameter and the line \(x=2\sqrt5\) intersect \(C\) at the points \(P\) and \(Q\). If the tangents at the points \(P\) and \(Q\) on the circle intersect at the point \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(\alpha^2-\beta^2\) is equal to
If the maximum distance of normal to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(b<2\), from the origin is \(1\), then the eccentricity of the ellipse is :
questions.sol: The maximum distance of a normal from the centre is \(a-b=1\), so \(b=1\).

questions.q: If the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) meets the line \(\dfrac x7+\dfrac y{2\sqrt6}=1\) on the \(x\)-axis and the line \(\dfrac x7-\dfrac y{2\sqrt6}=1\) on the \(y\)-axis, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
The acute angle between the pair of tangents drawn to the ellipse \(2x^2+3y^2=5\) from the point \((1,3)\) is
questions.sol: \((3-m)^2=\tfrac52m^2+\tfrac53\) gives \(9m^2+36m-44=0\): \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{16+\frac{176}9}}{\left|1-\frac{44}9\right|}\).

questions.q: The line \(y=x+1\) meets the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}2=1\) at two points \(P\) and \(Q\). If \(r\) is the radius of the circle with \(PQ\) as diameter then \((3r)^2\) is equal to
If \(m\) is the slope of a common tangent to the curves \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) and \(x^2+y^2=12\), then \(12m^2\) is equal to :
The locus of the mid point of the line segment joining the point \((4,3)\) and the points on the ellipse \(x^2+2y^2=4\) is an ellipse with eccentricity :
questions.sol: The locus is a half-size copy of the ellipse, so \(e\) is unchanged: \(e^2=1-\tfrac24\).

questions.q: Let the eccentricity of an ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\), be \(\dfrac14\). If this ellipse passes through the point \(\left(-4\sqrt{\dfrac25},3\right)\), then \(a^2+b^2\) is equal to :

Let \(PQ\) be a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) such that it subtends an angle of \(\dfrac\pi2\) at the point \((3,0)\). Let the line segment \(PQ\) be also a focal chord of the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a^2>b^2\). If \(e\) is the eccentricity of the ellipse \(E\), then the value of \(\dfrac1{e^2}\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The right angle at \((3,0)\) gives \(t^2+\tfrac1{t^2}=2\): \(PQ\) is the latus rectum \(x=1\), points \((1,\pm2)\). For \(E\): \(ae=1\) and \(\tfrac{b^2}a=2\), so \(a^2-2a-1=0\), \(a=1+\sqrt2\).

questions.q: Let \(\theta\) be the acute angle between the tangents to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}1=1\) and the circle \(x^2+y^2=3\) at their point of intersection in the first quadrant. Then \(\tan\theta\) is equal to
questions.sol: The point is \(\left(\tfrac32,\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)\); tangent slopes \(-\tfrac1{3\sqrt3}\) and \(-\sqrt3\).

questions.q: On the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}8+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\), let \(P\) be a point in the second quadrant such that the tangent at \(P\) to the ellipse is perpendicular to the line \(x+2y=0\). Let \(S\) and \(S'\) be the foci of the ellipse and \(e\) be its eccentricity. If \(A\) is the area of the triangle \(SPS'\) then, the value of \((5-e^2)\cdot A\) is
questions.sol: The tangent \(y=2x+6\) touches at \(P\left(-\tfrac83,\tfrac23\right)\). \(A=\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot\tfrac23\) and \(e^2=\tfrac12\).

questions.q: The line \(12x\cos\theta+5y\sin\theta=60\) is tangent to which of the following curves?
questions.sol: The line is \(\tfrac{x\cos\theta}5+\tfrac{y\sin\theta}{12}=1\), the tangent to \(\tfrac{x^2}{25}+\tfrac{y^2}{144}=1\).

questions.q: The locus of mid-points of the line segments joining \((-3,-5)\) and the points on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) is
questions.sol: \(\cos\theta=\tfrac{2x+3}2\), \(\sin\theta=\tfrac{2y+5}3\).

questions.q: Let \(E_1:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\). Let \(E_2\) be another ellipse such that it touches the end points of major axis of \(E_1\) and the foci of \(E_2\) are the end points of minor axis of \(E_1\). If \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) have same eccentricities, then its value is
questions.sol: \(E_2\) has minor semi-axis \(a\) and foci \((0,\pm b)\), so \(e_2^2=\tfrac{b^2}{a^2+b^2}\). Equating with \(1-\tfrac{b^2}{a^2}\): \(r^2+r-1=0\) for \(r=\tfrac{b^2}{a^2}\), and \(e^2=1-r=\left(\tfrac{\sqrt5-1}2\right)^2\).

questions.q: Let an ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a^2>b^2\), passes through \(\left(\sqrt{\dfrac32},1\right)\) and has eccentricity \(\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\). If a circle, centered at focus \(F(\alpha,0)\), \(\alpha>0\), of \(E\) and radius \(\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\), intersects \(E\) at two points \(P\) and \(Q\), then \(PQ^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(a^2=3\), \(b^2=2\), \(F(1,0)\). The focal distance \(\sqrt3-\tfrac x{\sqrt3}=\tfrac2{\sqrt3}\) gives \(x=1\), \(y^2=\tfrac43\).

questions.q: If a tangent to the ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=4\) meets the tangents at the extremities of its major axis at \(B\) and \(C\), then the circle with \(BC\) as diameter passes through the point
questions.sol: The ordinates of \(B\), \(C\) have product \(1\), so the circle \((x^2-4)+(y-y_1)(y-y_2)=0\) meets \(y=0\) at \(x^2=3\) (the foci).

questions.q: A ray of light through \((2,1)\) is reflected at a point \(P\) on the \(y\)-axis and then passes through the point \((5,3)\). If this reflected ray is the directrix of an ellipse with eccentricity \(\dfrac13\) and the distance of the nearer focus from this directrix is \(\dfrac8{\sqrt{53}}\), then the equation of the other directrix can be
questions.sol: The reflected ray joins \((-2,1)\) (the image of \((2,1)\)) to \((5,3)\): \(2x-7y+11=0\). \(\tfrac ae-ae=\tfrac8{\sqrt{53}}\) gives \(a=\tfrac3{\sqrt{53}}\), and the directrices are \(\tfrac{2a}e=\tfrac{18}{\sqrt{53}}\) apart.

questions.q: If the points of intersections of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) and the circle \(x^2+y^2=4b\), \(b>4\) lie on the curve \(y^2=3x^2\), then \(b\) is equal to
Let \(L\) be the tangent line to the parabola \(y^2=4x-20\) at \((6,2)\). If \(L\) is also a tangent to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}2+\dfrac{y^2}b=1\), then the value of \(b\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(L:y=x-4\); tangency \(16=2\cdot1+b\).

questions.q: Let a tangent be drawn to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{27}+y^2=1\) at \((3\sqrt3\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), where \(\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\). Then the value of \(\theta\) such that the sum of intercepts on axes made by this tangent is minimum, is equal to
questions.sol: The intercept sum \(\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{\cos\theta}+\tfrac1{\sin\theta}\) is stationary when \(\tan^3\theta=\tfrac1{3\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: For which of the following curves, the line \(x+\sqrt3y=2\sqrt3\) is the tangent at the point \(\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2,\dfrac12\right)\)?
questions.sol: The point lies on \(x^2+9y^2=9\), where the tangent is \(\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2x+\tfrac92y=9\), i.e. the given line.

questions.q: If the curve \(x^2+2y^2=2\) intersects the line \(x+y=1\) at two points \(P\) and \(Q\), then the angle subtended by the line segment \(PQ\) at the origin is
questions.sol: \(P(0,1)\), \(Q\left(\tfrac43,-\tfrac13\right)\); \(OQ\) is \(\tan^{-1}\tfrac14\) below the \(x\)-axis.

questions.q: Let \(e_1\) and \(e_2\) be the eccentricities of the ellipse, \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) \((b<5)\) and the hyperbola, \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) respectively satisfying \(e_1e_2=1\). If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the distances between the foci of the ellipse and the foci of the hyperbola respectively, then the ordered pair \((\alpha,\beta)\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(\left(1-\tfrac{b^2}{25}\right)\left(1+\tfrac{b^2}{16}\right)=1\) gives \(b^2=9\): \(e_1=\tfrac45\), \(e_2=\tfrac54\).

questions.q: Let \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) \((a>b)\) be a given ellipse, length of whose latus rectum is \(10\). If its eccentricity is the maximum value of the function, \(\phi(t)=\dfrac5{12}+t-t^2\), then \(a^2+b^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(e=\phi\left(\tfrac12\right)=\tfrac23\), \(b^2=\tfrac59a^2\), and \(\tfrac{2b^2}a=10\) gives \(a=9\).

questions.q: Let \(x=4\) be a directrix to an ellipse whose centre is at the origin and its eccentricity is \(\dfrac12\). If \(P(1,\beta)\), \(\beta>0\) is a point on this ellipse, then the equation of the normal to it at \(P\) is
If the coordinates of two points \(A\) and \(B\) are \((\sqrt7,0)\) and \((-\sqrt7,0)\) respectively and \(P\) is any point on the conic, \(9x^2+16y^2=144\), then \(PA+PB\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(A\), \(B\) are the foci of \(\tfrac{x^2}{16}+\tfrac{y^2}9=1\).

questions.q: If the point \(P\) on the curve, \(4x^2+5y^2=20\) is farthest from the point \(Q(0,-4)\), then \(PQ^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: With \(P(\sqrt5\cos\theta,2\sin\theta)\): \(PQ^2=21+16s-s^2\), \(s=\sin\theta\le1\).

questions.q: Which of the following points lies on the locus of the foot of perpendicular drawn upon any tangent to the ellipse, \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}2=1\) from any of its foci?
questions.sol: The locus is the auxiliary circle \(x^2+y^2=4\).

questions.q: If the normal at an end of a latus rectum of an ellipse passes through an extremity of the minor axis, then the eccentricity \(e\) of the ellipse satisfies
questions.sol: The normal at \(\left(ae,\tfrac{b^2}a\right)\) is \(\tfrac{ax}e-ay=a^2e^2\); through \((0,-b)\): \(b=ae^2\), so \(1-e^2=e^4\).

questions.q: If the distance between the foci of an ellipse is \(6\) and the distance between its directrices is \(12\), then the length of its latus rectum is
questions.sol: \(ae=3\) and \(\tfrac ae=6\): \(a^2=18\), \(b^2=9\), latus rectum \(\tfrac{18}{3\sqrt2}\).

questions.q: If \(3x+4y=12\sqrt2\) is a tangent to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) for some \(a\in R\), then the distance between the foci of the ellipse is

Let the line \(y=mx\) and the ellipse \(2x^2+y^2=1\) intersect at a point \(P\) in the first quadrant. If the normal to this ellipse at \(P\) meets the co-ordinate axes at \(\left(-\dfrac1{3\sqrt2},0\right)\) and \((0,\beta)\), then \(\beta\) is equal to
questions.sol: The normal \(\tfrac x{2x_1}-\tfrac y{y_1}=-\tfrac12\) has \(x\)-intercept \(-x_1\), so \(x_1=\tfrac1{3\sqrt2}\), \(y_1=\tfrac{2\sqrt2}3\), and \(\beta=\tfrac{y_1}2\).

questions.q: The length of the minor axis (along \(y\)-axis) of an ellipse in the standard form is \(\dfrac4{\sqrt3}\). If this ellipse touches the line, \(x+6y=8\); then its eccentricity is
questions.sol: \(b^2=\tfrac43\); tangency of \(y=-\tfrac x6+\tfrac43\): \(\tfrac{16}9=\tfrac{a^2}{36}+\tfrac43\), so \(a^2=16\) and \(e^2=\tfrac{11}{12}\).

questions.q: If the tangents on the ellipse \(4x^2+y^2=8\) at the points \((1,2)\) and \((a,b)\) are perpendicular to each other, then \(a^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: The slopes are \(-2\) and \(-\tfrac{4a}b\), so \(b=-8a\); then \(4a^2+64a^2=8\).

questions.q: In an ellipse, with centre at the origin, if the difference of the lengths of major axis and minor axis is \(10\) and one of the foci is at \((0,5\sqrt3)\), then the length of its latus rectum is
questions.sol: The semi-axes satisfy \(B-A=5\), \(B^2-A^2=75\): \(B=10\), \(A=5\); latus rectum \(\tfrac{2A^2}B\).

questions.q: If the tangent to the parabola \(y^2=x\) at a point \((\alpha,\beta)\), \((\beta>0)\) is also a tangent to the ellipse, \(x^2+2y^2=1\), then \(\alpha\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac1{4m}\) with \(\tfrac1{16m^2}=m^2+\tfrac12\): \(m^2=\tfrac{\sqrt2-1}4\), and \(\alpha=\tfrac1{4m^2}\).

questions.q: If the line \(x-2y=12\) is tangent to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) at the point \(\left(3,\dfrac{-9}2\right)\), then the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse is
questions.sol: Comparing \(\tfrac{3x}{a^2}-\tfrac{9y}{2b^2}=1\) with \(\tfrac x{12}-\tfrac y6=1\): \(a^2=36\), \(b^2=27\).

questions.q: The tangent and normal to the ellipse \(3x^2+5y^2=32\) at the point \(P(2,2)\) meet the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\) and \(R\), respectively. Then the area (in sq. units) of the triangle \(PQR\) is
questions.sol: Tangent \(3x+5y=16\) gives \(Q\left(\tfrac{16}3,0\right)\); the normal (slope \(\tfrac53\)) gives \(R\left(\tfrac45,0\right)\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{68}{15}\cdot2\).

questions.q: If the normal to the ellipse \(3x^2+4y^2=12\) at a point \(P\) on it is parallel to the line, \(2x+y=4\) and the tangent to the ellipse at \(P\) passes through \(Q(4,4)\) then \(PQ\) is equal to
questions.sol: The normal at \((2\cos\theta,\sqrt3\sin\theta)\) has slope \(\tfrac2{\sqrt3}\tan\theta=-2\), and the tangent through \((4,4)\) selects \(\theta=120^\circ\): \(P\left(-1,\tfrac32\right)\).

questions.q: An ellipse, with foci at \((0,2)\) and \((0,-2)\) and minor axis of length \(4\), passes through which of the following points?

If tangents are drawn to the ellipse \(x^2+2y^2=2\) at all points on the ellipse other than its four vertices, then the mid points of the tangents intercepted between the coordinate axes lie on the curve
questions.sol: The midpoint is \(\left(\tfrac1{\sqrt2\cos\theta},\tfrac1{2\sin\theta}\right)\).

questions.q: Let the length of the latus rectum of an ellipse with its major axis along \(x\)-axis and centre at the origin, be \(8\). If the distance between the foci of this ellipse is equal to the length of its minor axis, then which one of the following points lies on it?
questions.sol: \(ae=b\) gives \(a^2=2b^2\); with \(b^2=4a\): \(a=8\), \(b^2=32\). \((4\sqrt3,2\sqrt2)\) gives \(\tfrac{48}{64}+\tfrac8{32}=1\). (The book key prints (d).)

questions.q: Let \(S\) and \(S'\) be the foci of an ellipse and \(B\) be any one of the extremities of its minor axis. If \(\Delta S'BS\) is a right angled triangle with right angle at \(B\) and area \((\Delta S'BS)=8\) sq. units, then the length of a latus rectum of the ellipse is
questions.sol: The right angle at \(B\) means \(b=c\); area \(c^2=8\), so \(b^2=8\), \(a^2=16\).

questions.q: If \(\beta\) is one of the angles between the normals to the ellipse, \(x^2+3y^2=9\) at the points \((3\cos\theta,\sqrt3\sin\theta)\) and \((-3\sin\theta,\sqrt3\cos\theta)\); \(\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), then \(\dfrac{2\cot\beta}{\sin2\theta}\) is equal to
questions.sol: The normal slopes are \(\sqrt3\tan\theta\) and \(-\sqrt3\cot\theta\), so \(\tan\beta=\dfrac{\sqrt3(\tan\theta+\cot\theta)}2=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\sin2\theta}\).

questions.q: If the length of the latus rectum of an ellipse is \(4\) units and the distance between a focus and its nearest vertex on the major axis is \(\dfrac32\) units, then its eccentricity is
The eccentricity of an ellipse whose centre is at the origin is \(\dfrac12\). If one of its directrices is \(x=-4\), then the equation of the normal to it at \(\left(1,\dfrac32\right)\) is

Consider an ellipse, whose centre is at the origin and its major axis is along the \(x\)-axis. If its eccentricity is \(\dfrac35\) and the distance between its foci is \(6\), then the area (in sq. units) of the quadrilateral inscribed in the ellipse, with the vertices as the vertices of the ellipse, is
questions.sol: \(a=5\), \(b=4\); the rhombus has area \(2ab\).

questions.q: The eccentricity of an ellipse having centre at the origin, axes along the co-ordinate axes and passing through the points \((4,-1)\) and \((-2,2)\) is

If the tangent at a point on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{27}+\dfrac{y^2}3=1\) meets the coordinate axes at \(A\) and \(B\), and \(O\) is the origin, then the minimum area (in sq. units) of the triangle \(OAB\) is
questions.sol: The area is \(\tfrac{ab}{\sin2\theta}\ge ab=9\).

questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the quadrilateral formed by the tangents at the end points of the latus rectum to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}5=1\), is
questions.sol: The tangents at \(\left(2,\pm\tfrac53\right)\) meet the axes at \(\left(\tfrac92,0\right)\) and \((0,\pm3)\); the rhombus has area \(2\cdot\tfrac92\cdot3\).

questions.q: If the distance between the foci of an ellipse is half the length of its latus rectum, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.sol: \(2ae=\tfrac{b^2}a\) gives \(e^2+2e-1=0\).

questions.q: The locus of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the centre of the ellipse \(x^2+3y^2=6\) on any tangent to it is
questions.sol: The foot \((h,k)\) lies on the tangent \(hx+ky=h^2+k^2\), and the tangency condition is \((h^2+k^2)^2=a^2h^2+b^2k^2\).

questions.q: The equation of the circle passing through the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) and having centre at \((0,3)\) is
questions.sol: The foci are \((\pm\sqrt7,0)\), so \(r^2=7+9\).

questions.q:
Statement 1 : An equation of a common tangent to the parabola \(y^2=16\sqrt3x\) and the ellipse \(2x^2+y^2=4\) is \(y=2x+2\sqrt3\)
Statement 2 : If the line \(y=mx+\dfrac{4\sqrt3}m\), \((m\ne0)\) is a common tangent to the parabola \(y^2=16\sqrt3x\) and the ellipse \(2x^2+y^2=4\), then \(m\) satisfies \(m^4+2m^2=24\).
opts: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true; Statement 2 is not a correct explanation for Statement 1.
Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true; Statement 2 is a correct explanation for Statement 1.

questions.q: An ellipse is drawn by taking a diameter of the circle \((x-1)^2+y^2=1\) as its semi-minor axis and a diameter of the circle \(x^2+(y-2)^2=4\) as its semi-major axis. If the centre of the ellipse is at the origin and its axes are the coordinate axes, then the equation of the ellipse is
Equation of the ellipse whose axes are the axes of coordinates and which passes through the point \((-3,1)\) and has eccentricity \(\sqrt{\dfrac25}\) is

The ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=4\) is inscribed in a rectangle aligned with the coordinate axes, which in turn is inscribed in another ellipse that passes through the point \((4,0)\). Then the equation of the ellipse is
questions.sol: The rectangle has corners \((\pm2,\pm1)\); \(\tfrac{x^2}{16}+\tfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) through \((2,1)\) gives \(b^2=\tfrac43\).

questions.q: A focus of an ellipse is at the origin. The directrix is the line \(x=4\) and the eccentricity is \(\dfrac12\). Then the length of the semi-major axis is
questions.sol: Focus-to-directrix distance \(\tfrac ae-ae=2a-\tfrac a2=4\).

questions.q: In an ellipse, the distance between its foci is \(6\) and minor axis is \(8\). Then its eccentricity is,
An ellipse has \(OB\) as semi minor axis, \(F\) and \(F'\) its foci and the angle \(FBF'\) is a right angle. Then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
The eccentricity of an ellipse, with its centre at the origin, is \(1/2\). If one of the directrices is \(x=4\), then the equation of the ellipse is

Let \(C\) be the circle \(x^2+(y-1)^2=2\), \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) be two ellipses whose centres lie at the origin and major axes lie on \(x\)-axis and \(y\)-axis respectively. Let the straight line \(x+y=3\) touch the curves \(C\), \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) at \(P(x_1,y_1)\), \(Q(x_2,y_2)\) and \(R(x_3,y_3)\) respectively. Given that \(P\) is the mid point of the line segment \(QR\) and \(PQ=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}3\), the value of \(9(x_1y_1+x_2y_2+x_3y_3)\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(P=(1,2)\). On the line, \(PQ=\sqrt2|x_2-1|\), so \(x_2=\tfrac53\) (for \(E_1\) the contact point \(\left(\tfrac{a^2}3,\tfrac{b^2}3\right)\) has \(x>y\)): \(Q\left(\tfrac53,\tfrac43\right)\), \(R\left(\tfrac13,\tfrac83\right)\). Sum \(9\left(2+\tfrac{20}9+\tfrac89\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(E_1:\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) be an ellipse. Ellipse \(E_i\)'s are constructed such that their centres and eccentricities are same as that of \(E_1\), and the length of minor axis of \(E_i\) is the length of major axis of \(E_{i+1}\) \((i\ge1)\). If \(A_i\) is the area of the ellipse \(E_i\), then \(\dfrac5\pi\left(\sum_{i=1}^\infty A_i\right)\), is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(a_{i+1}=b_i=\tfrac23a_i\), so \(A_i=\tfrac23\pi a_i^2\) and \(\sum a_i^2=\tfrac{9}{1-4/9}=\tfrac{81}5\). \(\sum A_i=\tfrac{54\pi}5\).

questions.q: If the points of intersection of two distinct conics \(x^2+y^2=4b\) and \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) lie on the curve \(y^2=3x\), then \(3\sqrt3\) times the area of the rectangle formed by the intersection points is ________.
questions.sol: The intersections are \(x^2=\tfrac{16b}{b+4}\), \(y^2=\tfrac{4b^2}{b+4}\), symmetric in both axes, so the points with \(x<0\) can never lie on \(y^2=3x\): the conditions are inconsistent. (The NTA key gives 432; treated as bonus.)

questions.q: Let an ellipse with centre \((1,0)\) and latus rectum of length \(\dfrac12\) have its major axis along \(x\)-axis. If its minor axis subtends an angle \(60^\circ\) at the foci, then the square of the sum of the lengths of its minor and major axes is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(\tan30^\circ=\tfrac bc\) gives \(c=\sqrt3b\), \(a=2b\); \(\tfrac{2b^2}a=\tfrac12\) gives \(a=1\), \(b=\tfrac12\). \((2a+2b)^2=9\).

questions.q: The line \(x=8\) is the directrix of the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) with the corresponding focus \((2,0)\). If the tangent to \(E\) at the point \(P\) in the first quadrant passes through the point \((0,4\sqrt3)\) and intersects the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\), then \((3PQ)^2\) is equal to ________.
Let \(C\) be the largest circle centred at \((2,0)\) and inscribed in the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{36}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\). If \((1,\alpha)\) lies on \(C\), then \(10\alpha^2\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: The squared distance from \((2,0)\) to \((6\cos t,4\sin t)\) is \(20\cos^2t-24\cos t+20\), minimum \(12.8\) at \(\cos t=0.6\). \(1+\alpha^2=12.8\).

questions.q: Let a tangent to the curve \(9x^2+16y^2=144\) intersect the coordinate axes at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Then, the minimum length of the line segment \(AB\) is ________.
questions.sol: \(AB^2=\tfrac{16}{\cos^2\theta}+\tfrac9{\sin^2\theta}\ge(4+3)^2\).

questions.q: If the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse \(x^2+4y^2+2x+8y-\lambda=0\) is \(4\), and \(l\) is the length of its major axis, then \(\lambda+l\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \((x+1)^2+4(y+1)^2=\lambda+5\); latus rectum \(\tfrac{\sqrt{\lambda+5}}2=4\) gives \(\lambda=59\) and \(l=16\).

questions.q: Let the tangents at the points \(P\) and \(Q\) on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}2+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) meet at the point \(R(\sqrt2,2\sqrt2-2)\). If \(S\) is the focus of the ellipse on its negative major axis, then \(SP^2+SQ^2\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(S=(0,-\sqrt2)\). The chord of contact \(\tfrac x{\sqrt2}+\tfrac{(\sqrt2-1)y}2=1\) meets the ellipse at \(P(\sqrt2,0)\) and \(Q(1,\sqrt2)\): \(SP^2=4\), \(SQ^2=1+8\).

questions.q: If two tangents drawn from a point \((\alpha,\beta)\) lying on the ellipse \(25x^2+4y^2=1\) to the parabola \(y^2=4x\) are such that the slope of one tangent is four times the other, then the value of \((10\alpha+5)^2+(16\beta^2+50)^2\) equals ________.
questions.sol: \(m^2\alpha-m\beta+1=0\) with roots \(4m,m\) gives \(4\beta^2=25\alpha\); with the ellipse, \(25\alpha^2+25\alpha=1\). Then \((10\alpha+5)^2=4+25\) and \((100\alpha+50)^2=2500(4\alpha^2+4\alpha+1)=2900\).

questions.q: Let the common tangents to the curves \(4(x^2+y^2)=9\) and \(y^2=4x\) intersect at the point \(Q\). Let an ellipse, centered at the origin \(O\), has lengths of semi-minor and semi-major axes equal to \(OQ\) and \(6\), respectively. If \(e\) and \(l\) respectively denote the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of this ellipse, then \(\dfrac l{e^2}\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac1m\) at distance \(\tfrac32\): \(9m^4+9m^2-4=0\), \(m^2=\tfrac13\); the tangents meet at \(\left(-\tfrac1{m^2},0\right)=(-3,0)\). \(b=3\), \(a=6\): \(l=3\), \(e^2=\tfrac34\).

questions.q: If the minimum area of the triangle formed by a tangent to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{b^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{4a^2}=1\) and the co-ordinate axis is \(kab\), then \(k\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: Minimum area is the product of the semi-axes, \(b\cdot2a\).

questions.q: Let \(E\) be an ellipse whose axes are parallel to the co-ordinates axes, having its center at \((3,-4)\), one focus at \((4,-4)\) and one vertex at \((5,-4)\). If \(mx-y=4\), \(m>0\) is a tangent to the ellipse \(E\), then the value of \(5m^2\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(a=2\), \(c=1\), \(b^2=3\). Shifting the centre to the origin, the line becomes \(Y=mX+3m\); tangency: \(9m^2=4m^2+3\).

questions.q: Let \(L\) be a common tangent line to the curves \(4x^2+9y^2=36\) and \((2x)^2+(2y)^2=31\). Then the square of the slope of the line \(L\) is ________.

Let one focus of the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be at \((\sqrt{10},0)\) and the corresponding directrix be \(x=\dfrac9{\sqrt{10}}\). If \(e\) and \(l\) respectively are the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of \(H\), then \(9(e^2+l)\) is equal to :

Let the sum of the focal distances of the point \(P(4,3)\) on the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be \(8\sqrt{\dfrac53}\). If for \(H\), the length of the latus rectum is \(l\) and the product of the focal distances of the point \(P\) is \(m\), then \(9l^2+6m\) is equal to :
questions.sol: The focal distances are \(ex\pm a\), so their sum \(8e\) gives \(e^2=\tfrac53\), \(b^2=\tfrac23a^2\); through \(P\): \(a^2=\tfrac52\), \(b^2=\tfrac53\). \(l^2=\tfrac{4b^4}{a^2}=\tfrac{40}9\), \(m=16e^2-a^2=\tfrac{145}6\).

questions.q: Let \(e_1\) and \(e_2\) be the eccentricities of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{b^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{25}=1\) and the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), respectively. If \(b<5\) and \(e_1e_2=1\), then the eccentricity of the ellipse having its axes along the coordinate axes and passing through all four foci (two of the ellipse and two of the hyperbola) is :
Let the foci of a hyperbola be \((1,14)\) and \((1,-12)\). If it passes through the point \((1,6)\), then the length of its latus-rectum is :
questions.sol: Centre \((1,1)\), \(c=13\); \((1,6)\) is on the axis, so it is a vertex: \(a=5\), \(b^2=144\).

questions.q: Let \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\) and \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{B^2}=1\). Let the distance between the foci of \(E\) and the foci of \(H\) be \(2\sqrt3\). If \(a-A=2\), and the ratio of the eccentricities of \(E\) and \(H\) is \(\dfrac13\), then the sum of the lengths of their latus rectums is equal to :
questions.sol: Both focal distances are \(2\sqrt3\), so \(ae=AE=\sqrt3\) and \(\tfrac eE=\tfrac Aa=\tfrac13\): \(A=1\), \(a=3\), \(b^2=6\), \(B^2=2\). Sum \(\tfrac{12}3+\tfrac41\).

questions.q: If \(A\) and \(B\) are the points of intersection of the circle \(x^2+y^2-8x=0\) and the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) and a point \(P\) moves on the line \(2x-3y+4=0\), then the centroid of \(\Delta PAB\) lies on the line :

Consider a hyperbola \(H\) having centre at the origin and foci on the \(x\)-axis. Let \(C_1\) be the circle touching the hyperbola \(H\) and having the centre at the origin. Let \(C_2\) be the circle touching the hyperbola \(H\) at its vertex and having the centre at one of its foci. If areas (in sq. units) of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are \(36\pi\) and \(4\pi\), respectively, then the length (in units) of latus rectum of \(H\) is

Let \(H:\dfrac{-x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be the hyperbola, whose eccentricity is \(\sqrt3\) and the length of the latus rectum is \(4\sqrt3\). Suppose the point \((\alpha,6)\), \(\alpha>0\) lies on \(H\). If \(\beta\) is the product of the focal distances of the point \((\alpha,6)\), then \(\alpha^2+\beta\) is equal to

Let the foci of a hyperbola \(H\) coincide with the foci of the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{100}+\dfrac{(y-1)^2}{75}=1\) and the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(H\) be the reciprocal of the eccentricity of the ellipse \(E\). If the length of the transverse axis of \(H\) is \(\alpha\) and the length of its conjugate axis is \(\beta\), then \(3\alpha^2+2\beta^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: For \(E\): \(e=\tfrac12\), \(c=5\). For \(H\): \(e=2\), so the semi-axes are \(\tfrac52\) and \(\tfrac{5\sqrt3}2\): \(\alpha^2=25\), \(\beta^2=75\).

questions.q: For \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), if the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(x^2-y^2\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta=5\) is \(\sqrt7\) times eccentricity of the ellipse \(x^2\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta+y^2=5\), then the value of \(\theta\) is
questions.sol: \(e_H^2=1+\sin^2\theta\) and \(e_E^2=\cos^2\theta\); \(1+\sin^2\theta=7-7\sin^2\theta\) gives \(\sin^2\theta=\tfrac34\).

questions.q: Let \(e_1\) be the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) and \(e_2\) be the eccentricity of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\), which passes through the foci of the hyperbola. If \(e_1e_2=1\), then the length of the chord of the ellipse parallel to the \(x\)-axis and passing through \((0,2)\) is
questions.sol: \(e_1=\tfrac54\), so \(e_2=\tfrac45\); the ellipse passes through \((\pm5,0)\): \(a=5\), \(b^2=9\). At \(y=2\): \(x^2=25\cdot\tfrac59\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a point on the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) in the first quadrant such that the area of triangle formed by \(P\) and the two foci of \(H\) is \(2\sqrt{13}\). Then, the square of the distance of \(P\) from the origin is
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12\cdot2\sqrt{13}\cdot y=2\sqrt{13}\) gives \(y=2\), then \(x^2=18\).

questions.q: If the foci of a hyperbola are same as that of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}{25}=1\) and the eccentricity of the hyperbola is \(\dfrac{15}8\) times the eccentricity of the ellipse, then the smaller focal distance of the point \(\left(\sqrt2,\dfrac{14}3\sqrt{\dfrac25}\right)\) on the hyperbola, is equal to
questions.sol: Foci \((0,\pm4)\), \(e=\tfrac32\), so the transverse semi-axis (along \(y\)) is \(\tfrac83\). Smaller focal distance \(ey-\tfrac83\).

questions.q: Let \(P(x_0,y_0)\) be the point on the hyperbola \(3x^2-4y^2=36\), which is nearest to the line \(3x+2y=1\). Then \(\sqrt2(y_0-x_0)\) is equal to
questions.sol: The tangent at \(P\) is parallel to the line: \(\tfrac{3x_0}{4y_0}=-\tfrac32\), so \(x_0=-2y_0\) and \(y_0^2=\tfrac92\). The nearer one is \(\left(\tfrac6{\sqrt2},-\tfrac3{\sqrt2}\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(T\) and \(C\) respectively be the transverse and conjugate axes of the hyperbola \(16x^2-y^2+64x+4y+44=0\). Then the area of the region above the parabola \(x^2=y+4\), below the transverse axis \(T\) and on the right of the conjugate axis \(C\) is:

Let the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}7=1\) and the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{144}-\dfrac{y^2}\alpha=\dfrac1{25}\) coincide. Then the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola is :

Let the tangent drawn to the parabola \(y^2=24x\) at the point \((\alpha,\beta)\) is perpendicular to the line \(2x+2y=5\). Then the normal to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{\alpha^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{\beta^2}=1\) at the point \((\alpha+4,\beta+4)\) does not pass through the point :
If the line \(x-1=0\) is a directrix of the hyperbola \(kx^2-y^2=6\), then the hyperbola passes through the point

Let the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) pass through the point \((2\sqrt2,-2\sqrt2)\). A parabola is drawn whose focus is same as the focus of \(H\) with positive abscissa and the directrix of the parabola passes through the other focus of \(H\). If the length of the latus rectum of the parabola is \(e\) times the length of the latus rectum of \(H\), where \(e\) is the eccentricity of \(H\), then which of the following points lies on the parabola?
questions.sol: The parabola's latus rectum is \(4ae=e\cdot\tfrac{2b^2}a\), so \(b^2=2a^2\); then \(a^2=4\), \(c=2\sqrt3\) and the parabola is \(y^2=8\sqrt3x\).

questions.q: Let the focal chord of the parabola \(P:y^2=4x\) along the line \(L:y=mx+c\), \(m>0\) meet the parabola at the points \(M\) and \(N\). Let the line \(L\) be a tangent to the hyperbola \(H:x^2-y^2=4\). If \(O\) is the vertex of \(P\) and \(F\) is the focus of \(H\) on the positive \(x\)-axis, then the area of the quadrilateral \(OMFN\) is :
questions.sol: \(c=-m\) and \(m^2=4m^2-4\): \(m^2=\tfrac43\). \(|y_M-y_N|=4\sqrt{1+\tfrac1{m^2}}=2\sqrt7\); area \(\tfrac12\cdot2\sqrt2\cdot2\sqrt7\).

questions.q: Let \(\lambda x-2y=\mu\) be a tangent to the hyperbola \(a^2x^2-y^2=b^2\). Then \(\left(\dfrac\lambda a\right)^2-\left(\dfrac\mu b\right)^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(\tfrac{\mu^2}4=\tfrac{b^2}{a^2}\cdot\tfrac{\lambda^2}4-b^2\).

questions.q: The normal to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) at the point \((8,3\sqrt3)\) on it passes through the point.

Let the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be \(\sqrt{\dfrac52}\) and length of its latus rectum be \(6\sqrt2\). If \(y=2x+c\) is a tangent to the hyperbola \(H\), then the value of \(c^2\) is equal to

Let \(a>0\), \(b>0\). Let \(e\) and \(l\) respectively be the eccentricity and length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). Let \(e'\) and \(l'\) respectively be the eccentricity and length of the latus rectum of its conjugate hyperbola. If \(e^2=\dfrac{11}{14}l\) and \((e')^2=\dfrac{11}8l'\), then the value of \(77a+44b\) is equal to :

The point \(P(-2\sqrt6,\sqrt3)\) lies on the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) having eccentricity \(\dfrac{\sqrt5}2\). If the tangent and normal at \(P\) to the hyperbola intersect its conjugate axis at the points \(Q\) and \(R\) respectively, then \(QR\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(b^2=\tfrac{a^2}4\) gives \(a^2=12\), \(b^2=3\). The tangent meets \(x=0\) at \(-\tfrac{b^2}{y_0}=-\sqrt3\), the normal at \(\tfrac{(a^2+b^2)y_0}{b^2}=5\sqrt3\).

questions.q: The locus of the mid points of the chords of the hyperbola \(x^2-y^2=4\), which touch the parabola \(y^2=8x\), is
questions.sol: The chord \(hx-ky=h^2-k^2\) has slope \(\tfrac hk\) and intercept \(-\tfrac{h^2-k^2}k\); tangency \(c=\tfrac2m\) gives \(k^2(h-2)=h^3\).

questions.q: Let a line \(L:2x+y=k\), \(k>0\) be a tangent to the hyperbola \(x^2-y^2=3\). If \(L\) is also a tangent to the parabola \(y^2=\alpha x\), then \(\alpha\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(k^2=3\cdot4-3\) gives \(k=3\); for the parabola \(3=\tfrac\alpha{4(-2)}\).

questions.q: The locus of the centroid of the triangle formed by any point \(P\) on the hyperbola \(16x^2-9y^2+32x+36y-164=0\), and its foci is
The locus of the midpoints of the chord of the circle, \(x^2+y^2=25\) which is tangent to the hyperbola, \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\) is
questions.sol: The chord \(hx+ky=h^2+k^2\); tangency \(c^2=9m^2-16\) gives \((h^2+k^2)^2=9h^2-16k^2\).

questions.q: Consider a hyperbola \(H:x^2-2y^2=4\). Let the tangent at a point \(P(4,\sqrt6)\) meet the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\) and latus rectum at \(R(x_1,y_1)\), \(x_1>0\). If \(F\) is a focus of \(H\) which is nearer to the point \(P\), then the area of \(\Delta QFR\) is equal to
questions.sol: Tangent \(x-\tfrac{\sqrt6}2y=1\): \(Q(1,0)\), \(F(\sqrt6,0)\), \(R\left(\sqrt6,\tfrac{2(\sqrt6-1)}{\sqrt6}\right)\). Area \(\tfrac{(\sqrt6-1)^2}{\sqrt6}\).

questions.q: A hyperbola passes through the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\) and its transverse and conjugate axes coincide with major and minor axes of the ellipse, respectively. If the product of their eccentricities is one, then the equation of the hyperbola is
questions.sol: The ellipse has foci \((\pm3,0)\), \(e=\tfrac35\). The hyperbola: \(a=3\), \(e=\tfrac53\), \(b^2=16\).

questions.q: A line parallel to the straight line \(2x-y=0\) is tangent to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}4-\dfrac{y^2}2=1\) at the point \((x_1,y_1)\). Then \(x_1^2+5y_1^2\) is equal to
questions.sol: Tangent slope \(\tfrac{x_1}{2y_1}=2\) gives \(x_1=4y_1\), \(y_1^2=\tfrac27\), \(x_1^2=\tfrac{32}7\).

questions.q: For some \(\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), if the eccentricity of the hyperbola, \(x^2-y^2\sec^2\theta=10\) is \(\sqrt5\) times the eccentricity of the ellipse, \(x^2\sec^2\theta+y^2=5\), then the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse, is
questions.sol: \(e_H^2=1+\cos^2\theta\), \(e_E^2=\sin^2\theta\): \(\cos^2\theta=\tfrac23\). Latus rectum \(\tfrac{2\cdot5\cos^2\theta}{\sqrt5}\).

questions.q: A hyperbola having the transverse axis of length \(\sqrt2\) has the same foci as that of the ellipse \(3x^2+4y^2=12\), then this hyperbola does not pass through which of the following points?

Let \(P(3,3)\) be a point on the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). If the normal to it at \(P\) intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((9,0)\) and \(e\) is its eccentricity, then the ordered pair \((a^2,e^2)\) is equal to
questions.sol: The normal meets the \(x\)-axis at \(e^2x_1=9\), so \(e^2=3\), \(b^2=2a^2\); through \((3,3)\): \(a^2=\tfrac92\).

questions.q: If the line \(y=mx+c\) is a common tangent to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{100}-\dfrac{y^2}{64}=1\) and the circle \(x^2+y^2=36\), then which one of the following is true?
