If \(e_1\) and \(e_2\) are the eccentricities of the ellipse, \(\dfrac{x^2}{18}+\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) and the hyperbola, \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) respectively and \((e_1,e_2)\) is a point on the ellipse, \(15x^2+3y^2=k\), then \(k\) is equal to
If the eccentricity of the standard hyperbola passing through the point \((4,6)\) is \(2\), then the equation of the tangent to the hyperbola at \((4,6)\) is
If the line \(y=mx+7\sqrt3\) is normal to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{24}-\dfrac{y^2}{18}=1\), then a value of \(m\) is
questions.sol: Normal condition \(c=\tfrac{m(a^2+b^2)}{\sqrt{a^2-b^2m^2}}\): \(7\sqrt3\sqrt{24-18m^2}=42m\), so \(m^2=\tfrac45\).

questions.q: If a directrix of a hyperbola centred at the origin and passing through the point \((4,-2\sqrt3)\) is \(5x=4\sqrt5\) and its eccentricity is \(e\), then
If \(5x+9=0\) is the directrix of the hyperbola \(16x^2-9y^2=144\), then its corresponding focus is
questions.sol: \(a=3\), \(e=\tfrac53\); the directrix \(x=-\tfrac95\) goes with the focus \((-ae,0)\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be the point of intersection of the common tangents to the parabola \(y^2=12x\) and the hyperbola \(8x^2-y^2=8\). If \(S\) and \(S'\) denote the foci of the hyperbola where \(S\) lies on the positive \(x\)-axis, then \(P\) divides \(SS'\) in a ratio
questions.sol: \(\tfrac9{m^2}=m^2-8\) gives \(m^2=9\); the tangents \(y=\pm(3x+1)\) meet at \(P\left(-\tfrac13,0\right)\). \(SP:PS'=\tfrac{10}3:\tfrac83\).

questions.q: Let \(0<\theta<\dfrac\pi2\). If the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{\cos^2\theta}-\dfrac{y^2}{\sin^2\theta}=1\) is greater than \(2\), then the length of its latus rectum lies in the interval
questions.sol: \(e=\sec\theta>2\) means \(\cos\theta<\tfrac12\); the latus rectum \(\tfrac{2\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\) is decreasing in \(\cos\theta\) and equals \(3\) at \(\tfrac12\).

questions.q: A hyperbola has its centre at the origin, passes through the point \((4,2)\) and has transverse axis of length \(4\) along the \(x\)-axis. Then the eccentricity of the hyperbola is
The equation of a tangent to the hyperbola \(4x^2-5y^2=20\) parallel to the line \(x-y=2\) is
Let \(S=\left\{(x,y)\in R^2:\dfrac{y^2}{1+r}-\dfrac{x^2}{1-r}=1\right\}\) where \(r\ne\pm1\). Then \(S\) represents
opts: a hyperbola whose eccentricity is \(\dfrac2{\sqrt{r+1}}\), when \(0<r<1\).
a hyperbola whose eccentricity is \(\dfrac2{\sqrt{1-r}}\), when \(0<r<1\).
an ellipse whose eccentricity is \(\dfrac1{\sqrt{r+1}}\), when \(r>1\).
an ellipse whose eccentricity is \(\sqrt{\dfrac2{r+1}}\), when \(r>1\).
questions.sol: For \(r>1\): \(\tfrac{y^2}{r+1}+\tfrac{x^2}{r-1}=1\) with \(e^2=1-\tfrac{r-1}{r+1}\). (For \(0<r<1\) the hyperbola has \(e=\sqrt{\tfrac2{1+r}}\).)

questions.q: Equation of a common tangent to the parabola \(y^2=4x\) and the hyperbola \(xy=2\) is
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\tfrac1m\) in \(xy=2\): discriminant \(\tfrac1{m^2}+8m=0\), \(m=-\tfrac12\).

questions.q: If a hyperbola has length of its conjugate axis equal to \(5\) and the distance between its foci is \(13\), then the eccentricity of the hyperbola is
If the vertices of a hyperbola be at \((-2,0)\) and \((2,0)\) and one of its foci be at \((-3,0)\), then which one of the following points does not lie on this hyperbola?
Tangents are drawn to the hyperbola \(4x^2-y^2=36\) at the points \(P\) and \(Q\). If these tangents intersect at the point \(T(0,3)\), then the area (in sq. units) of \(\Delta PTQ\) is
questions.sol: The chord of contact is \(y=-12\), giving \(x=\pm3\sqrt5\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot6\sqrt5\cdot15\).

questions.q: If the tangent drawn to the hyperbola \(4y^2=x^2+1\) intersect the co-ordinate axes at the distinct points \(A\) and \(B\), then the locus of the mid point of \(AB\) is
questions.sol: The tangent \(4yy_1-xx_1=1\) has midpoint \(\left(-\tfrac1{2x_1},\tfrac1{8y_1}\right)\); substituting into \(4y_1^2-x_1^2=1\) gives \(\tfrac1{16k^2}-\tfrac1{4h^2}=1\).

questions.q: A normal to the hyperbola, \(4x^2-9y^2=36\) meets the co-ordinate axes \(x\) and \(y\) at \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. If the parallelogram \(OABP\) (\(O\) being the origin) is formed, then the locus of \(P\) is
questions.sol: The normal at \((3\sec\theta,2\tan\theta)\) is \(3x\cos\theta+2y\cot\theta=13\), so \(P=\left(\tfrac{13}3\sec\theta,\tfrac{13}2\tan\theta\right)\).

questions.q: The locus of the point of intersection of the lines, \(\sqrt2x-y+4\sqrt2k=0\) and \(\sqrt2kx+ky-4\sqrt2=0\) (\(k\) is any non-zero real parameter), is
opts: a hyperbola with length of its transverse axis \(8\sqrt2\).
an ellipse with length of its major axis \(8\sqrt2\).
questions.sol: Eliminating \(k\): \((y-\sqrt2x)(y+\sqrt2x)=32\), i.e. \(\tfrac{y^2}{32}-\tfrac{x^2}{16}=1\).

questions.q: A hyperbola passes through the point \(P(\sqrt2,\sqrt3)\) and has foci at \((\pm2,0)\). Then the tangent to this hyperbola at \(P\) also passes through the point
questions.sol: \(a^2=1\), \(b^2=3\); tangent \(\sqrt2x-\tfrac y{\sqrt3}=1\).

questions.q: The locus of the point of intersection of the straight lines, \(tx-2y-3t=0\) and \(x-2ty+3=0\) \((t\in R)\), is
opts: a hyperbola with the length of conjugate axis \(3\)
an ellipse with the length of major axis \(6\)

questions.q: The eccentricity of the hyperbola whose length of the latus rectum is equal to \(8\) and the length of its conjugate axis is equal to half of the distance between its foci, is

Let \(a\) and \(b\) respectively be the semi-transverse and semi-conjugate axes of a hyperbola whose eccentricity satisfies the equation \(9e^2-18e+5=0\). If \(S(5,0)\) is a focus and \(5x=9\) is the corresponding directrix of this hyperbola, then \(a^2-b^2\) is equal to

A hyperbola whose transverse axis is along the major axis of the conic \(\dfrac{x^2}3+\dfrac{y^2}4=4\), and has vertices at the foci of this conic. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is \(\dfrac32\), then which of the following points does not lie on it?
questions.sol: The conic \(\tfrac{x^2}{12}+\tfrac{y^2}{16}=1\) has foci \((0,\pm2)\), so the hyperbola is \(\tfrac{y^2}4-\tfrac{x^2}5=1\).

questions.q: An ellipse passes through the foci of the hyperbola, \(9x^2-4y^2=36\) and its major and minor axes lie along the transverse and conjugate axes of the hyperbola respectively. If the product of eccentricities of the two conics is \(1/2\), then which of the following points does not lie on the ellipse?
questions.sol: The hyperbola has \(e=\tfrac{\sqrt{13}}2\) and foci \((\pm\sqrt{13},0)\); the ellipse has \(a^2=13\), \(e^2=\tfrac1{13}\), \(b^2=12\).

questions.q: The normal to a curve at \(P(x,y)\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(G\). If the distance of \(G\) from the origin is twice the abscissa of \(P\), then the curve is a
questions.sol: \(G=(x+yy',0)\), so \(x+yy'=\pm2x\). \(yy'=x\) gives \(y^2-x^2=c\) (hyperbola); \(yy'=-3x\) gives \(3x^2+y^2=c\) (ellipse). (The book key gives (b), (c).)

questions.q: For the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{\cos^2\alpha}-\dfrac{y^2}{\sin^2\alpha}=1\), which of the following remains constant when \(\alpha\) varies ?
questions.sol: \(c^2=\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha=1\).

questions.q: The locus of a point \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) moving under the condition that the line \(y=\alpha x+\beta\) is a tangent to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) is
The foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) and the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{144}-\dfrac{y^2}{81}=\dfrac1{25}\) coincide. Then the value of \(b^2\) is
questions.sol: The hyperbola has \(c^2=\tfrac{144+81}{25}=9\), so \(16-b^2=9\).

questions.q: Let the product of focal distances of the point \(P(4,2\sqrt3)\) on the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be \(32\). Let the length of the conjugate axis of \(H\) be \(p\) and the length of its latus rectum be \(q\). Then \(p^2+q^2\) is equal to ________.
If the equation of the hyperbola with foci \((4,2)\) and \((8,2)\) is \(3x^2-y^2-\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0\), then \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma\) is equal to ________.

Consider the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) having one of its focus at \(P(-3,0)\). If the latus rectum through its other focus subtends a right angle at \(P\) and \(a^2b^2=\alpha\sqrt2-\beta\), \(\alpha,\beta\in N\), then \(\alpha+\beta\) is ________.
questions.sol: The right angle at \(P\) gives \(\tfrac{b^2}a=6\), so \(a^2+6a=9\), \(a=3(\sqrt2-1)\). \(a^2b^2=6a^3=162(5\sqrt2-7)\).

questions.q: Let the lengths of the transverse and conjugate axes of a hyperbola in standard form be \(2a\) and \(2b\), respectively, and one focus and the corresponding directrix of this hyperbola be \((-5,0)\) and \(5x+9=0\), respectively. If the product of the focal distances of a point \((\alpha,2\sqrt5)\) on the hyperbola is \(p\), then \(4p\) is equal to ________.

Let the circle \(C\) touch the line \(x-y+1=0\), have the centre on the positive \(x\)-axis, and cut off a chord of length \(\dfrac4{\sqrt{13}}\) along the line \(-3x+2y=1\). Let \(H\) be the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{\alpha^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{\beta^2}=1\), whose one of the foci is the centre of \(C\) and the length of the transverse axis is the diameter of \(C\). Then \(2\alpha^2+3\beta^2\) is equal to ________.

Let \(H_1:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) and \(H_2:-\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{B^2}=1\) be two hyperbolas having length of latus rectums \(15\sqrt2\) and \(12\sqrt5\) respectively. Let their eccentricities be \(e_1=\sqrt{\dfrac52}\) and \(e_2\) respectively. If the product of the lengths of their transverse axes is \(100\sqrt{10}\), then \(25e_2^2\) is equal to ________.

Let \(A\) be a square matrix of order \(2\) such that \(|A|=2\) and the sum of its diagonal elements is \(-3\). If the points \((x,y)\) satisfying \(A^2+xA+yI=O\) lie on a hyperbola, whose transverse axis is parallel to the \(x\)-axis, eccentricity is \(e\) and the length of the latus rectum is \(l\), then \(e^4+l^4\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: By Cayley–Hamilton \(A^2+3A+2I=O\), so \((x-3)A+(y-2)I=O\); as \(A\) is not scalar, only \((3,2)\) works — no hyperbola. NTA dropped this question (bonus).

questions.q: The length of the latus rectum and directrices of a hyperbola with eccentricity \(e\) are \(9\) and \(x=\pm\dfrac4{\sqrt3}\), respectively. Let the line \(y-\sqrt3x+\sqrt3=0\) touch this hyperbola at \((x_0,y_0)\). If \(m\) is the product of the focal distances of the point \((x_0,y_0)\), then \(4e^2+m\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(\tfrac ae=\tfrac4{\sqrt3}\) and \(\tfrac{2b^2}a=9\) give \(8e^3-8e=9\sqrt3\), which is not consistent with the given tangent. NTA dropped this question (bonus).

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the focus of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}3-\dfrac{y^2}5=1\), on the positive \(x\)-axis. Let \(C\) be the circle with its centre at \(A(\sqrt6,\sqrt5)\) and passing through the point \(S\). If \(O\) is the origin and \(SAB\) is a diameter of \(C\), then the square of the area of the triangle \(OSB\) is ________.
questions.sol: \(S=(2\sqrt2,0)\) and \(B=2A-S\) has ordinate \(2\sqrt5\). Area \(\tfrac12\cdot2\sqrt2\cdot2\sqrt5=2\sqrt{10}\).

questions.q: Let the latus ractum of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) subtend an angle of \(\dfrac\pi3\) at the centre of the hyperbola. If \(b^2\) is equal to \(\dfrac lm(1+\sqrt n)\), where \(l\) and \(m\) are co-prime numbers, then \(l^2+m^2+n^2\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(\tfrac{b^2/3}c=\tan\tfrac\pi6\) gives \(b^4=3(9+b^2)\), so \(b^2=\tfrac32(1+\sqrt{13})\).

questions.q: Let the foci and length of the latus rectum of an ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b\) be \((\pm5,0)\) and \(\sqrt{50}\), respectively. Then, the square of the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{b^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{a^2b^2}=1\) equals

Let the eccentricity of an ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) is reciprocal to that of the hyperbola \(2x^2-2y^2=1\). If the ellipse intersects the hyperbola at right angles, then square of length of the latus-rectum of the ellipse is ________.
questions.sol: The hyperbola has \(e=\sqrt2\) and foci \((\pm1,0)\); orthogonal intersection means the conics are confocal: \(ae=1\) with \(e=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\) gives \(a^2=2\), \(b^2=1\), latus rectum \(\sqrt2\).

questions.q: Let \(H_n:\dfrac{x^2}{1+n}-\dfrac{y^2}{3+n}=1\), \(n\in N\). Let \(k\) be the smallest even value of \(n\) such that the eccentricity of \(H_k\) is a rational number. If \(l\) is the length of the latus rectum of \(H_k\), then \(21l\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(e^2=\tfrac{2n+4}{n+1}\) is a rational square first (for even \(n\)) at \(n=48\): \(e^2=\tfrac{100}{49}\). \(l=\tfrac{2\cdot51}7\).

questions.q: Let the tangent to the parabola \(y^2=12x\) at the point \((3,\alpha)\) be perpendicular to the line \(2x+2y=3\). Then the square of distance of the point \((6,-4)\) from the normal to the hyperbola \(\alpha^2x^2-9y^2=9\alpha^2\) at its point \((\alpha-1,\alpha+2)\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: The tangent at \((3,6)\) has slope \(1\), so \(\alpha=6\). The normal to \(\tfrac{x^2}9-\tfrac{y^2}{36}=1\) at \((5,8)\) is \(2x+5y=50\); distance\(^2=\tfrac{58^2}{29}\).

questions.q: Let \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) be the slopes of the tangents drawn from the point \(P(4,1)\) to the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{y^2}{25}-\dfrac{x^2}{16}=1\). If \(Q\) is the point from which the tangents drawn to \(H\) have slopes \(|m_1|\) and \(|m_2|\) and they make positive intercepts \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) on the \(x\)-axis, then \(\dfrac{(PQ)^2}{\alpha\beta}\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \((1-4m)^2=25-16m^2\) gives \(m=1,-\tfrac34\). For slopes \(1,\tfrac34\) from \(Q(h,k)\): \(\tfrac{2hk}{h^2+16}=\tfrac74\), \(\tfrac{k^2-25}{h^2+16}=\tfrac34\); positive intercepts need \(Q(-4,-7)\), with intercepts \(3\) and \(\tfrac{16}3\). \(\tfrac{64+64}{16}\).

questions.q: The foci of a hyperbola are \((\pm2,0)\) and its eccentricity is \(\dfrac32\). A tangent perpendicular to the line \(2x+3y=6\), is drawn at a point in the first quadrant on the hyperbola. If the intercepts made by the tangent on the \(x\)- and \(y\)-axes are \(a\) and \(b\) respectively, then \(|6a|+|5b|\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(a^2=\tfrac{16}9\), \(b^2=\tfrac{20}9\); slope \(\tfrac32\) gives \(c^2=4-\tfrac{20}9\). The first-quadrant contact uses \(y=\tfrac32x-\tfrac43\): intercepts \(\tfrac89\) and \(-\tfrac43\).

questions.q: The vertices of a hyperbola \(H\) are \((\pm6,0)\) and its eccentricity is \(\dfrac{\sqrt5}2\). Let \(N\) be the normal to \(H\) at a point in the first quadrant and parallel to the line \(\sqrt2x+y=2\sqrt2\). If \(d\) is the length of the line segment of \(N\) between \(H\) and the \(y\)-axis then \(d^2\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(b^2=9\). The normal at \((6\sec\theta,3\tan\theta)\) has slope \(-2\sin\theta=-\sqrt2\): point \((6\sqrt2,3)\), meeting the \(y\)-axis at \((0,15)\). \(d^2=72+144\).

questions.q: Let the equation of two diameters of a circle \(x^2+y^2-2x+2fy+1=0\) be \(2px-y=1\) and \(2x+py=4p\). Then the slope \(m\in(0,\infty)\) of the tangent to the hyperbola \(3x^2-y^2=3\) passing through the centre of the circle is equal to ________.
questions.sol: The centre \((1,-f)\) lies on both lines: \(2p^2-5p+2=0\). Centre \((1,0)\) admits no tangent, so the centre is \((1,3)\): \((3-m)^2=m^2-3\).

questions.q: An ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) passes through the vertices of the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{49}-\dfrac{y^2}{64}=-1\). Let the major and minor axes of the ellipse \(E\) coincide with the transverse and conjugate axes of the hyperbola \(H\), respectively. Let the product of the eccentricities of \(E\) and \(H\) be \(\dfrac12\). If \(l\) is the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse \(E\), then the value of \(113l\) is equal to ________.

A common tangent \(T\) to the curves \(C_1:\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}9=1\) and \(C_2:\dfrac{x^2}{42}-\dfrac{y^2}{143}=1\) does not pass through the fourth quadrant. If \(T\) touches \(C_1\) at \((x_1,y_1)\) and \(C_2\) at \((x_2,y_2)\), then \(|2x_1+x_2|\) is equal to ________.

For the hyperbola \(H:x^2-y^2=1\) and the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>b>0\), let the
(i) eccentricity of \(E\) be reciprocal of the eccentricity of \(H\), and
(ii) the line \(y=\sqrt{\dfrac52}x+K\) be a common tangent of \(E\) and \(H\). Then \(4(a^2+b^2)\) is equal to ________.

Let the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-y^2=1\) and the ellipse \(E:3x^2+4y^2=12\) be such that the length of latus rectum of \(H\) is equal to the length of latus rectum of \(E\). If \(e_H\) and \(e_E\) are the eccentricities of \(H\) and \(E\) respectively, then the value of \(12(e_H^2+e_E^2)\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(E\) has latus rectum \(3\), \(e_E^2=\tfrac14\). \(\tfrac2a=3\): \(e_H^2=1+\tfrac94\).

questions.q: Let a line \(L_1\) be tangent to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) and let \(L_2\) be the line passing through the origin and perpendicular to \(L_1\). If the locus of the point of intersection of \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) is \((x^2+y^2)^2=\alpha x^2+\beta y^2\), then \(\alpha+\beta\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: The foot of the perpendicular satisfies \((x^2+y^2)^2=16x^2-4y^2\).

questions.q: Let \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a>0\), \(b>0\), be a hyperbola such that the sum of lengths of the transverse and the conjugate axes is \(4(2\sqrt2+\sqrt{14})\). If the eccentricity \(H\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}2\), then the value of \(a^2+b^2\) is equal to ________.

Let \(A(\sec\theta,2\tan\theta)\) and \(B(\sec\phi,2\tan\phi)\), where \(\theta+\phi=\pi/2\), be two points on the hyperbola \(2x^2-y^2=2\). If \((\alpha,\beta)\) is the point of the intersection of the normals to the hyperbola at \(A\) and \(B\), then \((2\beta)^2\) is equal to ________.
questions.sol: \(2\sec^2\theta-4\tan^2\theta=2-2\tan^2\theta\ne2\), so the points \((\sec\theta,2\tan\theta)\) do not lie on \(2x^2-y^2=2\). NTA dropped this question (bonus).

questions.q: A square \(ABCD\) has all its vertices on the curve \(x^2y^2=1\). The midpoints of its sides also lie on the same curve. Then, the square of area of \(ABCD\) is ________.
questions.sol: Take vertices \(\left(a,\tfrac1a\right)\) and \(\left(-\tfrac1a,a\right)\) (a \(90^\circ\) rotation). Their midpoint on the curve gives \(\left(a^2-\tfrac1{a^2}\right)^2=16\), so \(a^2+\tfrac1{a^2}=2\sqrt5\). Side\(^2=2\left(a^2+\tfrac1{a^2}\right)=4\sqrt5\).

questions.q: The locus of the point of intersection of the lines \((\sqrt3)kx+ky-4\sqrt3=0\) and \(\sqrt3x-y-4(\sqrt3)k=0\) is a conic, whose eccentricity is ________.

Let \(O\) be the vertex of the parabola \(x^2=4y\) and \(Q\) be any point on it. Let the locus of the point \(P\), which divides the line segment \(OQ\) internally in the ratio \(2:3\), be the conic \(C\). Then the equation of the chord of \(C\) which is bisected at the point \((1,2)\) is:
questions.sol:
Take \(Q(2t,t^2)\). Then \(P=\tfrac25 Q=\left(\tfrac{4t}{5},\tfrac{2t^2}{5}\right)\). Eliminating \(t\): \(y=\tfrac{5}{8}x^2\), i.e. \(C:\ x^2=\tfrac85 y\).
Chord with mid-point \((1,2)\): \(T=S_1\) gives \(x\cdot1-\tfrac45(y+2)=1-\tfrac85\cdot2\), i.e. \(5x-4y-8=-11\), so \(5x-4y+3=0\).

questions.q: Let \(PQ\) and \(MN\) be two straight lines touching the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x-6y-3=0\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively. Let \(O\) be the centre of the circle and \(\angle AOB=\pi/3\). Then the locus of the point of intersection of the lines \(PQ\) and \(MN\) is:
questions.sol:
Centre \(O(2,3)\), radius \(4\). If \(T\) is the intersection of the tangents, \(OT\) bisects \(\angle AOB\), so \(OT=\dfrac{4}{\cos(\pi/6)}=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt3}\).
Locus: \((x-2)^2+(y-3)^2=\dfrac{64}{3}\iff 3(x^2+y^2)-12x-18y-25=0\).

questions.q: Let the foci of a hyperbola coincide with the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{36}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\). If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is \(5\), then the length of its latus rectum is:
questions.sol:
Ellipse: \(c^2=36-16=20\), foci \((\pm2\sqrt5,0)\). Hyperbola: \(ae=2\sqrt5\), \(e=5\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}\), \(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=\dfrac45\cdot24=\dfrac{96}{5}\).
Latus rectum \(=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{192/5}{2/\sqrt5}=\dfrac{96}{\sqrt5}\).

questions.q: Let a point \(A\) lie between the parallel lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) such that its distances from \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are \(6\) and \(3\) units respectively. Then the area (in sq. units) of the equilateral triangle \(ABC\), where the points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on the lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) respectively, is:
questions.sol:
Take \(A\) at the origin, \(L_1:y=6\), \(L_2:y=-3\), side \(s\). Let \(AB\) make angle \(\theta\) with the lines; then \(AC\) makes angle \(\theta-60^\circ\).
\(s\sin\theta=6\), \(s\sin(\theta-60^\circ)=-3\Rightarrow\sin\theta=-2\sin(\theta-60^\circ)\Rightarrow 2\sin\theta=\sqrt3\cos\theta\), so \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\) and \(\sin\theta=\sqrt{\dfrac37}\).
\(s^2=\dfrac{36}{3/7}=84\), area \(=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot84=21\sqrt3\).

questions.q: If the line \(\alpha x+4y=\sqrt7\), where \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), touches the ellipse \(3x^2+4y^2=1\) at the point \(P\) in the first quadrant, then one of the focal distances of \(P\) is:
questions.sol:
Tangent at \(P(x_1,y_1)\): \(3x_1x+4y_1y=1\). Comparing with \(\dfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt7}x+\dfrac{4}{\sqrt7}y=1\) gives \(y_1=\dfrac1{\sqrt7}\), and then \(3x_1^2=1-\dfrac47\Rightarrow x_1=\dfrac1{\sqrt7}\).
\(a^2=\tfrac13,\ b^2=\tfrac14\Rightarrow e^2=1-\tfrac34=\tfrac14\), \(e=\tfrac12\).
Focal distances \(a\pm ex_1=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\pm\dfrac1{2\sqrt7}\).

questions.q: Let one end of a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=16x\) be \((16,16)\). If \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) divides this focal chord internally in the ratio \(5:2\), then the minimum value of \(\alpha+\beta\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(a=4\); \((16,16)\) corresponds to \(t=2\), so the other end is \(t'=-\tfrac12\), i.e. \((1,-4)\).
Dividing in \(5:2\) from \((16,16)\): \(P=\left(\tfrac{37}{7},\tfrac{12}{7}\right)\), \(\alpha+\beta=7\).
Dividing in \(5:2\) from \((1,-4)\): \(P=\left(\tfrac{82}{7},\tfrac{72}{7}\right)\), \(\alpha+\beta=22\).
Minimum \(=7\).

questions.q: Let \(y^2=12x\) be the parabola with its vertex at \(O\). Let \(P\) be a point on the parabola and \(A\) be a point on the \(x\)-axis such that \(\angle OPA=90^\circ\). Then the locus of the centroid of such triangles \(OPA\) is:
questions.sol:
\(P(3t^2,6t)\), \(A(h,0)\). \(\overrightarrow{PO}\cdot\overrightarrow{PA}=0\): \(-3t^2(h-3t^2)+36t^2=0\Rightarrow h=3t^2+12\).
Centroid: \(X=\dfrac{6t^2+12}{3}=2t^2+4\), \(Y=2t\). Eliminating \(t\): \(X=\dfrac{Y^2}{2}+4\), i.e. \(y^2-2x+8=0\).

questions.q: If \(P\) is a point on the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\), \(Q\) is a point on the straight line \(5x+y+2=0\) and \(x-y+1=0\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(PQ\), then \(13\) times the sum of abscissa of all such points \(P\) is ______.
If the chord joining the points \(P_1(x_1,y_1)\) and \(P_2(x_2,y_2)\) on the parabola \(y^2=12x\) subtends a right angle at the vertex of the parabola, then \(x_1x_2-y_1y_2\) is equal to:

Let the set of all values of \(r\), for which the circles \((x+1)^2+(y+4)^2=r^2\) and \(x^2+y^2-4x-2y-4=0\) intersect at two distinct points, be the interval \((\alpha,\beta)\). Then \(\alpha\beta\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Centres \((-1,-4)\) and \((2,1)\), radii \(r\) and \(3\), \(d=\sqrt{34}\).
Two points of intersection \(\iff|r-3|<\sqrt{34}<r+3\iff\sqrt{34}-3<r<\sqrt{34}+3\).
\(\alpha\beta=34-9=25\).

questions.q: If the line \(\alpha x+2y=1\), where \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), does not meet the hyperbola \(x^2-9y^2=9\), then a possible value of \(\alpha\) is:
questions.sol:
Substituting \(y=\dfrac{1-\alpha x}{2}\): \((4-9\alpha^2)x^2+18\alpha x-45=0\).
No intersection \(\iff\) discriminant \(<0\) (and \(4-9\alpha^2\ne0\)): \(324\alpha^2+180(4-9\alpha^2)<0\iff\alpha^2>\tfrac59\approx0.556\).
Among the options only \(\alpha=0.8\) works.

questions.q:
Among the statements
(S1): If \(A(5,-1)\) and \(B(-2,3)\) are two vertices of a triangle whose orthocentre is \((0,0)\), then its third vertex is \((-4,-7)\)
and
(S2): If positive numbers \(2a,b,c\) are three consecutive terms of an A.P., then the lines \(ax+by+c=0\) are concurrent at \((2,-2)\),
questions.sol:
(S1) Let \(C=(h,k)\). \(\overrightarrow{HA}\perp BC\): \(5(h+2)-(k-3)=0\Rightarrow5h-k=-13\). \(\overrightarrow{HB}\perp AC\): \(-2(h-5)+3(k+1)=0\Rightarrow-2h+3k=-13\). So \(C=(-4,-7)\): true.
(S2) \(2b=2a+c\Rightarrow 2a-2b+c=0\), i.e. \((2,-2)\) lies on every line \(ax+by+c=0\): true.

questions.q: Let \(P(10,2\sqrt{15})\) be a point on the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), whose foci are \(S\) and \(S'\). If the length of its latus rectum is \(8\), then the square of the area of \(\Delta PSS'\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=8\Rightarrow b^2=4a\). Then \(\dfrac{100}{a^2}-\dfrac{60}{4a}=1\Rightarrow a^2+15a-100=0\Rightarrow a=5\), \(b^2=20\), \(c=\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt5\).
Area \(=\tfrac12\cdot2c\cdot2\sqrt{15}=3\sqrt5\cdot2\sqrt{15}=30\sqrt3\); square \(=2700\).

questions.q: Let the locus of the mid-point of the chord through the origin \(O\) of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) be the curve \(S\). Let \(P\) be any point on \(S\). Then the locus of the point which internally divides \(OP\) in the ratio \(3:1\) is:
questions.sol:
Chord from \(O\) to \((t^2,2t)\) has mid-point \(\left(\tfrac{t^2}{2},t\right)\), so \(S:\ y^2=2x\).
For \(P\left(\tfrac{s^2}{2},s\right)\), the point is \(\tfrac34P=\left(\tfrac{3s^2}{8},\tfrac{3s}{4}\right)\). With \(s=\tfrac{4y}{3}\): \(x=\tfrac{2y^2}{3}\), i.e. \(2y^2=3x\).

questions.q: Let \(S\) and \(S'\) be the foci of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1\) and \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) be a point on the ellipse in the first quadrant. If \((SP)^2+(S'P)^2-SP\cdot S'P=37\), then \(\alpha^2+\beta^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(e=\tfrac45\), \(SP+S'P=10\). \((SP+S'P)^2-3SP\cdot S'P=37\Rightarrow SP\cdot S'P=21\).
\(\left(5-\tfrac45\alpha\right)\left(5+\tfrac45\alpha\right)=21\Rightarrow\alpha^2=\tfrac{25}{4}\), and \(\beta^2=9\left(1-\tfrac14\right)=\tfrac{27}{4}\).
\(\alpha^2+\beta^2=13\).

questions.q: Let the line \(y-x=1\) intersect the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{2}+\dfrac{y^2}{1}=1\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\). Then the angle made by the line segment \(AB\) at the centre of the ellipse is:
questions.sol:
\(\dfrac{x^2}{2}+(x+1)^2=1\Rightarrow x\left(\tfrac32x+2\right)=0\): \(A(0,1)\), \(B\left(-\tfrac43,-\tfrac13\right)\).
\(\cos\angle AOB=\dfrac{-1/3}{\sqrt{17}/3}=-\dfrac1{\sqrt{17}}\), so \(\angle AOB=\pi-\tan^{-1}4=\dfrac\pi2+\tan^{-1}\dfrac14\).

questions.q: Let the domain of the function \(f(x)=\log_3\log_5\log_7(9x-x^2-13)\) be the interval \((m,n)\). Let the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) have eccentricity \(\dfrac n3\) and the length of the latus rectum \(\dfrac{8m}{3}\). Then \(b^2-a^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\log_5\log_7(\cdot)>0\Rightarrow9x-x^2-13>7\Rightarrow x^2-9x+20<0\Rightarrow(m,n)=(4,5)\).
\(e^2=\tfrac{25}{9}\Rightarrow b^2=\tfrac{16}{9}a^2\); \(\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{32a}{9}=\dfrac{32}{3}\Rightarrow a=3\), \(b^2=16\).
\(b^2-a^2=7\).

questions.q: A rectangle is formed by the lines \(x=0\), \(y=0\), \(x=3\) and \(y=4\). Let the line \(L\) be perpendicular to \(3x+y+6=0\) and divide the area of the rectangle into two equal parts. Then the distance of the point \(\left(\dfrac12,-5\right)\) from the line \(L\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
A line bisects the area of a rectangle iff it passes through its centre \(\left(\tfrac32,2\right)\). Slope \(\tfrac13\): \(L:\ 2x-6y+9=0\).
Distance \(=\dfrac{|1+30+9|}{\sqrt{40}}=\dfrac{40}{2\sqrt{10}}=2\sqrt{10}\).

questions.q: An equilateral triangle \(OAB\) is inscribed in the parabola \(y^2=4x\) with the vertex \(O\) at the vertex of the parabola. Then the minimum distance of the circle having \(AB\) as a diameter from the origin is:
questions.sol:
\(A,B=(x,\pm\tfrac{x}{\sqrt3})\) on \(y^2=4x\): \(\tfrac{x^2}{3}=4x\Rightarrow x=12\), so \(A,B=(12,\pm4\sqrt3)\).
The circle has centre \((12,0)\) and radius \(4\sqrt3\); minimum distance from \(O\) \(=12-4\sqrt3=4(3-\sqrt3)\).

questions.q: If the points of intersection of the ellipses \(x^2+2y^2-6x-12y+23=0\) and \(4x^2+2y^2-20x-12y+35=0\) lie on a circle of radius \(r\) and centre \((a,b)\), then the value of \(ab+18r^2\) is:
questions.sol:
\(S_1+\lambda S_2=0\) is a circle when \(1+4\lambda=2+2\lambda\), i.e. \(\lambda=\tfrac12\):
\(3x^2+3y^2-16x-18y+\tfrac{81}{2}=0\Rightarrow x^2+y^2-\tfrac{16}{3}x-6y+\tfrac{27}{2}=0\).
Centre \(\left(\tfrac83,3\right)\), \(r^2=\tfrac{64}{9}+9-\tfrac{27}{2}=\tfrac{47}{18}\).
\(ab+18r^2=8+47=55\).

questions.q: Let \(PQ\) be a chord of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{4}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis, such that \(OPQ\) is an equilateral triangle, \(O\) being the centre of the hyperbola. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is \(\sqrt3\), then the area of the triangle \(OPQ\) is:
questions.sol:
\(e^2=3\Rightarrow b^2=8\). In the equilateral triangle \(OP\) makes \(30^\circ\) with the \(x\)-axis: \(P=\left(h,\tfrac{h}{\sqrt3}\right)\).
\(\dfrac{h^2}{4}-\dfrac{h^2}{24}=1\Rightarrow h^2=\dfrac{24}{5}\). Side \(=PQ=\dfrac{2h}{\sqrt3}\), side\(^2=\dfrac{32}{5}\).
Area \(=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot\dfrac{32}{5}=\dfrac{8\sqrt3}{5}\).

questions.q: Let \(A(1,2)\) and \(C(-3,-6)\) be two diagonally opposite vertices of a rhombus, whose sides \(AD\) and \(BC\) are parallel to the line \(7x-y=14\). If \(B(\alpha,\beta)\) and \(D(\gamma,\delta)\) are the other two vertices, then \(|\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta|\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Centre \(M(-1,-2)\). \(AC\) has slope \(2\), so \(BD\) has slope \(-\tfrac12\) through \(M\); \(AD\) has slope \(7\) through \(A\).
Solving \(y=7x-5\) and \(y+2=-\tfrac12(x+1)\): \(D=\left(\tfrac13,-\tfrac83\right)\), \(B=2M-D=\left(-\tfrac73,-\tfrac43\right)\).
\(|\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta|=|2(-1-2)|=6\).

questions.q: Let each of the two ellipses \(E_1:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\ (a>b)\) and \(E_2:\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{B^2}=1\ (A<B)\) have eccentricity \(\dfrac45\). Let the lengths of the latus recta of \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) be \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) respectively, such that \(2l_1^2=9l_2\). If the distance between the foci of \(E_1\) is \(8\), then the distance between the foci of \(E_2\) is:
questions.sol:
\(E_1\): \(2ae=8\Rightarrow a=5\), \(b^2=9\), \(l_1=\tfrac{18}{5}\). Then \(l_2=\tfrac{2l_1^2}{9}=\tfrac{72}{25}\).
\(E_2\) (major axis along \(y\)): \(A^2=\tfrac{9}{25}B^2\), \(l_2=\tfrac{2A^2}{B}=\tfrac{18B}{25}=\tfrac{72}{25}\Rightarrow B=4\).
Distance between foci \(=2Be=\tfrac{32}{5}\).

questions.q: Let a circle of radius \(4\) pass through the origin \(O\), the points \(A(-\sqrt3a,0)\) and \(B(0,-\sqrt2b)\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real parameters and \(ab\ne0\). Then the locus of the centroid of \(\Delta OAB\) is a circle of radius:
questions.sol:
\(\angle AOB=90^\circ\), so \(AB\) is a diameter: \(3a^2+2b^2=64\).
Centroid \((h,k)=\left(-\tfrac{a}{\sqrt3},-\tfrac{\sqrt2b}{3}\right)\Rightarrow3a^2=9h^2\), \(2b^2=9k^2\), so \(h^2+k^2=\tfrac{64}{9}\): radius \(\tfrac83\).

questions.q: Let \(A(1,0)\), \(B(2,-1)\) and \(C\left(\dfrac73,\dfrac43\right)\) be three points. If the equation of the bisector of the angle \(ABC\) is \(\alpha x+\beta y=5\), then the value of \(\alpha^2+\beta^2\) is:
questions.sol:
\(\overrightarrow{BA}=(-1,1)\), \(|BA|=\sqrt2\); \(\overrightarrow{BC}=\left(\tfrac13,\tfrac73\right)\), \(|BC|=\tfrac{5\sqrt2}{3}\).
Sum of unit vectors \(\propto(-5,5)+(1,7)=(-4,12)\propto(-1,3)\). The bisector through \(B\) with direction \((-1,3)\): \(3x+y=5\).
\(\alpha^2+\beta^2=10\).

questions.q: Let the angles made with the positive \(x\)-axis by two straight lines drawn from the point \(P(2,3)\) and meeting the line \(x+y=6\) at a distance \(\sqrt{\dfrac23}\) from the point \(P\) be \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\). Then the value of \((\theta_1+\theta_2)\) is:
questions.sol:
The point \((2+r\cos\theta,\,3+r\sin\theta)\) with \(r=\sqrt{\tfrac23}\) lies on \(x+y=6\): \(\cos\theta+\sin\theta=\sqrt{\tfrac32}\), i.e. \(\sin\left(\theta+\tfrac\pi4\right)=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\).
\(\theta+\tfrac\pi4=\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac{2\pi}3\Rightarrow\theta=\tfrac\pi{12},\tfrac{5\pi}{12}\); sum \(=\tfrac\pi2\).

questions.q: Let the length of the latus rectum of an ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \((a>b)\), be \(30\). If its eccentricity is the maximum value of the function \(f(t)=-\dfrac34+2t-t^2\), then \((a^2+b^2)\) is equal to:
Let the image of the parabola \(x^2=4y\) in the line \(x-y=1\) be \((y+a)^2=b(x-c)\), \(a,b,c\in\mathbb{N}\). Then \(a+b+c\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
The image of \((x,y)\) in \(x-y=1\) is \((y+1,x-1)\). So a point \((X,Y)\) of the image comes from \((Y+1,X-1)\) on the parabola: \((Y+1)^2=4(X-1)\).
\(a=1,b=4,c=1\): \(a+b+c=6\).

questions.q: Let \((h,k)\) lie on the circle \(C:x^2+y^2=4\) and the point \((2h+1,3k+2)\) lie on an ellipse with eccentricity \(e\). Then the value of \(\dfrac{5}{e^2}\) is equal to ______.

Let \(y=x\) be the equation of a chord of the circle \(C_1\) (in the closed half-plane \(x\ge0\)) of diameter \(10\) passing through the origin. Let \(C_2\) be another circle described on the given chord as its diameter. If the equation of the chord of the circle \(C_2\), which passes through the point \((2,3)\) and is farthest from the centre of \(C_2\), is \(x+ay+b=0\), then \(a-b\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
A circle of diameter \(10\) through \(O\) lying in \(x\ge0\) touches the \(y\)-axis at \(O\): \(C_1:\ x^2+y^2-10x=0\). It meets \(y=x\) at \((0,0)\) and \((5,5)\).
\(C_2\): centre \(M\left(\tfrac52,\tfrac52\right)\). The chord through \(P(2,3)\) farthest from \(M\) is perpendicular to \(MP\), whose direction is \((-1,1)\):
\(-(x-2)+(y-3)=0\iff x-y+1=0\). So \(a=-1\), \(b=1\), \(a-b=-2\).

questions.q: Let \(ABC\) be an equilateral triangle with orthocentre at the origin and the side \(BC\) on the line \(x+2\sqrt2y=4\). If the co-ordinates of the vertex \(A\) are \((\alpha,\beta)\), then the greatest integer less than or equal to \(|\alpha+\sqrt2\beta|\) is:
questions.sol:
In an equilateral triangle the orthocentre is the centroid, so \(A=-2F\) where \(F\) is the foot of the perpendicular from \(O\) to \(BC\).
\(F=\tfrac{4}{9}(1,2\sqrt2)\), so \(A=\left(-\tfrac89,-\tfrac{16\sqrt2}{9}\right)\) and \(|\alpha+\sqrt2\beta|=\tfrac{8+32}{9}=\tfrac{40}{9}\approx4.44\).
Greatest integer \(=4\).

questions.q: For some \(\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola \(x^2-y^2\sec^2\theta=8\) be \(e_1\) and \(l_1\), respectively, and let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse \(x^2\sec^2\theta+y^2=6\) be \(e_2\) and \(l_2\), respectively. If \(e_1^2=e_2^2(\sec^2\theta+1)\), then \(\left(\dfrac{l_1l_2}{e_1e_2}\right)\tan^2\theta\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Hyperbola: \(a^2=8\), \(b^2=8\cos^2\theta\): \(e_1^2=1+\cos^2\theta\), \(l_1=4\sqrt2\cos^2\theta\).
Ellipse: \(\dfrac{x^2}{6\cos^2\theta}+\dfrac{y^2}{6}=1\): \(e_2^2=\sin^2\theta\), \(l_2=2\sqrt6\cos^2\theta\).
Condition: \(1+\cos^2\theta=\tan^2\theta(1+\cos^2\theta)\Rightarrow\theta=\tfrac\pi4\).
Then \(l_1=2\sqrt2\), \(l_2=\sqrt6\), \(e_1e_2=\sqrt{\tfrac32}\cdot\tfrac1{\sqrt2}=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\): value \(=\dfrac{2\sqrt{12}}{\sqrt3/2}\cdot1=8\).

questions.q: Let the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{144}+\dfrac{y^2}{169}=1\) and the hyperbola \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{\lambda^2}=-1\) have the same foci. If \(e\) and \(L\) respectively denote the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of \(H\), then the value of \(24(e+L)\) is:
questions.sol:
Foci of \(E\): \((0,\pm5)\). \(H:\ \dfrac{y^2}{\lambda^2}-\dfrac{x^2}{16}=1\) has foci \((0,\pm\sqrt{\lambda^2+16})\Rightarrow\lambda^2=9\).
\(e=\tfrac53\), \(L=\tfrac{2\cdot16}{3}=\tfrac{32}{3}\). \(24(e+L)=24\cdot\tfrac{37}{3}=296\).

questions.q: An ellipse has its centre at \((1,-2)\), one focus at \((3,-2)\) and one vertex at \((5,-2)\). Then the length of its latus rectum is:

Let \(A\) be the focus of the parabola \(y^2=8x\). Let the line \(y=mx+c\) intersect the parabola at two distinct points \(B\) and \(C\). If the centroid of the triangle \(ABC\) is \(\left(\dfrac73,\dfrac43\right)\), then \((BC)^2\) is equal to:

Let the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) intersect the \(x\)-axis at the points \(A(a,0)\), \(a>0\) and \(B(b,0)\). Let \(P(2\cos\alpha,2\sin\alpha)\), \(0<\alpha<\dfrac\pi2\) and \(Q(2\cos\beta,2\sin\beta)\) be two points such that \((\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac\pi2\). Then the point of intersection of \(AQ\) and \(BP\) lies on:
questions.sol:
\(A(2,0)\), \(B(-2,0)\). Arc \(PQ\) subtends \(90^\circ\) at the centre, so the chords \(AQ\) and \(BP\) meet at a constant angle \(\angle AXB=\tfrac12(180^\circ-90^\circ)=45^\circ\); \(X\) lies on a fixed circle through \(A,B\).
For \(\alpha=\tfrac\pi4\): \(P(\sqrt2,\sqrt2)\), \(Q(\sqrt2,-\sqrt2)\), and \(AQ\), \(BP\) meet at \((2\sqrt2,2)\).
The circle through \((\pm2,0)\) and \((2\sqrt2,2)\) is \(x^2+y^2-4y-4=0\).

questions.q: Let the mid-points of the sides of a triangle \(ABC\) be \(\left(\dfrac52,7\right)\), \(\left(\dfrac52,3\right)\) and \((4,5)\). If its incentre is \((h,k)\), then \(3h+k\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Each vertex is (sum of two mid-points) \(-\) (third): \((1,5),(4,9),(4,1)\).
Opposite side lengths: \(8,5,5\). Incentre \(=\dfrac{8(1,5)+5(4,9)+5(4,1)}{18}=\left(\tfrac83,5\right)\).
\(3h+k=13\).

questions.q: Let an ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(a<b\), pass through the point \((4,3)\) and have eccentricity \(\dfrac{\sqrt5}{3}\). Then the length of its latus rectum is:
questions.sol:
Major axis along \(y\): \(a^2=b^2(1-e^2)=\tfrac49b^2\). \(\dfrac{16}{a^2}+\dfrac9{b^2}=\dfrac{45}{b^2}=1\Rightarrow b^2=45\), \(a^2=20\).
Latus rectum \(=\dfrac{2a^2}{b}=\dfrac{40}{3\sqrt5}=\dfrac{8\sqrt5}{3}\).

questions.q: Let a circle \(C\) have its centre in the first quadrant, intersect the coordinate axes at exactly three points and cut off equal intercepts from the coordinate axes. If the length of the chord of \(C\) on the line \(x+y=1\) is \(\sqrt{14}\), then the square of the radius of \(C\) is ______.
questions.sol:
Exactly three points with equal intercepts: \(C\) passes through \(O\) with centre \((h,h)\): \(x^2+y^2-2hx-2hy=0\), \(r^2=2h^2\).
\(r^2-d^2=\tfrac{14}{4}\) with \(d=\tfrac{|2h-1|}{\sqrt2}\): \(2h^2-\tfrac{(2h-1)^2}{2}=\tfrac72\Rightarrow h=2\).
\(r^2=8\).

questions.q: Let a circle pass through the origin and its centre be the point of intersection of two mutually perpendicular lines \(x+(k-1)y+3=0\) and \(2x+k^2y-4=0\). If the line \(x-y+2=0\) intersects the circle at the points \(A\) and \(B\), then \((AB)^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Perpendicular: \(2+(k-1)k^2=0\Rightarrow(k+1)(k^2-2k+2)=0\Rightarrow k=-1\). Lines \(x-2y+3=0\), \(2x+y-4=0\) meet at \((1,2)\); \(r^2=5\).
Distance of the centre from \(x-y+2=0\) is \(\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\). \(AB^2=4\left(5-\tfrac12\right)=18\).

questions.q: Let \(O\) be the origin, and \(P\) and \(Q\) be two points on the rectangular hyperbola \(xy=12\) such that the mid-point of the line segment \(PQ\) is \(\left(\dfrac12,-\dfrac12\right)\). Then the area of the triangle \(OPQ\) equals:
questions.sol:
\(P\left(t_1,\tfrac{12}{t_1}\right)\), \(Q\left(t_2,\tfrac{12}{t_2}\right)\): \(t_1+t_2=1\), \(\tfrac{12(t_1+t_2)}{t_1t_2}=-1\Rightarrow t_1t_2=-12\).
Area \(=\tfrac12\left|\tfrac{12t_1}{t_2}-\tfrac{12t_2}{t_1}\right|=\tfrac{6|t_1-t_2||t_1+t_2|}{12}=\tfrac12\sqrt{1+48}=\tfrac72\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) be the point \((3,0)\) and circles with variable diameter \(AB\) touch the circle \(x^2+y^2=36\) internally. Let the curve \(C\) be the locus of the point \(B\). If the eccentricity of \(C\) is \(e\), then \(72e^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Centre \(M=\tfrac{A+B}{2}\), radius \(\tfrac{AB}{2}\). Internal tangency: \(OM=6-\tfrac{AB}{2}\Rightarrow|B+A|+|B-A|=12\).
So \(B\) lies on an ellipse with foci \((\pm3,0)\) and \(2a=12\): \(e=\tfrac12\), \(72e^2=18\).

questions.q: Let the line \(L_1:x+3=0\) intersect the lines \(L_2:x-y=0\) and \(L_3:3x+y=0\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. Let the bisector of the obtuse angle between the lines \(L_2\) and \(L_3\) intersect the line \(L_1\) at the point \(C\). Then \(BC^2:AC^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(A(-3,-3)\), \(B(-3,9)\). The directions \((1,1)\) and \((1,-3)\) make an obtuse angle (\(\cos<0\)); its bisector through \(O\) meets segment \(AB\) internally, so it bisects \(\angle AOB\).
By the angle bisector theorem \(\dfrac{BC}{AC}=\dfrac{OB}{OA}=\dfrac{\sqrt{90}}{\sqrt{18}}=\sqrt5\), so \(BC^2:AC^2=5:1\).

questions.q: Let the vertex \(A\) of a triangle \(ABC\) be \((1,2)\), and the mid-point of the side \(AB\) be \((5,-1)\). If the centroid of this triangle is \((3,4)\) and its circumcentre is \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(21(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to:

Suppose that two chords, drawn from the point \((1,2)\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2+x-3y=0\), are bisected by the \(y\)-axis. If the other ends of these chords are \(R\) and \(S\), and the mid-point of the line segment \(RS\) is \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(6(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Mid-point \((0,k)\) gives the other end \((-1,2k-2)\). On the circle: \((2k-2)^2-3(2k-2)=0\Rightarrow2k-2=0\) or \(3\).
\(R(-1,0)\), \(S(-1,3)\), mid-point \(\left(-1,\tfrac32\right)\). \(6(\alpha+\beta)=3\).

questions.q: Consider the parabola \(P:y^2=4kx\) and the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). Let the line segment joining the points of intersection of \(P\) and \(E\) be their latus rectums. If the eccentricity of \(E\) is \(e\), then \(e^2+2\sqrt2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Latus rectum ends: \((k,\pm2k)\) for \(P\) and \(\left(ae,\pm\tfrac{b^2}{a}\right)\) for \(E\). So \(k=ae\) and \(2ae=\tfrac{b^2}{a}=a(1-e^2)\).
\(e^2+2e-1=0\Rightarrow e=\sqrt2-1\); \(e^2+2\sqrt2=3-2\sqrt2+2\sqrt2=3\).

questions.q: Let \(P(3\cos\alpha,2\sin\alpha)\), \(\alpha\ne0\), be a point on the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1\), \(Q\) be a point on the circle \(x^2+y^2-14x-14y+82=0\) and \(R\) be a point on the line \(x+y=5\) such that the centroid of the triangle \(PQR\) is \(\left(2+\cos\alpha,3+\dfrac23\sin\alpha\right)\). Then the sum of the ordinates of all possible points \(R\) is:
questions.sol:
\(P+Q+R=(6+3\cos\alpha,9+2\sin\alpha)\Rightarrow Q+R=(6,9)\). With \(R(t,5-t)\): \(Q=(6-t,4+t)\).
\(Q\) on the circle (centre \((7,7)\), radius \(4\)): \((t+1)^2+(t-3)^2=16\Rightarrow t^2-2t-3=0\Rightarrow t=3,-1\).
Ordinates of \(R\): \(2\) and \(6\); sum \(=8\).

questions.q: Let \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be a hyperbola such that the distance between its foci is \(6\) and the distance between its directrices is \(\dfrac83\). If the line \(x=\alpha\) intersects the hyperbola \(H\) at the points \(A\) and \(B\) such that the area of the triangle \(AOB\) is \(4\sqrt{15}\), where \(O\) is the origin, then \(\alpha^2\) equals:
questions.sol:
\(ae=3\), \(\tfrac ae=\tfrac43\Rightarrow a^2=4\), \(e=\tfrac32\), \(b^2=5\).
\(A,B=\left(\alpha,\pm\sqrt5\sqrt{\tfrac{\alpha^2}{4}-1}\right)\); area \(=|\alpha|\sqrt5\sqrt{\tfrac{\alpha^2}{4}-1}=4\sqrt{15}\).
\(\alpha^2(\alpha^2-4)=192\Rightarrow\alpha^2=16\).

questions.q: Let \(A,B\) be points on the two half-lines \(x-\sqrt3|y|=\alpha\), \(\alpha>0\) at a distance of \(\alpha\) from their point of intersection \(P\). The line segment \(AB\) meets the angle bisector of the given half-lines at the point \(Q\). If \(PQ=\dfrac92\) and \(R\) is the radius of the circumcircle of \(\Delta PAB\), then \(\dfrac{\alpha^2}{R}\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
The half-lines start at \(P(\alpha,0)\) with slopes \(\pm\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\), so \(\angle APB=60^\circ\); with \(PA=PB=\alpha\), \(\triangle PAB\) is equilateral of side \(\alpha\).
\(Q\) is the mid-point of \(AB\): \(PQ=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\alpha=\tfrac92\Rightarrow\alpha=3\sqrt3\). \(R=\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt3}=3\).
\(\tfrac{\alpha^2}{R}=\tfrac{27}{3}=9\).

questions.q: Let \(A,B\) and \(C\) be the vertices of a variable right angled triangle inscribed in the parabola \(y^2=16x\). Let the vertex \(B\) containing the right angle be \((4,8)\) and the locus of the centroid of \(\Delta ABC\) be a conic \(C_0\). Then three times the length of latus rectum of \(C_0\) is ______.
questions.sol:
Points \((4t^2,8t)\); \(B\) has \(t=1\). Slope of \(BA\) \(=\tfrac{2}{t_1+1}\), so \(\angle B=90^\circ\Rightarrow(t_1+1)(t_2+1)=-4\).
With \(s=t_1+t_2\), \(p=t_1t_2=-5-s\): \(X=\tfrac43\left(1+s^2-2p\right)=\tfrac43\left((s+1)^2+10\right)\), \(Y=\tfrac83(1+s)\).
Eliminating \(s\): \(Y^2=\tfrac{16}{3}\left(X-\tfrac{40}{3}\right)\), latus rectum \(\tfrac{16}{3}\). Three times \(=16\).

questions.q: Let a focus of the ellipse \(E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be \(S(4,0)\) and its eccentricity be \(\dfrac45\). If the point \(P(3,\alpha)\) lies on \(E\) and \(O\) is the origin, then the area of \(\Delta POS\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(ae=4\Rightarrow a=5\), \(b^2=9\). \(\tfrac{9}{25}+\tfrac{\alpha^2}{9}=1\Rightarrow|\alpha|=\tfrac{12}{5}\).
Area \(=\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot\tfrac{12}{5}=\tfrac{24}{5}\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a moving point on the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x-8y+21=0\). Then the maximum distance of \(P\) from the vertex of the parabola \(x^2+6x+y+13=0\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Circle: centre \((3,4)\), radius \(2\). Parabola: \((x+3)^2=-(y+4)\), vertex \((-3,-4)\).
Distance between them \(=10\); maximum \(=10+2=12\).

questions.q: In an equilateral triangle \(PQR\), let the vertex \(P\) be at \((3,5)\) and the side \(QR\) be along the line \(x+y=4\). If the orthocentre of the triangle \(PQR\) is \((\alpha,\beta)\), then \(9(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Foot of the perpendicular from \(P\) to \(QR\): \(D=(1,3)\). In an equilateral triangle the orthocentre is the centroid, \(\tfrac23\) of the way from \(P\) to \(D\): \(\left(\tfrac53,\tfrac{11}{3}\right)\).
\(9(\alpha+\beta)=9\cdot\tfrac{16}{3}=48\).

questions.q: Let the point \(P\) be the vertex of the parabola \(y=x^2-6x+12\). If a line passing through the point \(P\) intersects the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-4y+3=0\) at the points \(R\) and \(S\), then the maximum value of \((PR+PS)^2\) is:
questions.sol:
\(P=(3,3)\); circle centre \(C(1,2)\), radius \(\sqrt2\); \(CP^2=5\), so \(P\) is outside.
If \(M\) is the foot of the perpendicular from \(C\) to the line, then \(PR+PS=2PM=2\sqrt{CP^2-CM^2}\le2\sqrt5\).
Maximum of \((PR+PS)^2=20\) (line through \(C\)).

questions.q: Let the directrix of the parabola \(P:y^2=8x\) cut the \(x\)-axis at the point \(A\). Let \(B(\alpha,\beta)\), \(\alpha>1\), be a point on \(P\) such that the slope of \(AB\) is \(\dfrac35\). If \(BC\) is a focal chord of \(P\), then six times the area of \(\Delta ABC\) is:
questions.sol:
\(A(-2,0)\), \(B(2t^2,4t)\): \(\dfrac{4t}{2t^2+2}=\dfrac35\Rightarrow3t^2-10t+3=0\Rightarrow t=3\) (since \(\alpha>1\)): \(B(18,12)\).
Focal chord: \(C\) has parameter \(-\tfrac13\): \(C\left(\tfrac29,-\tfrac43\right)\).
Area \(=\tfrac12\left|-2\left(12+\tfrac43\right)+18\left(-\tfrac43\right)+\tfrac29(-12)\right|=\tfrac{80}{3}\); six times \(=160\).

questions.q: Let the eccentricity \(e\) of a hyperbola satisfy the equation \(6e^2-11e+3=0\). If the foci of the hyperbola are \((3,5)\) and \((3,-4)\), then the length of its latus rectum is:
questions.sol:
\(e=\tfrac32\) (the root \(\tfrac13\) is rejected). \(2ae=9\Rightarrow a=3\), \(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=\tfrac{45}{4}\).
Latus rectum \(=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{15}{2}\).

questions.q: From the point \((-1,-1)\), two rays are sent making angles of \(45^\circ\) with the line \(x+y=0\). These rays get reflected from the mirror \(x+2y=1\). If the equations of the reflected rays are \(ax+by=9\) and \(cx+dy=7\), \(a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{Z}\), then the value of \(ad+bc\) is ______.
questions.sol:
The rays are \(y=-1\) and \(x=-1\); they meet the mirror at \((3,-1)\) and \((-1,1)\).
Reflecting the directions in the mirror (normal \((1,2)\)): \((1,0)\to\left(\tfrac35,-\tfrac45\right)\) and \((0,1)\to\left(-\tfrac45,-\tfrac35\right)\).
Reflected rays: \(4x+3y=9\) and \(-3x+4y=7\). So \(a=4,b=3,c=-3,d=4\) and \(ad+bc=16-9=7\).

questions.q: Let \(e_1\) and \(e_2\) be two distinct roots of the equation \(x^2-ax+2=0\). Let the sets \(\{a\in\mathbb{R}:e_1\text{ and }e_2\text{ are the eccentricities of hyperbolas}\}=(\alpha,\beta)\), and \(\{a\in\mathbb{R}:e_1\text{ and }e_2\text{ are the eccentricities of an ellipse and a hyperbola, respectively}\}=(\gamma,\infty)\). Then \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
With \(f(x)=x^2-ax+2\):
Both roots \(>1\): \(a^2>8\), \(f(1)=3-a>0\), \(\tfrac a2>1\Rightarrow a\in(2\sqrt2,3)\).
One root in \((0,1)\), other \(>1\): \(f(1)<0\) (and \(f(0)=2>0\)) \(\Rightarrow a>3\).
\(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=8+9+9=26\).

questions.q: If the eccentricity \(e\) of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), passing through \((6,4\sqrt3)\), satisfies \(15(e^2+1)=34e\), then the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{b^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{2(a^2+1)}=1\) is:
questions.sol:
\(15e^2-34e+15=0\Rightarrow e=\tfrac53\) (for a hyperbola), so \(b^2=\tfrac{16}{9}a^2\).
\(\dfrac{36}{a^2}-\dfrac{48\cdot9}{16a^2}=\dfrac9{a^2}=1\Rightarrow a^2=9\), \(b^2=16\).
The new hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{20}=1\) has latus rectum \(\dfrac{2\cdot20}{4}=10\).

questions.q: Let chord \(PQ\) of length \(3\sqrt{13}\) of the parabola \(y^2=12x\) be such that the ordinates of points \(P\) and \(Q\) are in the ratio \(1:2\). If the chord \(PQ\) subtends an angle \(\alpha\) at the focus of the parabola, then \(\sin\alpha\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(P(3t^2,6t)\), \(Q(12t^2,12t)\): \(PQ^2=81t^4+36t^2=117\Rightarrow t^2=1\). Take \(P(3,6)\), \(Q(12,12)\); focus \(S(3,0)\).
\(\overrightarrow{SP}=(0,6)\), \(\overrightarrow{SQ}=(9,12)\): \(\cos\alpha=\dfrac{72}{6\cdot15}=\dfrac45\), so \(\sin\alpha=\dfrac35\).

questions.q: Let the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+25=0\) be in the first quadrant and lie on the line \(2x-y=4\). Let the area of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle be \(27\sqrt3\). Then the square of the length of the chord of the circle on the line \(x=1\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{4}r^2=27\sqrt3\Rightarrow r^2=36\). Centre \((h,2h-4)\): \(h^2+(2h-4)^2-25=36\Rightarrow5h^2-16h-45=0\Rightarrow h=5\) (first quadrant), centre \((5,6)\).
Distance from \(x=1\) is \(4\); chord\(^2=4(36-16)=80\).

questions.q: Let \(C\) be a circle having centre in the first quadrant and touching the \(x\)-axis at a distance of \(3\) units from the origin. If the circle \(C\) has an intercept of length \(6\sqrt3\) on the \(y\)-axis, then the length of the chord of the circle \(C\) on the line \(x-y=3\) is:
questions.sol:
Centre \((3,r)\); \(2\sqrt{r^2-9}=6\sqrt3\Rightarrow r=6\).
Distance from \((3,6)\) to \(x-y=3\): \(\tfrac{6}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2\). Chord \(=2\sqrt{36-18}=6\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The eccentricity of an ellipse \(E\) with centre at the origin \(O\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\) and its directrices are \(x=\pm\dfrac{4\sqrt6}{3}\). Let \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be a hyperbola whose eccentricity is equal to the length of semi-major axis of \(E\), and whose length of latus rectum is equal to the length of minor axis of \(E\). Then the distance between the foci of \(H\) is:
questions.sol:
\(E\): \(\tfrac{A}{e}=\tfrac{4\sqrt6}{3}\Rightarrow A=2\sqrt2\), \(B^2=A^2(1-e^2)=2\), minor axis \(2\sqrt2\).
\(H\): \(e=2\sqrt2\Rightarrow b^2=7a^2\); \(\tfrac{2b^2}{a}=2\sqrt2\Rightarrow14a=2\sqrt2\Rightarrow a=\tfrac{\sqrt2}{7}\).
Distance between foci \(=2ae=2\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt2}{7}\cdot2\sqrt2=\tfrac87\).

questions.q: Let \(x=9\) be a directrix of an ellipse \(E\), whose centre is at the origin and eccentricity is \(\dfrac13\). Let \(P(\alpha,0)\), \(\alpha>0\), be a focus of \(E\) and \(AB\) be a chord passing through \(P\). Then the locus of the mid-point of \(AB\) is:
questions.sol:
\(\tfrac ae=9\Rightarrow a=3\), focus \((1,0)\), \(b^2=8\): \(\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{8}=1\).
Chord with mid-point \((h,k)\) (by \(T=S_1\)) passes through \((1,0)\): \(\dfrac h9=\dfrac{h^2}{9}+\dfrac{k^2}{8}\Rightarrow9k^2=8h(1-h)\).

questions.q: Let the line \(x-y=4\) intersect the circle \(C:(x-4)^2+(y+3)^2=9\) at the points \(Q\) and \(R\). If \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) is a point on \(C\) such that \(PQ=PR\), then \((6\alpha+8\beta)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(P\) lies on the perpendicular bisector of \(QR\), the line through the centre \((4,-3)\) perpendicular to \(x-y=4\): \(x+y=1\).
On \(C\): \(2(x-4)^2=9\Rightarrow x=4\pm\tfrac{3}{\sqrt2}\), \(y=-3\mp\tfrac3{\sqrt2}\).
\(6\alpha+8\beta=\mp\tfrac{6}{\sqrt2}\); square \(=18\).

questions.q: If a straight line drawn through the point of intersection of the lines \(4x+3y-1=0\) and \(3x+4y-1=0\) meets the co-ordinate axes at the points \(P\) and \(Q\), then the locus of the mid-point of \(PQ\) is:
questions.sol: The lines meet at \(\left(\tfrac17,\tfrac17\right)\). With intercepts \(2h,2k\): \(\dfrac{1}{14h}+\dfrac1{14k}=1\Rightarrow h+k=14hk\), i.e. \(x+y-14xy=0\).

questions.q: Let \(O\) be the vertex of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) and its chords \(OP\) and \(OQ\) are perpendicular to each other. If the locus of the mid-point of the line segment \(PQ\) is a conic \(C\), then the length of its latus rectum is:

Let \(\dfrac{x^2}{f(a^2+7a+3)}+\dfrac{y^2}{f(3a+15)}=1\) represent an ellipse with major axis along the \(y\)-axis, where \(f\) is a strictly decreasing positive function on \(\mathbb{R}\). If the set of all possible values of \(a\) is \(\mathbb{R}-[\alpha,\beta]\), then \(\alpha^2+\beta^2\) is equal to:

Consider the circle \(C:x^2+y^2-6x-8y-11=0\). Let a variable chord \(AB\) of the circle \(C\) subtend a right angle at the origin. If the locus of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin on the chord \(AB\) is the circle \(x^2+y^2-\alpha x-\beta y-\gamma=0\), then \(\alpha+\beta+2\gamma\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
If the foot is \((h,k)\), the chord is \(hx+ky=h^2+k^2\). Homogenising \(C\) with it, the right angle at \(O\) means the sum of the \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) coefficients is \(0\):
\(2-\dfrac{6h+8k}{h^2+k^2}-\dfrac{11}{h^2+k^2}=0\Rightarrow x^2+y^2-3x-4y-\tfrac{11}{2}=0\).
\(\alpha+\beta+2\gamma=3+4+11=18\).
